name: Algeria
nativeName: الجمهورية الجزائرية الديمقراطية الشعبية / Tagduda Tadzayrit Tamagdayt Taɣerfant
motto: بالشعب وللشعب (By the people and for the people)
highestPoint: Mount Tahat in the Hoggar Mountains (2,908 m)
longestRiver: Chelif River (700 km)
climate: Mediterranean along northern coastal belt; arid to hyper-arid desert across the Sahara covering over 80% of territory
naturalHazards: Earthquakes in northern mountainous zones
Severe mudslides and flash floods after winter rains
Sirocco sandstorms
environmentalIssues: Water scarcity and aquifer depletion in southern oases
biodiversity: Sahara-Mediterranean transition zone home to Barbary macaques, fennec foxes, cheetahs in Tassili n'Ajjer, and migratory birds
languages: French (widely used in commerce, administration, higher education)
legislature: Parliament (Council of the Nation and People's National Assembly)
latestElections: Presidential election September 2024 (Abdelmadjid Tebboune re-elected); legislative elections 2021
politicalSituation: Consolidated stability under President Tebboune with major public investment in green hydrogen, Sahara rail lines, and gas exports to Southern Europe.
foreignRelations: Prominent non-aligned power; key energy supplier to the European Union (Italy, Spain); supporter of Palestinian statehood and Sahrawi self-determination; member of AU, Arab League, OPEC, UN.
military: People's National Army (ANP) comprising Land Forces, Naval Forces, Air Force, and Air Defence.
adminDivisions: 58 provinces (wilayas)
history: Inhabited by indigenous Amazigh (Berber) peoples since antiquity; Numidian kingdoms flourished under Massinissa. Conquered by Carthage, Rome, and the Vandals before 7th-century Arab-Islamic expansion. Ruled by Rustamid, Fatimid, Zirid, and Ottoman Regencies. French colonized Algeria in 1830, leading to a brutal 132-year colonial era capped by the Algerian War of Independence (1954–1962) costing over a million Algerian lives. Post-independence socialist industrialization gave way to the tragic 'Black Decade' civil conflict in the 1990s, followed by national reconciliation and oil-driven modernization.
recentEvents2020_2026: Enacted post-Hirak constitutional revisions, hosted the 2022 Arab League Summit and 2023 African Nations Championship, expanded Trans-Mediterranean gas pipeline exports, and re-elected President Tebboune in 2024 while advancing the Gara Djebilet iron ore mega-rail link.
education: Universal free compulsory schooling to age 16; network of major polytechnic and research universities (USTHB Algiers, University of Constantine).
healthcare: Subsidized public healthcare network through national social insurance (CNAS) alongside expanding private clinics.
socialCustoms: Deep tradition of hospitality (karam), mint tea rituals, Friday family couscous gatherings, reverence for war martyrs (shuhada).
etiquette: Respectful greetings with right hand or double cheek kiss among same gender, modest attire outside coastal resort areas.
nationalIdentity: Forged through Amazigh roots, Islamic heritage, Arabic linguistic primacy, and heroic resistance during the anti-colonial liberation struggle.
energy: Natural gas (95%), expanding solar photovoltaic arrays through the Solar 1000MW program
tourism: Cultural and desert tourism centered on Tassili n'Ajjer, Roman ruins of Timgad and Djemila, and the white Mediterranean city of Algiers.
employment: Public administration, national oil company Sonatrach, construction, and emerging logistics.
debtInflation: Very low external public debt backed by substantial foreign exchange reserves; managed consumer inflation via grain subsidies.
transport: East-West Highway (Autoroute Est-Ouest spanning 1,216 km), expanding high-speed SNTF rail network into the Sahara, Algiers Metro.
cuisine: Couscous with lamb and seasonal vegetables, Mechoui spit-roasted lamb, Shakshouka, Tajine Zitoune, Makroudh, Baklava, Mint tea with pine nuts.
music: Raï (UNESCO heritage, Cheb Khaled, Cheb Mami), Chaabi (El Hadj M'Hamed El Anka), Andalusi classical music, Tuareg desert blues.
dance: Allaoui warrior dance, Kabyle folk dance, Tuareg sword dance.
art: Calligraphy, Mohamed Racim miniature paintings, Baya Mahieddine modernist folk art, Saharan rock art engravings.
architecture: Moorish and Ottoman palaces in the Casbah of Algiers, French colonial Haussmannian boulevards, M'zab Valley cubist earthen settlements.
literature: Kateb Yacine (Nedjma), Assia Djebar, Mouloud Feraoun, Yasmina Khadra, Tahar Djaout.
cinema: Lakhdar-Hamina's 'Chronicle of the Years of Fire' (Palme d'Or winner 1975), The Battle of Algiers (Gillo Pontecorvo co-production).
sports: Football (African Cup of Nations champions 1990, 2019; Desert Foxes), Middle-distance running (Noureddine Morceli, Hassiba Boulmerka, Taoufik Makhloufi), Boxing (Imane Khelif Olympic Gold 2024).
media: El Moudjahid, El Watan, Liberté, Echourouk, Télévision Algérienne (EPTV).
clothing: Karakou velvet embroidered jacket, Burnous wool cloak, Gandoura, traditional Berber silver fibula and headdress.
crafts: Ghardaïa handwoven carpets, Kabyle enamelled silver jewelry, Sahara leatherwork, ceramic pottery from Tizi Ouzou.
unescoIntangible: Raï music
Sbeiba ritual and ceremonies in Djanet
Couscous traditions (multinational)
Imzad music of Tuareg communities
flagDescription: Two equal vertical bands of green (fly side) and white (hoist side), with a red five-pointed star inside a red crescent centered along the dividing line.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features the crescent and star of Islam, the hand of Fatima, rising sun over the Atlas mountains, olive branches, and industrial/agricultural gears.
landmarks: Great Mosque of Algiers (Djamaa el Djazaïr)
travelNotes: Visa required for most foreign travelers; magnificent desert excursions require registered tour guides; vibrant, welcoming Mediterranean coastline.
shortSummary: Algeria is Africa's largest country by land area, uniting stunning Mediterranean coastlines, ancient Roman ruins, the monumental Grand Mosque of Algiers, and the majestic expanses of the Sahara desert.
geography: Highest point: Mount Tahat in the Hoggar Mountains (2,908 m). Lowest point: Chott Melrhir (-40 m). Longest river: Chelif River (700 km). Climate: Mediterranean along northern coastal belt; arid to hyper-arid desert across the Sahara covering over 80% of territory. Biodiversity: Sahara-Mediterranean transition zone home to Barbary macaques, fennec foxes, cheetahs in Tassili n'Ajjer, and migratory birds.
economy: Sectors: Hydrocarbons & Industry 40%, Services 46%, Agriculture 14%. Key industries: Petroleum and natural gas refining, Petrochemicals, Iron and steel manufacturing (El Hadjar), Phosphates and fertilizers, Automotive assembly, Cement. Natural resources: Natural gas, Crude petroleum, Iron ore (Gara Djebilet), Phosphates, Uranium, Zinc, Lead. Major exports: Liquefied natural gas (LNG), Crude petroleum, Refined petroleum products, Fertilizers and ammonia, Dates.
culture: Cuisine: Couscous with lamb and seasonal vegetables, Mechoui spit-roasted lamb, Shakshouka, Tajine Zitoune, Makroudh, Baklava, Mint tea with pine nuts.. Music & Dance: Raï (UNESCO heritage, Cheb Khaled, Cheb Mami), Chaabi (El Hadj M'Hamed El Anka), Andalusi classical music, Tuareg desert blues.. Sports: Football (African Cup of Nations champions 1990, 2019; Desert Foxes), Middle-distance running (Noureddine Morceli, Hassiba Boulmerka, Taoufik Makhloufi), Boxing (Imane Khelif Olympic Gold 2024).. Festivals: Festival du Raï (Oran), Timgad International Music Festival, Sbeiba Festival of Djanet, National Date Festival (Biskra).

name: Angola
motto: Virtus Unita Fortior (Virtue is stronger when united)
highestPoint: Morro do Môco (2,620 m)
longestRiver: Kwanza River (960 km)
climate: Semi-arid in southern coast; tropical wet-and-dry across central plateau; humid equatorial in Cabinda exclave
naturalHazards: Localized heavy rainfall and urban flash flooding
Periodic prolonged droughts in southern provinces (Cunene, Namibe)
environmentalIssues: Past clearance of unexploded landmines from civil war era
biodiversity: Quiçama National Park, Iona National Park home to desert-adapted lions, giant sable antelope (Palanca Negra Gigante), and Welwitschia mirabilis
mainPoliticalParties: People's Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA)
National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA)
latestElections: General election 2022 (President João Lourenço re-elected); next scheduled 2027
politicalSituation: Diversification drive away from petroleum dependence under President João Lourenço; privatization of state assets and anti-corruption campaigns.
foreignRelations: Key leader in Southern African Development Community (SADC) and African Union; major economic partnerships with China, the United States, Portugal, and the EU.
military: Angolan Armed Forces (FAA) comprising Army, Navy, and National Air Force.
internationalOrgs: OPEC (withdrew Jan 2024 to set independent output quotas)
adminDivisions: 18 provinces (restructuring into 21 provinces enacted 2024/2025)
history: Kingdom of Kongo and Ndongo kingdoms thrived before Portuguese arrival in 1482 led by Diogo Cão. Queen Nzinga Mbande fiercely resisted Portuguese colonization in the 17th century. Gained independence in 1975 following the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon. Plunged into a devastating 27-year Cold War proxy civil conflict (MPLA vs. UNITA) that ended in 2002 after Jonas Savimbi's death. Modern era marked by rapid petroleum-fueled reconstruction, urban expansion in Luanda, and economic diversification.
recentEvents2020_2026: Left OPEC in 2024 to ramp up national crude and refining capacity, modernized the Benguela Railway connecting DRC and Zambian copper belts to Lobito Port (Lobito Atlantic Railway backed by G7/US/EU), and expanded agro-industrial corridors.
education: Agostinho Neto University; public educational reforms aimed at expanding rural primary access and Portuguese-language proficiency.
healthcare: National Health Service (SNS) undergoing rehabilitation with new provincial hospitals built in Luanda and Cabinda.
socialCustoms: Extended family community networks (Óbito mourning traditions), Sunday street gatherings, vibrant street markets.
etiquette: Firm handshakes, greeting the eldest first, respectful tone in administrative discussions.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated through the endurance of Queen Nzinga, resilience through decades of war, Semba rhythm, and the emblematic giant sable antelope.
energy: Hydroelectric power (Laúca, Caculo Cabaça dams) providing over 65% of electricity, balance from thermal and natural gas
tourism: Emerging eco-tourism focused on Kalandula Falls, Leba Pass, Kissama National Park, and pristine Atlantic surfing beaches at Cabo Ledo.
employment: High proportion in informal commerce, agriculture, oil sector contracting, and retail.
debtInflation: Managing bilateral debt restructuring (notably with Chinese creditors) alongside monetary stabilization policies by Banco Nacional de Angola.
transport: Lobito Atlantic Railway Corridor, expanded Luanda Antonio Agostinho Neto International Airport, trans-national highway links.
airports: Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport (Luanda New Airport)
ports: Port of Lobito (vital mining transit hub)
cuisine: Muamba de Galinha (chicken stew with palm oil and okra), Calulu de Peixe, Funge (cassava or corn flour paste), Mufete (grilled fish with sweet potato and beans), Kizaca.
music: Semba (ancestor of Brazilian samba), Kizomba, Kuduro (upbeat electronic urban dance), Rebita.
dance: Kizomba (globally popular partner dance), Kuduro, Semba, Tarraxinha.
art: Chokwe Cwe Mwana Pwo carved wooden masks, contemporary painting at Luanda Triennale.
architecture: Portuguese colonial architecture in Cidade Alta of Luanda; modernist 1960s cinemas in Lobito; contemporary gleaming waterfront high-rises on Luanda Bay.
literature: Agostinho Neto (Sagrada Esperança), Pepetela (Mayombe, Camões Prize winner), Ondjaki (Os Transparentes), José Eduardo Agualusa.
cinema: Pochedas film productions, DocLuanda international documentary festival.
sports: Basketball (Angolan national team 11-time AfroBasket champions), Football (Palancas Negras, 2006 World Cup, 2024 AFCON quarter-finalists), Handball (women's team continental powerhouse).
media: Jornal de Angola, TPA (Televisão Pública de Angola), TV Zimbo, Rádio Nacional de Angola.
clothing: Samakaka traditional geometric printed fabric; modern cosmopolitan fashion in Luanda.
crafts: Pensador (The Thinker) carved statuettes, Chokwe basketry, beadwork.
worldHeritageSites: Mbanza Kongo, Vestiges of the Capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo
unescoIntangible: Sona, sand drawings of the Chokwe people (inscribed 2023)
famousPeople: Eduardo Camavinga (born in Cabinda refugee camp)
flagDescription: Two horizontal bands of red (blood shed during colonial oppression and liberation struggle) and black (the African continent), with a central yellow emblem of a half gear wheel, a machete, and a five-pointed star.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a crossed machete and hoe against a rising sun, encircled by a half cog wheel, coffee sprig, and cotton, surmounted by a yellow star over an open book.
landmarks: Kalandula Falls (one of Africa's largest waterfalls)
travelNotes: E-visa system implemented for international tourism; malaria prophylaxis strongly advised; stunning natural scenery and vibrant urban nightlife.
shortSummary: Angola is a dynamic southwest African nation endowed with immense mineral and petroleum wealth, breathtaking landscapes from Kalandula Falls to the Namib Desert, and an irresistible global cultural imprint through Kizomba and Semba music.
geography: Highest point: Morro do Môco (2,620 m). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Kwanza River (960 km). Climate: Semi-arid in southern coast; tropical wet-and-dry across central plateau; humid equatorial in Cabinda exclave. Biodiversity: Quiçama National Park, Iona National Park home to desert-adapted lions, giant sable antelope (Palanca Negra Gigante), and Welwitschia mirabilis.
economy: Sectors: Oil & Mining 45%, Services 35%, Agriculture 12%, Manufacturing 8%. Key industries: Petroleum extraction and refining, Diamond mining (Catoca mine), Cement and construction materials, Beverages and brewing, Logistics and port operations. Natural resources: Crude petroleum, Diamonds, Natural gas, Iron ore, Copper, Hydropower potential. Major exports: Crude petroleum, Rough diamonds, Liquefied natural gas, Refined petroleum, Coffee.
culture: Cuisine: Muamba de Galinha (chicken stew with palm oil and okra), Calulu de Peixe, Funge (cassava or corn flour paste), Mufete (grilled fish with sweet potato and beans), Kizaca.. Music & Dance: Semba (ancestor of Brazilian samba), Kizomba, Kuduro (upbeat electronic urban dance), Rebita.. Sports: Basketball (Angolan national team 11-time AfroBasket champions), Football (Palancas Negras, 2006 World Cup, 2024 AFCON quarter-finalists), Handball (women's team continental powerhouse).. Festivals: Luanda Carnival (Carnaval de Luanda), Festas do Mar (Namibe), Sumbe Music Festival (FestiSumbe).

name: Benin
nationalAnthem: L'Aube Nouvelle (The Dawn of a New Day)
highestPoint: Mont Sokbaro (658 m)
lowestPoint: Bight of Benin / Atlantic Ocean (0 m)
longestRiver: Ouémé River (510 km)
climate: Tropical hot and humid in south with two rainy seasons; semi-arid Sahelian savanna in north with dry Harmattan winds
naturalHazards: Harmattan dust storms in winter
Coastal erosion along the Gulf of Guinea
Periodic northern droughts
environmentalIssues: Water contamination in stilt village ecosystems
biodiversity: Pendjari National Park (part of W-Arly-Pendjari complex) harboring West Africa's last viable populations of lions, elephants, and cheetahs
latestElections: Legislative elections 2023; Presidential elections scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Extensive port modernization at Cotonou and economic digitization under President Patrice Talon; regional counter-extremism operations in northern border parks.
foreignRelations: Member of ECOWAS, West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA), African Union, Francophonie; close security cooperation with regional neighbors.
military: Benin Armed Forces (FAB) comprising Army, Navy, Air Force, and National Gendarmerie.
adminDivisions: 12 departments
history: Heartland of the formidable Kingdom of Dahomey (founded c. 1600), renowned for royal palaces at Abomey, the Dahomey Amazons (all-female military regiment), and sophisticated bronze arts. Ouidah was a tragic epicenter of the transatlantic slave trade. Colonized by France in 1894 as French Dahomey. Attained independence in 1960. Underwent military coups until Mathieu Kérékou established a Marxist-Leninist state in 1972, renaming it Benin in 1975. Pioneered sub-Saharan Africa's peaceful democratic transition in 1990 through the historic National Conference.
recentEvents2020_2026: Celebrated the historic restitution of 26 royal Dahomey treasures from France exhibited at the Presidency; inaugurated the 30-meter bronze Amazon statue in Cotonou; completed the Cotonou Port expansion and modernized the GDIZ industrial free zone.
historicalFigures: Toussaint Louverture (father was Allada prince from Dahomey)
religions: Christianity (Catholic and Celestial Church of Christ) ~48.5%
education: University of Abomey-Calavi (one of West Africa's largest universities); expanding vocational and technical training schools.
healthcare: Regional hospital centers and community dispensaries; ARCH universal healthcare pilot program.
socialCustoms: Veneration of ancestral spirits (Vodun festival celebrated annually on January 10 as national holiday), vibrant drumming circles, colorful wax fabric tailoring.
etiquette: Right-hand use for eating and giving items, polite inquiries about family welfare before starting business.
nationalIdentity: Defined by Dahomey royal heritage, Vodun spiritual philosophy, intellectual leadership ('the Latin Quarter of Africa'), and communal solidarity.
industries: Food processing and palm oil refining
Port logistics and transit trade to Niger/Nigeria
energy: Electricity imports from Nigeria/Ghana via WAPP supplemented by domestic solar plants (Illoulofin Solar Plant) and Maria Gléta gas turbine power plant
tourism: Cultural tourism to Ganvié (stilt village 'Venice of Africa'), the Ouidah Door of No Return slave memorial, Royal Palaces of Abomey, and Pendjari wildlife safaris.
employment: Informal trade, agricultural smallholders, logistics and transport operations centered on Cotonou.
debtInflation: Prudent macroeconomic management within WAEMU monetary framework maintaining single-digit inflation and strong euro-pegged currency.
transport: Autonomous Port of Cotonou, modernized coastal highway linking Lagos to Lomé, Glo-Djigbé industrial airport corridor.
ports: Port of Cotonou (major transit gateway for landlocked Sahel)
cuisine: Amiwo (red corn flour paste with chicken or fish), Pâte rouge, Kuli-kuli (fried peanut snacks), Aloko (fried plantains), Akassa with Gboma soup, Wagasi (fried Peul cheese).
festivals: National Vodun Festival (Fête du Vodoun, January 10 in Ouidah)
music: Highlife, Tchinkounmè, Traditional Vodun drumming, Afrobeat, Angélique Kidjo (5-time Grammy winner).
dance: Agbadja, Kpétè, Zinli, Guèlèdè masquerade dance.
art: Dahomey royal applique tapestries, cast brass figures, contemporary African painting at Fondation Zinsou in Cotonou.
architecture: Royal Palaces of Abomey earthen bas-relief structures; Afro-Brazilian style colonial two-story houses in Porto-Novo and Ouidah; Tata Somba fortress-like clay compounds.
literature: Olympe Bhêly-Quénum (Un piège sans fin), Paul Hazoumé (Doguicimi), Florent Couao-Zotti.
cinema: Sylvestre Amoussou, Idrissou Mora-Kpai; emerging documentary and fiction film industry.
sports: Football (The Cheetahs, formerly The Squirrels, 2019 AFCON quarter-finalists), Boxing, Traditional wrestling.
media: La Nation, Le Matinal, ORTB (Office de Radiodiffusion et Télévision du Bénin), Canal 3 Bénin.
clothing: Bazin boubou, colorful Kente-like Akwete and wax prints, traditional Dahomey royal tunic.
crafts: Carved wooden Gelede masks, bronze casting, woven reed mats from Lake Nokoué.
worldHeritageSites: W-Arly-Pendjari Complex (shared with Niger and Burkina Faso)
Koutammakou, the Land of the Batammariba (extension into Benin)
unescoIntangible: Oral heritage of Gelede (with Nigeria and Togo)
Vodun spiritual and cultural practices
flagDescription: Two equal horizontal bands of yellow (top) and red (bottom) with a vertical green band on the hoist side (Pan-African colors representing hope, courage, and wealth).
coatOfArmsDescription: Quartered shield with a Somba castle, the Star of Benin, a palm tree, and a sailing ship, supported by two leopards and topped by two cornucopias with the national motto.
landmarks: Door of No Return in Ouidah
travelNotes: Safe destination for international cultural travelers; Cotonou offers excellent dining and arts; respect local Vodun shrines and photography prohibitions.
shortSummary: Benin is the historic cradle of the Dahomey Kingdom and Vodun spirituality, famed for the extraordinary stilt village of Ganvié, vibrant musical pioneers like Angélique Kidjo, and richly preserved UNESCO royal heritage.
geography: Highest point: Mont Sokbaro (658 m). Lowest point: Bight of Benin / Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Ouémé River (510 km). Climate: Tropical hot and humid in south with two rainy seasons; semi-arid Sahelian savanna in north with dry Harmattan winds. Biodiversity: Pendjari National Park (part of W-Arly-Pendjari complex) harboring West Africa's last viable populations of lions, elephants, and cheetahs.
economy: Sectors: Services 48%, Agriculture 38%, Industry 14%. Key industries: Cotton ginning and textiles, Food processing and palm oil refining, Cement manufacturing, Port logistics and transit trade to Niger/Nigeria. Natural resources: Arable land, Limestone and marble, Offshore petroleum reserves, Timber. Major exports: Raw cotton, Cashew nuts, Shea butter, Gold, Refined petroleum re-exports.
culture: Cuisine: Amiwo (red corn flour paste with chicken or fish), Pâte rouge, Kuli-kuli (fried peanut snacks), Aloko (fried plantains), Akassa with Gboma soup, Wagasi (fried Peul cheese).. Music & Dance: Highlife, Tchinkounmè, Traditional Vodun drumming, Afrobeat, Angélique Kidjo (5-time Grammy winner).. Sports: Football (The Cheetahs, formerly The Squirrels, 2019 AFCON quarter-finalists), Boxing, Traditional wrestling.. Festivals: National Vodun Festival (Fête du Vodoun, January 10 in Ouidah), Quintessence Film Festival, Gani Festival in Nikki.

name: Botswana
nationalAnthem: Fatshe leno la rona (Blessed Be This Noble Land)
highestPoint: Otse Hill (1,491 m)
lowestPoint: Confluence of Limpopo and Shashe Rivers (513 m)
longestRiver: Okavango River / Limpopo River (border)
climate: Semi-arid continental; warm winters and scorching summers; unpredictable summer rainfall across the Kalahari
naturalHazards: Recurrent periodic droughts
Dry desert winds carrying dust
Bushfires in dry seasons
environmentalIssues: Human-wildlife conflict along unfenced conservation corridors
biodiversity: Home to the world's largest concentration of African elephants in Chobe National Park and extraordinary wetland biodiversity in the Okavango Delta
government: Unitary parliamentary republic under an executive presidency
legislature: Parliament (National Assembly and advisory Ntlo ya Dikgosi)
latestElections: Historic general election October 2024 (UDC victory, ending 58 years of BDP governance; peaceful transfer of power to Duma Boko); next scheduled 2029
politicalSituation: Model of enduring African democracy; smooth 2024 political transition focused on economic diversification, youth employment, and citizen economic empowerment.
foreignRelations: Founding member and headquarters host of SADC in Gaborone; stalwart supporter of the International Criminal Court and rules-based international order; strong partnerships with US, EU, and diamond market hubs.
military: Botswana Defence Force (BDF) renowned for professional anti-poaching operations and UN peacekeeping.
adminDivisions: 10 rural districts and 6 urban councils
history: Inhabited by San hunter-gatherers for tens of thousands of years (evidenced by Tsodilo rock art). Bantu-speaking Batswana settled the region by the 17th century, organizing into powerful kingdoms under Dikgosi (chiefs). In 1885, Three Dikgosi (Khama III, Sebele I, Bathoen I) traveled to London to request British protection against Boer expansion, leading to the Bechuanaland Protectorate. Gained independence in 1966 under Sir Seretse Khama as one of the world's poorest nations. Discovery of vast kimberlite diamond pipes at Orapa transformed Botswana into an upper-middle-income miracle with impeccable governance.
recentEvents2020_2026: Concluded landmark new 10-year diamond sales and mining joint venture agreement between Debswana and De Beers in 2023; orchestrated a historic democratic transfer of power in October 2024 as Duma Boko was inaugurated President; opened the Kazungula Bridge corridor.
education: University of Botswana; Botswana International University of Science and Technology (BIUST); free public primary and secondary education.
healthcare: Universal free healthcare clinic network; world-renowned HIV prevention and universal antiretroviral therapy rollout (Treat All program).
socialCustoms: Kgotla (traditional community consensus assembly), Bogadi (bride wealth), Pula greeting invoking blessings and precious rain.
etiquette: Greeting with 'Dumela' using both hands or cupping the right elbow, respect for elders and chiefs (Dikgosi).
nationalIdentity: Grounded in peaceful consensus (Therisanyo), Setswana language, cattle-keeping heritage, and pride in pristine wildlife conservation.
energy: Coal-fired power (Morupule Power Station) complemented by major ongoing utility-scale solar projects in the Kalahari
tourism: High-value, low-impact eco-tourism model centered on luxury safari lodges in the Okavango Delta, Chobe river cruises, and Makgadikgadi quad biking.
employment: Civil service, diamond beneficiation, tourism hospitality, commercial agriculture.
debtInflation: Very low sovereign debt, high sovereign credit rating, strong Pula currency basket linked to the South African Rand and IMF SDR.
transport: A1 Trans-Kalahari Highway, Kazungula Bridge over the Zambezi River linking to Zambia, Botswana Railways network.
airports: Sir Seretse Khama International Airport (GBE in Gaborone)
ports: Landlocked; primary oceanic freight access through Port of Durban (South Africa) and Port of Walvis Bay (Namibia)
cuisine: Seswaa (slow-cooked pounded beef or goat), Pap (maize porridge), Morogo (wild spinach), Vetkoek (Magwinya), Dikgobe (beans and corn), Mopane worms.
festivals: Son of the Soil Cultural Festival
music: Traditional Tswana folk music with clapping and leg rattles (Phathisi), Borankana, contemporary Afro-pop and jazz.
dance: Setapa, Borankana stamp dancing, Tsutsube (San trance dance).
art: Tsodilo Hills San rock art, contemporary basket weaving from Ngamiland, ostrich eggshell jewelry.
architecture: Traditional circular thatched rondavels with cow dung polished floors; modern architectural landmarks in Gaborone Central Business District.
literature: Bessie Head (Maru, When Rain Clouds Gather), Alexander McCall Smith ('The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency' set in Gaborone).
cinema: Filming location for iconic wildlife documentaries (National Geographic, BBC Planet Earth); budding local film industry.
sports: Athletics (Letsile Tebogo 200m Olympic Gold Medalist Paris 2024, Botswana 4x400m Olympic Silver), Football (Zebras), Netball.
media: Btv (Botswana Television), Radio Botswana, Mmegi, The Botswana Gazette, Sunday Standard.
clothing: Traditional German print fabric (Leteisi) worn at weddings; kaross animal skin cloaks; modern business attire.
crafts: Intricately coiled palm fiber baskets (Shorobe), hand-carved wooden animals, leather sand sandals.
worldHeritageSites: Okavango Delta (1000th UNESCO World Heritage site)
unescoIntangible: Diketo traditional board game
Earthenware pottery-making skills in Kgatleng District
flagDescription: Light blue field with a horizontal black stripe across the center, flanked above and below by thin white stripes (symbolizing rain/water and racial harmony).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features three cogwheels, a bull's head, and three waves of water, supported by two zebras (one holding an elephant tusk, one holding a sorghum stalk) over the motto 'PULA'.
travelNotes: One of Africa's safest, most peaceful travel destinations; self-drive 4x4 routes require preparation; exceptional safari experiences.
shortSummary: Botswana is a beacon of African democratic stability and prosperity, world-renowned for the crystal-clear waters of the Okavango Delta, the elephant-rich Chobe National Park, and Olympic sprinting glory.
geography: Highest point: Otse Hill (1,491 m). Lowest point: Confluence of Limpopo and Shashe Rivers (513 m). Longest river: Okavango River / Limpopo River (border). Climate: Semi-arid continental; warm winters and scorching summers; unpredictable summer rainfall across the Kalahari. Biodiversity: Home to the world's largest concentration of African elephants in Chobe National Park and extraordinary wetland biodiversity in the Okavango Delta.
economy: Sectors: Services 60%, Mining 22%, Manufacturing 6%, Agriculture 2%. Key industries: Diamond mining and cutting/polishing, Copper and nickel mining, Soda ash and salt extraction, Eco-tourism and safari hospitality, Beef processing. Natural resources: Gem-quality diamonds (Jwaneng, Orapa), Copper, Coal, Soda ash, Potash, Uranium, Wildlife. Major exports: Rough and polished diamonds, Bovine beef cuts (to EU/UK), Copper-nickel matte, Soda ash, Machinery.
culture: Cuisine: Seswaa (slow-cooked pounded beef or goat), Pap (maize porridge), Morogo (wild spinach), Vetkoek (Magwinya), Dikgobe (beans and corn), Mopane worms.. Music & Dance: Traditional Tswana folk music with clapping and leg rattles (Phathisi), Borankana, contemporary Afro-pop and jazz.. Sports: Athletics (Letsile Tebogo 200m Olympic Gold Medalist Paris 2024, Botswana 4x400m Olympic Silver), Football (Zebras), Netball.. Festivals: Maitisong Festival (Gaborone), Ditiro tsa Mmino wa Setswana, President's Day Celebrations, Son of the Soil Cultural Festival.

name: Burkina Faso
nationalDay: December 11 (Proclamation of the Republic), August 4 (Revolution Day)
nationalAnthem: Une Seule Nuit (The Anthem of Victory / One Single Night)
motto: La Patrie ou la Mort, nous vaincrons (Fatherland or Death, we shall conquer)
highestPoint: Mount Tenakourou (749 m)
longestRiver: Mouhoun (Black Volta) River (1,352 km total course)
climate: Sahelian in the north transitioning to tropical savanna in the south with a single rainy season from June to September
naturalHazards: Recurrent Sahelian droughts
Harmattan wind storms
Localized flooding during monsoon downpours
biodiversity: Arly National Park (WAP complex), Nazinga Game Ranch with elephant populations, and Sindou Peaks geological formations
headOfState: President of the Transition Captain Ibrahim Traoré
latestElections: Presidential/legislative elections last held 2020; transitional roadmap extended through 2029 under sovereign security focus
politicalSituation: Transition government led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré focused on national sovereignty, reclaiming territory from insurgent groups, and establishing the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) with Mali and Niger.
foreignRelations: Member of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES); withdrew from ECOWAS in 2024 alongside Mali and Niger; deepened bilateral security and economic ties with Russia, China, Turkey, and regional neighbors.
military: Burkinabé Armed Forces (FAB) augmented by the Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland (VDP).
adminDivisions: 13 regions and 45 provinces
history: Inhabited since antiquity; heartland of the Mossi Kingdoms (including Ouagadougou, Tenkodogo, Yatenga) established in the 11th-15th centuries, famous for their Mogho Naba emperors and cavalry. French protectorate imposed in 1896 as French Upper Volta. Attained independence in 1960. In 1983, charismatic revolutionary leader Thomas Sankara took power, launching sweeping anti-imperialist, feminist, and public health reforms and renaming the nation Burkina Faso ('Land of Incorruptible People') before his assassination in 1987. Blaise Compaoré ruled until ousted by a popular uprising in 2014. Following growing regional security challenges, Captain Ibrahim Traoré assumed leadership in September 2022.
recentEvents2020_2026: Founded the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) with Mali and Niger in 2024; mobilized mass domestic security initiatives (VDP); launched state-owned tomato processing and gold refining plants; hosted FESPACO pan-African cinema festival.
historicalFigures: Yennenga (legendary Mossi princess mother of the Mossi nation)
education: Joseph Ki-Zerbo University in Ouagadougou; Nazi Boni University in Bobo-Dioulasso; national programs promoting literacy in national languages.
healthcare: Free healthcare policy for pregnant women and children under five; expanding community health workers across rural communes.
socialCustoms: Deep tradition of collective labor (Naam groups), welcoming guests with cool water, respected role of traditional chieftains (Mogho Naba).
etiquette: Inquiring about family health at length, presenting gifts with the right hand, honoring community elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the spirit of the Mossi cavalry, Thomas Sankara's self-reliance ethos ('consume what we produce'), and the proud Burkinabé identity of incorruptibility.
industries: Industrial and artisanal gold mining (Essakane, Mana)
energy: Expansion of utility-scale solar photovoltaic power (Zagtouli Solar Plant, Kodéni) reducing reliance on imported electricity from Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana
tourism: Cultural and film tourism centered on FESPACO in Ouagadougou, SIAO crafts exhibition, Sindou Peaks, and the Granaries of Tiébélé.
employment: Over 75% in subsistence agriculture and pastoralism, artisanal mining, and informal urban micro-enterprises.
debtInflation: Fiscal discipline supported by gold export windfalls and localized agricultural production drives.
transport: Abidjan-Ouagadougou railway corridor (Sitarail), trans-Sahelian asphalt highway network.
airports: Thomas Sankara International Airport (OUA in Ouagadougou)
ports: Landlocked; vital maritime transit links through Port of Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire), Port of Lomé (Togo), and Port of Tema (Ghana)
cuisine: Riz Gras (savory seasoned rice), Tô (sorghum or corn porridge with okra or baobab leaf sauce), Poulet Bicyclette (grilled free-range chicken), Babenda (fermented leaf stew), Dolo (fermented sorghum beer).
festivals: FESPACO (Panafrican Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou)
music: Balafon xylophone, Djembe, Kora, traditional Mossi Bendré drum, contemporary artists like Smarty and Alif Naaba.
dance: Warba acrobatic hip-shaking dance of the Mossi, Liwaga, Dodo dance.
art: Lost-wax bronze foundry sculptures of Ouagadougou, hand-painted geometric mural painting of the Kassena women of Tiébélé.
architecture: Sudano-Sahelian Grand Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso built of mud and timber beams; intricately painted earthen compounds of Tiébélé.
literature: Norbert Zongo (Le Parachutage), Monique Ilboudo, Joseph Ki-Zerbo (eminent African historian: 'A quand l'Afrique?').
cinema: The film capital of Africa (FESPACO headquarters); legendary directors Idrissa Ouédraogo (Tilaï, Yaaba) and Gaston Kaboré (Wend Kuuni).
sports: Football (Les Étalons / The Stallions, 2013 AFCON runners-up, 2022 semi-finalists), Cycling (Tour du Faso), Traditional wrestling, Athletics (Hugues Fabrice Zango, Triple Jump World Champion & Olympic medalist).
media: Sidwaya, L'Observateur Paalga, Le Pays, RTB (Radiodiffusion Télévision du Burkina).
clothing: Faso Dan Fani (handwoven local cotton fabric championed by Thomas Sankara as a national emblem of pride); Koko Dunda hand-dyed indigo fabric.
crafts: Bronze casting, handwoven Faso Dan Fani textiles, carved wooden masks (Bobo, Bwa, Mossi butterfly masks), leatherwork.
worldHeritageSites: Ancient Ferrous Metallurgy Sites of Burkina Faso
unescoIntangible: Cultural practices and expressions linked to the Balafon (with Mali and Côte d'Ivoire)
flagDescription: Two equal horizontal bands of red (top, revolutionary struggle) and green (bottom, agricultural richness and hope), with a yellow five-pointed star in the center.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a shield with the national flag design, supported by two rearing white stallions (étalons), flanked by crossed spears and an open book over the national motto.
travelNotes: Travel requires up-to-date security assessments; Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso remain vibrant epicenters of African cinema, craft arts, and warm hospitality.
shortSummary: Burkina Faso, the proud 'Land of Incorruptible People', is Africa's cultural heart for cinema and crafts, celebrated for the historic FESPACO film festival, handwoven Faso Dan Fani textiles, and the painted earthen architecture of Tiébélé.
geography: Highest point: Mount Tenakourou (749 m). Lowest point: Mouhoun (Black Volta) River (200 m). Longest river: Mouhoun (Black Volta) River (1,352 km total course). Climate: Sahelian in the north transitioning to tropical savanna in the south with a single rainy season from June to September. Biodiversity: Arly National Park (WAP complex), Nazinga Game Ranch with elephant populations, and Sindou Peaks geological formations.
economy: Sectors: Agriculture & Livestock 31%, Industry & Mining 28%, Services 41%. Key industries: Industrial and artisanal gold mining (Essakane, Mana), Cotton ginning and textiles, Food processing and brewing (Brakina), Soap and vegetable oils. Natural resources: Gold (leading export revenue), Zinc, Manganese, Phosphate, Arable land. Major exports: Gold bullion, Raw cotton, Sesame seeds, Shea butter and nuts, Live livestock, Zinc ores.
culture: Cuisine: Riz Gras (savory seasoned rice), Tô (sorghum or corn porridge with okra or baobab leaf sauce), Poulet Bicyclette (grilled free-range chicken), Babenda (fermented leaf stew), Dolo (fermented sorghum beer).. Music & Dance: Balafon xylophone, Djembe, Kora, traditional Mossi Bendré drum, contemporary artists like Smarty and Alif Naaba.. Sports: Football (Les Étalons / The Stallions, 2013 AFCON runners-up, 2022 semi-finalists), Cycling (Tour du Faso), Traditional wrestling, Athletics (Hugues Fabrice Zango, Triple Jump World Champion & Olympic medalist).. Festivals: FESPACO (Panafrican Film and Television Festival of Ouagadougou), SIAO (International Art and Craft Fair), Jazz à Ouaga.
sources: National Statistical Office of Burkina Faso

name: Burundi
highestPoint: Mount Heha (2,684 m)
longestRiver: Ruvubu River (part of uppermost Nile Basin) / Rusizi River
climate: Equatorial highland with two wet seasons (February–May, September–November); pleasantly cool in mountains, hot along Lake Tanganyika
naturalHazards: Soil erosion and devastating landslides during torrential seasonal rains
Droughts in northeastern valleys
environmentalIssues: Soil exhaustion due to extreme population density
biodiversity: Kibira National Park (montane rainforest harboring chimpanzees and colobus monkeys) and Ruvubu National Park
mainPoliticalParties: National Council for the Defense of Democracy – Forces for the Defense of Democracy (CNDD-FDD)
latestElections: General elections 2020 (Évariste Ndayishimiye elected); legislative and municipal elections 2025; next presidential 2027
politicalSituation: Consolidation of diplomatic re-engagement with the EU, US, and East African Community under President Ndayishimiye; investment in youth entrepreneurship and agricultural cooperatives.
foreignRelations: Member of East African Community (EAC), African Union, International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR), UN; prominent troop contributor to African Union peacekeeping missions (ATMIS in Somalia).
military: National Defence Force of Burundi (FDNB).
adminDivisions: 18 provinces (legislated restructuring into 5 new provinces enacted 2024/2025: Bujumbura, Burunga, Butanyerera, Gitega, Buhumuza)
history: Ancient Kingdom of Burundi emerged in the 16th century under Mwami (King) Cambarantama, characterized by sacred royal drum ceremonies (Karyenda). Incorporated into German East Africa in 1899, then Belgian Ruanda-Urundi mandate following WWI. Gained independence in 1962 as a constitutional monarchy before becoming a republic in 1966. Decades of tragic post-colonial ethnic violence and civil war culminated in the landmark Arusha Peace and Reconciliation Agreement of 2000, creating an ethnic power-sharing constitutional structure.
recentEvents2020_2026: Normalised ties with European and international donors; designated Gitega as political capital; advanced the standard gauge railway (SGR) link to Tanzania's port of Dar es Salaam; promoted agricultural value-chains in specialty high-altitude specialty Arabica coffees.
education: University of Burundi in Bujumbura; free primary education introduced in 2005.
healthcare: Community health centers, faith-based hospitals; free maternal and under-five healthcare policy.
socialCustoms: Ukuri (truthfulness), deep communal solidarity, traditional beer sharing with hollow reeds (Inzoga y'umugurano), sacred role of royal drumming.
etiquette: Greetings with handshakes held with both hands to show sincerity, soft-spoken speech, deference to elders.
nationalIdentity: Bound by universal Kirundi language, shared cultural drum traditions (Ingoma), coffee-growing heritage on thousand emerald hills.
industries: Coffee and tea washing and processing
naturalResources: Nickel (one of world's largest undeveloped reserves)
energy: Expansion of hydropower (Jiji and Mulembwe hydro projects, Ruzizi III) and off-grid mini-hydro networks
tourism: Eco-tourism along Lake Tanganyika beaches (Saga Beach), Kibira rainforest chimpanzee tracking, Chutes de la Karera waterfalls, and royal drum performances at Gishora.
employment: Over 85% in rural subsistence farming and cooperative coffee cultivation.
debtInflation: Monetary stabilization supported by IMF Extended Credit Facility and regional EAC trade facilitation.
transport: Key water freight routes on Lake Tanganyika linking Port of Bujumbura to Kigoma (Tanzania) and Kalemie (DRC); road links to Kigali and Dar es Salaam.
airports: Melchior Ndadaye International Airport (BJM in Bujumbura)
ports: Port of Bujumbura (lake port on Lake Tanganyika)
cuisine: Mukeke (delicious endemic Lake Tanganyika fish, grilled or fried), Ndagala (tiny crispy dried fish), Ibiharage (fried red kidney beans), Ubugali (cassava fufu), Matoke (steamed plantains).
music: The Royal Drummers of Burundi (world-renowned polyrhythmic percussion using ancient hollowed-out tree drums), Inanga string zither music.
dance: Agasimbo acrobatic leap dancing, Intore warrior dance, Umutsibo.
art: Agaseke woven lidded peace baskets, geometric calabash engravings, wooden spear and shield carvings.
architecture: Traditional circular royal compounds (Ingome) built of bamboo and thatch; colonial lakeside villas in Bujumbura.
literature: Gérard Niyungeko, Roland Rugero (Baho!), rich oral traditions of heroic poetry (Ibyivugo).
cinema: Emerging documentary cinema; FESTICAB (Burundi International Film Festival).
sports: Athletics (Vénuste Niyongabo 1996 Olympic 5000m Gold, Francine Niyonsaba 2016 Olympic 800m Silver), Football (Intamba mu Rugamba, 2019 AFCON qualification).
media: RTNB (Radio-Télévision Nationale du Burundi), Iwacu newspaper, Radio Isanganiro.
clothing: Imvutano traditional flowing ceremonial wrap worn by women; modern tailored attire.
crafts: Intricate Agaseke coil-woven baskets, wood carvings, clay pottery.
unescoIntangible: Ritual dance of the royal drum (inscribed 2014)
famousPeople: Gaël Faye (novelist and musician, Small Country)
flagDescription: A white saltire (diagonal cross) dividing the flag into alternating red (top and bottom) and green (hoist and fly) triangles, with a white central disk containing three red six-pointed stars edged in green arranged in a triangle.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features the head of a lion on a red shield, behind which three traditional African spears emerge, resting above a scroll bearing the motto 'Ubumwe, Ibikorwa, Iterambere'.
travelNotes: Visitors captivated by the thunderous energy of the Gishora drummers and tranquil shores of Lake Tanganyika; hospitality is gentle and heartfelt.
shortSummary: Burundi, the verdant 'Heart of Africa', rises amidst the rolling emerald hills of the Great Rift Valley, famed worldwide for the awe-inspiring polyrhythms of its UNESCO-inscribed Royal Drummers and the pristine expanse of Lake Tanganyika.
geography: Highest point: Mount Heha (2,684 m). Lowest point: Lake Tanganyika (772 m). Longest river: Ruvubu River (part of uppermost Nile Basin) / Rusizi River. Climate: Equatorial highland with two wet seasons (February–May, September–November); pleasantly cool in mountains, hot along Lake Tanganyika. Biodiversity: Kibira National Park (montane rainforest harboring chimpanzees and colobus monkeys) and Ruvubu National Park.
economy: Sectors: Agriculture 40%, Services 42%, Industry 18%. Key industries: Light consumer goods manufacturing, Coffee and tea washing and processing, Beer brewing (Brarudi / Primus, Amstel), Nickel and rare earth exploration (Musongati). Natural resources: Nickel (one of world's largest undeveloped reserves), Rare earth minerals (Gakara), Vanadium, Peat, Hydropower potential. Major exports: Specialty Arabica coffee, Black tea, Gold, Rare earth minerals, Beer.
culture: Cuisine: Mukeke (delicious endemic Lake Tanganyika fish, grilled or fried), Ndagala (tiny crispy dried fish), Ibiharage (fried red kidney beans), Ubugali (cassava fufu), Matoke (steamed plantains).. Music & Dance: The Royal Drummers of Burundi (world-renowned polyrhythmic percussion using ancient hollowed-out tree drums), Inanga string zither music.. Sports: Athletics (Vénuste Niyongabo 1996 Olympic 5000m Gold, Francine Niyonsaba 2016 Olympic 800m Silver), Football (Intamba mu Rugamba, 2019 AFCON qualification).. Festivals: Independence Day Celebrations (July 1), National Drum Festival (Gitega), Fête du Travail.

name: Cabo Verde
nativeName: República de Cabo Verde / Kabu Verdi
highestPoint: Pico do Fogo (2,829 m active volcano on Fogo Island)
longestRiver: Ribeira Principal (seasonal mountain torrent streams)
majorLakes: Pedra de Lume salt crater lake (Sal)
climate: Subtropical dry and mild; tempered by the cool Canary Current and trade winds; sporadic summer rainfall
naturalHazards: Volcanic eruptions (Pico do Fogo last erupted 2014-2015)
Prolonged multi-year cyclical droughts
environmentalIssues: Soil degradation from severe wind and infrequent flash storms
Severe freshwater scarcity reliant on desalinization
biodiversity: Volcanic archipelago rich in endemic flora and reptile species, world-renowned nesting grounds for loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) on Boa Vista and Sal
languages: Cabo Verdean Creole / Kriolu (national mother tongue spoken by all)
currency: Cabo Verdean Escudo (CVE, Esc, pegged to Euro)
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister Ulisses Correia e Silva
mainPoliticalParties: African Party for the Independence of Cabo Verde (PAICV)
Democratic and Independent Cabo Verdean Union (UCID)
latestElections: Presidential election 2021 (José Maria Neves elected); legislative elections 2021; next general elections 2026
politicalSituation: Ranked among Africa's highest in good governance, press freedom, and human rights; exemplary democratic stability with peaceful alternation of power.
foreignRelations: Special Partnership with the European Union; member of ECOWAS, African Union, CPLP, UN; strong diaspora linkages across the US (New England), Portugal, France, and the Netherlands.
military: Armed Forces of Cabo Verde (National Guard and Coast Guard).
adminDivisions: 22 municipalities across 10 islands (9 inhabited: Santiago, São Vicente, Santo Antão, Fogo, Sal, Boa Vista, São Nicolau, Brava, Maio)
history: Uninhabited volcanic islands discovered and settled by Portuguese navigators in 1462. Became a central transatlantic crossroads for the slave trade, provisioning ships, and sugar production. Distinct Cabo Verdean Creole culture and language developed through blending of African and Portuguese populations. Amílcar Cabral led the intellectual and armed national liberation movement (PAIGC) in Guinea-Bissau and Cabo Verde. Achieved independence in 1975. Transitioned seamlessly to multi-party democracy in 1991.
recentEvents2020_2026: Achieved malaria-free certification from the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2024; expanded renewable wind and solar power past 35% of national generation; rebounded to record tourism surpassing 1 million annual visitors across Sal and Boa Vista.
education: University of Cabo Verde (Uni-CV); Jean Piaget University; high national literacy and compulsory schooling to age 15.
healthcare: Well-organized public health system with universal child immunization; regional hospitals in Praia and Mindelo.
socialCustoms: Morabeza (legendary Cabo Verdean spirit of warmth, hospitality, and welcoming kindness), evening tocatina music sessions in local taverns.
etiquette: Warm greetings with handshakes and polite inquiries, respect for community elders, relaxed island pacing.
nationalIdentity: Defined by Morabeza, Kriolu language, Saudade (wistful longing for the homeland felt by its massive global diaspora), and vibrant musical genres.
energy: Global leader in insular renewables: expanding wind farms (Cabeólica) and solar farms targeting 50%+ renewable electricity by 2030
tourism: Premier tourist destination in West Africa; pristine white-sand beaches and windsurfing in Sal and Boa Vista, cultural music festivals in Mindelo, trekking in Santo Antão.
employment: Hospitality and tourism services, civil service, construction, maritime transport.
debtInflation: Exchange rate stability guaranteed by currency peg to the Euro; low inflation supported by Banco de Cabo Verde.
transport: Inter-island passenger and cargo ferries (CV Interilhas); international airports connecting to Europe, the Americas, and mainland Africa.
airports: Amílcar Cabral International Airport (SID on Sal)
Nelson Mandela International Airport (RAI in Praia)
Aristides Pereira Airport (BVC on Boa Vista)
cuisine: Cachupa (national dish: slow-cooked corn, beans, cassava, sweet potato with fish or pork - served as Cachupa Rica or morning Cachupa Frita), Pastel de Milho with tuna, Grilled freshly caught Garoupa, Grogue (potent sugarcane spirit), Pudim de Queijo (goat cheese flan).
festivals: Carnaval de Mindelo (dazzling Brazilian-style Carnival on São Vicente)
music: Morna (UNESCO intangible heritage; popularized globally by the 'Barefoot Diva' Cesária Évora), Coladeira, Funaná (accordion-driven high-tempo dance), Batuque.
dance: Funaná, Coladeira, Batuque (rhythmic polyrhythmic drumming and hip movement), Passada.
art: Vibrant seaside naive painting, volcanic stone sculpture on Fogo, modern fiber arts.
architecture: Sobrado two-story colonial merchant houses in São Filipe and Mindelo; UNESCO-listed stone ruins and pillory of Cidade Velha.
literature: Claridade literary movement (Baltasar Lopes, Manuel Lopes), Germano Almeida (The Last Will and Testament of Senhor da Silva Araújo, Camões Prize winner).
cinema: Mindelo International Film Festival (Oiá); internationally acclaimed short films and music documentaries.
sports: Windsurfing and Kitesurfing (world champions Josh Angulo, Airton Cozzolino), Football (Blue Sharks / Tubarões Azuis, historic 2024 AFCON quarter-finalists), Basketball (Edy Tavares, Real Madrid EuroLeague superstar).
media: RTC (Radiotelevisão Caboverdiana), A Nação, Expresso das Ilhas.
clothing: Pano de Terra (traditional handwoven geometric cotton wrap cloth); vibrant contemporary island resort fashion.
crafts: Pano de Terra weaving, coconut shell carvings, volcanic ash figurines from Fogo, clay pottery.
worldHeritageSites: Cidade Velha, Historic Centre of Ribeira Grande (first European colonial settlement in the tropics)
unescoIntangible: Morna, musical practice of Cabo Verde (inscribed 2019)
flagDescription: A blue field with a horizontal white-red-white band crossing the lower half, overlaid towards the hoist side with a circle of ten yellow five-pointed stars representing the main islands.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a blue triangle enclosing a white torch over three curved blue waves, encircled by ten gold stars and laurel branches, topped by a plumb-bob representing rectitude.
landmarks: Cidade Velha and Fort Real de São Filipe
travelNotes: Very safe, welcoming destination; excellent conditions for hiking, diving, and wind sports; celebrated worldwide for live music in every seaside café.
shortSummary: Cabo Verde is an enchanting Atlantic archipelago of ten volcanic islands, celebrated as an African model of democratic freedom, home to soulful UNESCO-inscribed Morna music, and stunning golden beaches.
geography: Highest point: Pico do Fogo (2,829 m active volcano on Fogo Island). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Ribeira Principal (seasonal mountain torrent streams). Climate: Subtropical dry and mild; tempered by the cool Canary Current and trade winds; sporadic summer rainfall. Biodiversity: Volcanic archipelago rich in endemic flora and reptile species, world-renowned nesting grounds for loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) on Boa Vista and Sal.
economy: Sectors: Services & Tourism 75%, Industry 17%, Agriculture & Fisheries 8%. Key industries: Tourism and coastal resort hospitality, Fish canning (tuna and mackerel), Beverage production (grogue rum, Strela beer), Shoe and textile manufacturing, Ship repair and bunkering. Natural resources: Salt (Sal island), Pozzolana (volcanic rock for cement), Fish and seafood, Sun and wind energy. Major exports: Processed and canned fish, Scrap metals, Footwear and garments, Grogue rum, Specialty Fogo coffee.
culture: Cuisine: Cachupa (national dish: slow-cooked corn, beans, cassava, sweet potato with fish or pork - served as Cachupa Rica or morning Cachupa Frita), Pastel de Milho with tuna, Grilled freshly caught Garoupa, Grogue (potent sugarcane spirit), Pudim de Queijo (goat cheese flan).. Music & Dance: Morna (UNESCO intangible heritage; popularized globally by the 'Barefoot Diva' Cesária Évora), Coladeira, Funaná (accordion-driven high-tempo dance), Batuque.. Sports: Windsurfing and Kitesurfing (world champions Josh Angulo, Airton Cozzolino), Football (Blue Sharks / Tubarões Azuis, historic 2024 AFCON quarter-finalists), Basketball (Edy Tavares, Real Madrid EuroLeague superstar).. Festivals: Carnaval de Mindelo (dazzling Brazilian-style Carnival on São Vicente), Baía das Gatas Music Festival, Kriol Jazz Festival (Praia), Gamboa Festival.
sources: National Statistical Office of Cabo Verde

name: Cameroon
nativeName: République du Cameroun / Republic of Cameroon
nationalAnthem: Chant de Ralliement (O Cameroon, Cradle of our Forefathers)
motto: Paix, Travail, Patrie / Peace, Work, Fatherland
highestPoint: Mount Cameroon / Fako (4,040 m active volcano)
lowestPoint: Bight of Biafra / Atlantic Ocean (0 m)
longestRiver: Sanaga River (918 km)
climate: Tropical and humid along southern coastal belt; equatorial rainforest in central and southern interior; semi-arid Sahel in the far north
naturalHazards: Volcanic activity at Mount Cameroon
Limnic eruption gas release risk at crater lakes (Lake Nyos)
Seasonal flash flooding in northern plains
environmentalIssues: Deforestation in the Congo Basin fringe
biodiversity: Often called 'Africa in Miniature' for encompassing every major African ecological zone: dense equatorial jungle, coastal mangroves, volcanic highlands, and northern savanna with Dja Faunal Reserve
mainPoliticalParties: Movement for the Renaissance of Cameroon (MRC)
latestElections: Presidential election 2018; legislative/municipal 2020; presidential and legislative elections scheduled 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Long-serving President Paul Biya; ongoing dialogue and reconstruction efforts in the Anglophone Northwest and Southwest regions; major infrastructure modernization (Kribi Deep Sea Port).
foreignRelations: Member of CEMAC, African Union, Commonwealth of Nations, Francophonie, UN; major regional economic powerhouse of Central Africa.
military: Cameroon Armed Forces (FAC) including the elite Rapid Intervention Battalion (BIR).
adminDivisions: 10 regions
history: Site of the ancient Sao civilization around Lake Chad and the powerful Mandara Kingdom; ancestral homeland of the Bantu migrations that populated Central and Southern Africa. German protectorate established in 1884 as Kamerun. Following WWI, partitioned by the League of Nations into French Cameroun and British Cameroons. French Cameroun gained independence in 1960 under Ahmadou Ahidjo, joining with southern British Cameroons in 1961 to form a bilingual federal republic. Paul Biya succeeded to the presidency in 1982.
recentEvents2020_2026: Successfully hosted the 33rd Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) in 2022; expanded the Kribi Deep Sea Port second phase; advanced the Nachtigal 420MW hydroelectric dam into full commercial operation; deepened Central African transport corridors.
education: Bilingual university system: University of Yaoundé I & II, University of Buea (Anglo-Saxon model), University of Douala.
healthcare: Provincial and district referral hospital network; expanding national universal health coverage (CSU) pilot.
socialCustoms: Chefferies (traditional sacred chiefdoms of the Bamiléké and Bamum kingdoms), elaborate funeral ceremonies celebrating life, vibrant street snack culture.
etiquette: Respectful greetings inquiring about family, sharing kola nuts as a sign of welcome and respect, respectful posture before traditional Fons (rulers).
nationalIdentity: Celebrated as 'Africa in Miniature', footballing supremacy (Indomitable Lions), Makossa music, and bilingual coexistence.
industries: Petroleum and natural gas extraction and refining (Limbe)
energy: Abundant hydroelectricity (Sanaga River, Song Loulou, Edéa, Nachtigal 420MW facility) generating over 70% of national power
tourism: Eco-tourism and cultural tours: climbing Mount Cameroon (Race of Hope), wildlife viewing in Waza and Lobéké National Parks, visiting the Royal Palace of Foumban.
employment: Informal services, agro-industrial plantations (CDC, Socapalm), civil administration, shipping logistics.
debtInflation: Anchor economy of CEMAC; monetary policy directed by BEAC maintaining regional foreign currency reserves.
transport: Trans-Cameroon railway (Camrail) connecting Douala to Ngaoundéré; modern deep-sea container terminal at Kribi.
ports: Port of Douala (historic estuary commercial hub)
Port of Kribi (modern deepwater port capable of handling Cape-size vessels)
cuisine: Ndolé (bitterleaf stew with peanuts, crayfish, shrimp or beef), Poulet DG (chicken with plantains and bell peppers), Achu soup with yellow sauce, Koki beans, Eru with water fufu, Suya skewers.
festivals: Nguon Festival of the Bamum Kingdom (UNESCO recognized)
Ngondo water festival of the Sawa people on the Wouri River
music: Makossa (Manu Dibango's 'Soul Makossa'), Bikutsi (fast 6/8 polyrhythm popularized by Les Têtes Brulées), Assiko, modern Afro-pop.
dance: Bikutsi hip movements, Makossa, Bamum royal court dances.
art: Bamum bronze casting, Bamiléké beaded elephant masks and carved wooden thrones, Bamenda Grassfields royal stools.
architecture: Royal Palace of Foumban (incorporating German and traditional Bamum architecture); earthen domed Mousgoum huts (teleuk) in the Far North.
literature: Mongo Beti (Poor Christ of Bomba), Ferdinand Oyono (Houseboy), Francis Bebey, Calixthe Beyala.
cinema: Jean-Pierre Bekolo (Quartier Mozart), Bassek Ba Kobhio (Sango Malo); Ecrans Noirs film festival in Yaoundé.
sports: Football: Indomitable Lions (5-time AFCON champions, historic 1990 World Cup quarter-finalists; legendary stars Samuel Eto'o, Roger Milla), MMA / Boxing (Francis Ngannou, UFC Heavyweight Champion).
media: Cameroon Tribune, CRTV (Cameroon Radio Television), Canal 2 International, Equinoxe TV.
clothing: Toghu (intricately embroidered heavy black velvet royal tunic from the Northwest), Kaba Ngondo loose flowing dress worn by Sawa women.
crafts: Intricately embroidered Toghu fabrics, beadwork, bronze foundry sculptures, woven cane furniture.
worldHeritageSites: Sangha Trinational (Lobéké National Park sector shared with CAR and Congo)
unescoIntangible: Nguon, rituals of guidance and associated expressions of the Bamum community (inscribed 2023)
flagDescription: Three equal vertical bands of green, red, and yellow, with a yellow five-pointed star in the center of the red band (the 'Star of Unity').
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a shield with the map of Cameroon and scales of justice against the national colors, supported by crossed fasces and the motto 'Paix, Travail, Patrie'.
landmarks: Royal Palace of the Sultan of Foumban
Lobe Waterfalls (plunging directly into the ocean)
travelNotes: A world in one country with unmatched ecological and cultural diversity; Douala is a bustling commercial center, while Kribi offers tranquil palm-fringed ocean beaches.
shortSummary: Cameroon is celebrated as 'Africa in Miniature' for its stunning geographic spectrum from Mount Cameroon's volcanic peak to northern savanna reserves, its world-famous footballing legacy, and the infectious grooves of Makossa music.
geography: Highest point: Mount Cameroon / Fako (4,040 m active volcano). Lowest point: Bight of Biafra / Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Sanaga River (918 km). Climate: Tropical and humid along southern coastal belt; equatorial rainforest in central and southern interior; semi-arid Sahel in the far north. Biodiversity: Often called 'Africa in Miniature' for encompassing every major African ecological zone: dense equatorial jungle, coastal mangroves, volcanic highlands, and northern savanna with Dja Faunal Reserve.
economy: Sectors: Services 50%, Agriculture 22%, Industry 28%. Key industries: Petroleum and natural gas extraction and refining (Limbe), Aluminium smelting (Alucam), Food processing (beverages, cocoa, sugar), Timber processing, Cement and construction materials. Natural resources: Crude petroleum, Natural gas, Bauxite (Minim-Martap), Iron ore (Mbalam), Timber, Hydropower. Major exports: Crude petroleum, Cocoa beans and paste, Sawn timber and logs, Liquefied natural gas, Bananas, Aluminium.
culture: Cuisine: Ndolé (bitterleaf stew with peanuts, crayfish, shrimp or beef), Poulet DG (chicken with plantains and bell peppers), Achu soup with yellow sauce, Koki beans, Eru with water fufu, Suya skewers.. Music & Dance: Makossa (Manu Dibango's 'Soul Makossa'), Bikutsi (fast 6/8 polyrhythm popularized by Les Têtes Brulées), Assiko, modern Afro-pop.. Sports: Football: Indomitable Lions (5-time AFCON champions, historic 1990 World Cup quarter-finalists; legendary stars Samuel Eto'o, Roger Milla), MMA / Boxing (Francis Ngannou, UFC Heavyweight Champion).. Festivals: Nguon Festival of the Bamum Kingdom (UNESCO recognized), Mount Cameroon Race of Hope, Ngondo water festival of the Sawa people on the Wouri River.

name: Central African Republic
motto: Zo Kwe Zo (Every human being is a person)
highestPoint: Mont Ngaoui (1,410 m)
longestRiver: Ubangi River (major Congo tributary, border river)
climate: Tropical wet-and-dry with a wet season from May to October; hot humid equatorial climate in the far southern rainforests
naturalHazards: Harmattan dusty winter winds
Periodic flash floods along the Ubangi river basin
Wildfires in dry savanna season
environmentalIssues: Poaching of forest elephants and rhinos
biodiversity: Dzanga-Sangha Special Reserve harboring extraordinary densities of western lowland gorillas and forest elephants gathering at the Dzanga Bai mineral clearing
languages: Sango (national language spoken across the country)
latestElections: Presidential/legislative elections 2020/2021; constitutional referendum 2023; general elections scheduled 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Restoration of state authority across provincial administrative centers under President Touadéra with MINUSCA peacekeeping support and bilateral security assistance; economic formalization.
foreignRelations: Member of CEMAC, African Union, Francophonie, UN; strategic security cooperation with Russia, Rwanda, and multilateral stabilization partners.
military: Central African Armed Forces (FACA).
adminDivisions: 20 prefectures (including capital city of Bangui)
history: Inhabited by diverse hunter-gatherer and agriculturalist societies; ancient megaliths of Bouar date back to the 1st millennium BC. Devastated by 18th- and 19th-century slave raiding from coastal kingdoms and northern sultanates. Colonized by France in the late 19th century as Ubangi-Shari (Oubangui-Chari), marked by harsh concessionary rubber and cotton regimes. Barthélemy Boganda emerged as founding visionary, coining the national motto 'Zo Kwe Zo' before his untimely death in 1959. Independence achieved in 1960. Underwent turbulent decades including the regime of Jean-Bédel Bokassa (who proclaimed himself Emperor Bokassa I in 1976). Faustin-Archange Touadéra elected president in 2016.
recentEvents2020_2026: Enacted the 2023 Constitution; secured greater territorial control over major mining corridors; advanced agricultural recovery programs; deepened regional trade via the Ubangi River and Bangui-Douala transit corridor.
historicalFigures: Barthélemy Boganda (founding father and pan-African visionary)
education: University of Bangui; rebuilding primary schooling infrastructure across rural prefectures.
healthcare: Bangui Community Hospital; reliance on international humanitarian healthcare partners and missionary clinics.
socialCustoms: Zo Kwe Zo humanistic philosophy emphasizing universal dignity, communal clearing and harvest groups (Koubaye), storytelling under moonlight.
etiquette: Gentle handshakes with warm eye contact, sharing meals from common platters, greeting neighbors respectfully in Sango.
nationalIdentity: Unified by the universally spoken indigenous Sango language, reverence for Barthélemy Boganda, and natural wonders like the Boali Falls.
energy: Boali Hydroelectric Falls power station supplying Bangui, supplemented by thermal generators and expanding solar arrays (Danzi Solar Plant)
tourism: Pristine wilderness tourism centered on Dzanga-Sangha National Park (world-class tracking of western lowland gorillas, forest elephants, and bongo antelopes) and Boali Waterfalls.
employment: Predominantly artisanal diamond mining, subsistence farming, and small-scale riverine commerce.
debtInflation: Financial support under IMF Extended Credit Facility program; currency stability provided by the Central African CFA franc.
transport: Barge transport on the Ubangi River during high-water season; vital road freight corridor linking Bangui to the Port of Douala (Cameroon).
ports: River Port of Bangui (on the Ubangi River)
cuisine: Kanda ti nyma (beef meatballs wrapped in crushed pumpkin seed paste), Gozo (thick cassava fufu dough), Maboké (fresh river fish steamed in banana leaves with spices), Ngunza (cassava leaves stewed with peanut butter), Fried plantains (Alloco).
music: Traditional Sanza (thumb piano) music, Polyphonic singing of the Aka Pygmies (UNESCO masterpiece), Central African rumba.
dance: Gbégbé, Montika, traditional initiation dances.
art: Butterfly wing mosaic art (tableaux en ailes de papillon) distinctive to Bangui, carved wooden stools, woven fiber baskets.
architecture: Colonial brick and red clay tile buildings in central Bangui; traditional round thatched earthen houses in rural savanna.
literature: Pierre Makombo Bamboté, Étienne Goyémidé (Le Silence de la forêt), Adrienne Yabouza.
cinema: Léonce Ngabo, emerging documentary cinema showcasing cultural preservation.
sports: Basketball (national passion; 2-time AfroBasket Champions: 1974, 1987), Football (Les Fauves du Bas-Oubangui).
media: Le Confident, L'Hirondelle, Radio Ndeke Luka (leading independent radio station), Télévision Centrafricaine (TVCA).
clothing: Vibrant tailored boubous and pagne wrap skirts; western casual wear in Bangui.
crafts: Butterfly wing collages, wooden mortars and pestles, woven fish traps, beadwork.
worldHeritageSites: Sangha Trinational (Dzanga-Ndoki National Park sector shared with Cameroon and Congo)
unescoIntangible: Polyphonic singing of the Aka Pygmies of Central Africa (inscribed 2008)
flagDescription: Four horizontal bands of blue, white, green, and yellow, overlaid by a vertical red band down the center, with a yellow five-pointed star in the upper hoist corner of the blue band.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a quartered shield with an elephant head, a baobab tree, three stars, and an open hand, behind two national flags and beneath a rising sun over the motto 'Zo Kwe Zo'.
travelNotes: Travel requires specialized planning and guided ecotourism logistics; Dzanga-Sangha is an incomparable, once-in-a-lifetime wildlife destination for dedicated eco-travelers.
shortSummary: The Central African Republic sits at the ecological heart of the continent, home to the universally spoken Sango tongue, the magical forest elephants and gorillas of Dzanga-Sangha, and the humanistic philosophy of 'Zo Kwe Zo'.
geography: Highest point: Mont Ngaoui (1,410 m). Lowest point: Ubangi River (335 m). Longest river: Ubangi River (major Congo tributary, border river). Climate: Tropical wet-and-dry with a wet season from May to October; hot humid equatorial climate in the far southern rainforests. Biodiversity: Dzanga-Sangha Special Reserve harboring extraordinary densities of western lowland gorillas and forest elephants gathering at the Dzanga Bai mineral clearing.
economy: Sectors: Agriculture 53%, Services 32%, Industry 15%. Key industries: Artisanal diamond and gold mining, Timber and lumber sawmilling, Brewing (Mocaf beer), Cotton processing and soap manufacturing. Natural resources: Diamonds (high-value gem quality), Gold, Uranium (Bakouma), Timber, Arable land, Hydropower. Major exports: Rough diamonds, Timber and logs, Gold, Coffee, Cotton.
culture: Cuisine: Kanda ti nyma (beef meatballs wrapped in crushed pumpkin seed paste), Gozo (thick cassava fufu dough), Maboké (fresh river fish steamed in banana leaves with spices), Ngunza (cassava leaves stewed with peanut butter), Fried plantains (Alloco).. Music & Dance: Traditional Sanza (thumb piano) music, Polyphonic singing of the Aka Pygmies (UNESCO masterpiece), Central African rumba.. Sports: Basketball (national passion; 2-time AfroBasket Champions: 1974, 1987), Football (Les Fauves du Bas-Oubangui).. Festivals: Republic Day (December 1), Boganda Day (March 29), Independence Day (August 13).
sources: National Statistical Office of Central African Republic

name: Chad
nationalDay: August 11 (Independence Day), December 1 (Freedom and Democracy Day)
highestPoint: Emi Koussi in the Tibesti Mountains (3,445 m volcanic peak)
longestRiver: Chari River (1,400 km)
majorLakes: Lakes of Ounianga (UNESCO desert oasis lakes)
climate: Hyper-arid desert in the northern Sahara; semi-arid Sahelian belt in the center; tropical savanna with summer rains in the southern Soudanian zone
naturalHazards: Hot, dry, dust-laden Harmattan winds
Recurrent severe droughts
Plagues of desert locusts
biodiversity: Zakouma National Park, celebrated as one of Africa's greatest conservation turnarounds, home to revitalized herds of African elephants, Kordofan giraffes, and lions
languages: Chadian Arabic (official and national lingua franca)
mainPoliticalParties: National Union for Democracy and Renewal (UNDR)
latestElections: Presidential election May 2024 (Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno elected); legislative and local elections December 2024
politicalSituation: Completion of constitutional transition with peaceful elections in 2024; Chad acts as a pivotal military anchor for regional counter-terror operations and refugee humanitarian response.
foreignRelations: Member of CEMAC, Community of Sahel-Saharan States (CEN-SAD), African Union, Francophonie, OIC, UN; key regional security partner with France, the US, and neighboring states.
military: Chadian National Army (ANT), renowned across the Sahel as one of the region's most battle-hardened and mobile armed forces.
adminDivisions: 23 provinces
history: Inhabited since the dawn of humanity (fossil hominid 'Toumaï' / Sahelanthropus tchadensis discovered in the Djurab Desert dating back 7 million years). Major medieval Sahelian empires flourished, notably the Kanem-Bornu Empire, the Bagirmi Sultanate, and the Wadai Empire, dominating trans-Saharan trade routes. French conquered the region by 1900, incorporating it into French Equatorial Africa. Independence gained in 1960 under François Tombalbaye. Post-independence era experienced civil conflict and the Libyan-Chadian War (1978–1987, famous for the 'Toyota War'). Idriss Déby ruled from 1990 until his death in 2021; succeeded by his son Mahamat Déby.
recentEvents2020_2026: Adopted the Fifth Republic Constitution in 2023; concluded transition with democratic elections in 2024; hosted over one million Sudanese refugees fleeing the Darfur war; nationalized key oil assets (Chad-Cameroon pipeline) to bolster state revenues.
education: University of N'Djamena; King Faisal University; vocational training centers in Moundou and Sarh.
healthcare: National General Referral Hospital of N'Djamena; expanding vaccination coverage across mobile pastoralist populations.
socialCustoms: Strong traditions of nomadic hospitality (diyafa), mint tea ceremonies with three rounds, elder mediation in family and clan matters.
etiquette: Greetings with right hand placed over the heart, respectful inquiries before discussing business, modesty in dress.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated as the 'Dead Heart of Africa' transformed into the resilient soul of the Sahel, proud warrior traditions, and astonishing geological monuments.
energy: Expanding solar mini-grids and the Sedigui gas-to-power generation plant complementing thermal fuel stations in N'Djamena
exports: Crude petroleum (via Chad-Cameroon pipeline to Kribi)
tourism: Extraordinary adventure tourism: UNESCO-listed Ennedi Massif sandstone towers and arches, Lakes of Ounianga, Zakouma National Park safari expeditions, and prehistoric Saharan rock art.
employment: Over 80% engaged in pastoral livestock herding, subsistence agriculture, and cross-border Sahelian trade.
debtInflation: First nation to conclude debt treatment under the G20 Common Framework; CEMAC monetary discipline.
transport: Trans-Sahelian road corridors connecting to Douala and Port Sudan; heavy reliance on seasonal trucking routes.
airports: Hassan Djamous International Airport (NDJ in N'Djamena)
ports: Landlocked; primary oceanic freight access through Port of Douala and Port of Kribi in Cameroon
cuisine: Daraba (okra, sweet potato, and peanut butter stew with dried fish or meat), Kissar (fluffy sourdough pancake crepe), La Bouillie (warm spiced grain porridge with peanut and lemon), Chadian grilled mutton skewers, Karkadeh (hibiscus tea).
festivals: Gerewol festival of the Wodaabe (courtship dance in southern Chad)
music: Traditional Chadian lute (Chégué), Kakaki long horns, modern Chadian rhythms (Tibesti band, Maoundoé Célestin).
dance: Sai dance, Gourna dance of the Toupouri, acrobatic camel dances.
art: Ancient Sao terracotta heads, stunning prehistoric rock paintings of the Ennedi, woven camel hair carpets.
architecture: Mud-brick earthen architecture of the Wadai Sultanate; monumental sandstone arches sculpted by wind in Ennedi; modern Grand Mosque of N'Djamena.
literature: Antoine Bangui (Prisonnier de Tombalbaye), Nimrod (poet and essayist), Koulsy Lamko.
cinema: Mahamat-Saleh Haroun (one of Africa's greatest film directors: A Screaming Man won Cannes Jury Prize 2010; Daratt; Lingui, The Sacred Bonds).
sports: Football (Les Sao), Traditional wrestling (lutte traditionnelle, immensely popular spectator sport), Athletics.
media: Le Progrès, N'Djamena Hebdo, ONAMA (Office National des Médias Audiovisuels).
clothing: White or embroidered Djellaba and turban (Tagelmust) for men; colorful Lafai wrap sheets worn by women.
crafts: Hand-tooled camel leather saddles, woven colorful mats, brass ornaments, hand-knotted desert rugs.
worldHeritageSites: Lakes of Ounianga (18 interconnected hyper-saline and freshwater desert lakes)
Ennedi Massif: Natural and Cultural Landscape
unescoIntangible: Oral and cultural traditions of the Ennedi plateau
flagDescription: Three equal vertical bands of blue (sky, hope, and southern agriculture), yellow (sun and northern desert), and red (progress, unity, and blood shed for independence) - identical in design to the flag of Romania.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a shield with yellow and blue zigzag lines, supported by a goat (representing the north) and a lion (representing the south), surmounted by a rising sun and the motto 'Unité, Travail, Progrès'.
travelNotes: Remote and awe-inspiring desert destination requiring licensed expedition operators; Ennedi and Zakouma offer some of the most pristine and majestic landscapes on earth.
shortSummary: Chad, the geographic crossroads where the Sahara meets the Sahel, astounds with the wind-carved sandstone arches of Ennedi, the miraculous desert oasis lakes of Ounianga, and the acclaimed cinema of Mahamat-Saleh Haroun.
geography: Highest point: Emi Koussi in the Tibesti Mountains (3,445 m volcanic peak). Lowest point: Bodélé Depression (160 m). Longest river: Chari River (1,400 km). Climate: Hyper-arid desert in the northern Sahara; semi-arid Sahelian belt in the center; tropical savanna with summer rains in the southern Soudanian zone. Biodiversity: Zakouma National Park, celebrated as one of Africa's greatest conservation turnarounds, home to revitalized herds of African elephants, Kordofan giraffes, and lions.
economy: Sectors: Agriculture & Livestock 45%, Oil & Industry 28%, Services 27%. Key industries: Crude petroleum extraction (Doba oilfields), Cotton processing (Cotontchad in Moundou), Brewing (Gala beer), Textiles and leather tanning, Gum arabic processing. Natural resources: Petroleum, Uranium, Natron (soda ash), Kaolin, Fish (Lake Chad), Gold. Major exports: Crude petroleum (via Chad-Cameroon pipeline to Kribi), Raw cotton, Live cattle and meat, Gum arabic, Sesame.
culture: Cuisine: Daraba (okra, sweet potato, and peanut butter stew with dried fish or meat), Kissar (fluffy sourdough pancake crepe), La Bouillie (warm spiced grain porridge with peanut and lemon), Chadian grilled mutton skewers, Karkadeh (hibiscus tea).. Music & Dance: Traditional Chadian lute (Chégué), Kakaki long horns, modern Chadian rhythms (Tibesti band, Maoundoé Célestin).. Sports: Football (Les Sao), Traditional wrestling (lutte traditionnelle, immensely popular spectator sport), Athletics.. Festivals: Gerewol festival of the Wodaabe (courtship dance in southern Chad), National Day (August 11), Dary Festival (National Cultural Festival).

name: Comoros
nativeName: Udzima wa Komori / Union des Comores / الاتحاد القمري
nationalAnthem: Udzima wa ya Masiwa (The Union of the Great Islands)
highestPoint: Mount Karthala (2,361 m active shield volcano)
longestRiver: Short seasonal mountain streams / crater lake streams
majorLakes: Dziani Boundouni (saline crater lake on Mohéli)
