climate: Tropical marine with two seasons: hot and humid rainy season from November to April, and a cooler dry season from May to October
naturalHazards: Eruptions and volcanic ash from Mount Karthala
Tropical cyclones during the monsoon season
Tsunamis risk
environmentalIssues: Deforestation for firewood and ylang-ylang distillation
Soil erosion on steep volcanic slopes
biodiversity: Mohéli Marine Park (sanctuary for green sea turtles and dugongs), Mount Karthala endemic scops owl, Livingstone's fruit bat, and the prehistoric Coelacanth fish in surrounding deep waters
currency: Comorian Franc (KMF, CF, pegged to Euro)
legislature: Assembly of the Union (Assemblée de l'Union)
mainPoliticalParties: Convention for the Renewal of the Comoros (CRC)
latestElections: Presidential election January 2024 (Azali Assoumani re-elected); legislative elections scheduled 2025
politicalSituation: President Azali Assoumani served as Chairperson of the African Union in 2023; focus on the 'Emerging Comoros 2030' plan, port expansions, and renewable geothermal exploration on Mount Karthala.
foreignRelations: Member of Indian Ocean Commission (IOC), Arab League, African Union, Francophonie, OIC, UN; strong partnerships with France, Saudi Arabia, UAE, China, and Morocco.
military: National Army of Development (AND) comprising Defense Forces and Gendarmerie.
adminDivisions: 3 autonomous islands: Grande Comore (Ngazidja), Anjouan (Nzwani), and Mohéli (Mwali)
history: Settled by Austronesian voyagers, Bantu agriculturalists, and Shirazi Arab and Persian merchants from the 8th century onwards, establishing prosperous island sultanates. Known as the 'Perfume Islands' for their rich spices and essential oils. French protectorate declared over Mayotte in 1841 and over the other three islands by 1886. Gained independence in 1975, while Mayotte chose to remain under French administration. Experienced over 20 coups and mercenary interventions (notably Bob Denard) before establishing the 2001 Fomboni reconciliation accord creating a rotating presidency among the three islands.
recentEvents2020_2026: Chaired the African Union throughout 2023; expanded deepwater port facilities at Boingoma (Mohéli) and Moroni; commenced preliminary exploratory drilling for Karthala geothermal energy; made historic debut in the Africa Cup of Nations.
historicalFigures: Sultan Said Ali bin Said Omar
ethnicGroups: Antalote, Cafre, Makoa, Oimatsaha, Sakalava (blended Afro-Arab-Malagasy) ~98%
education: University of the Comoros (established 2003); network of traditional Quranic schools (Madrasas) and public secondary colleges.
healthcare: El-Maarouf National Hospital in Moroni (modernized with international funding); regional health centers on Anjouan and Mohéli.
socialCustoms: Grand Mariage (Anda): prestigious traditional wedding system elevating social status in the community; generous gift-giving and communal feasts.
etiquette: Respectful greetings using Islamic salutations, modest dress adhering to Islamic norms, deference to village elders and notables.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the fragrance of ylang-ylang and vanilla, the cultural bond of the Shikomor tongue, devotion to Sunni Islamic traditions, and oceanic resilience.
industries: Distillation of ylang-ylang essential oil (world's top exporter)
energy: Developing Karthala geothermal energy project to replace heavy fuel oil thermal generators; expanding solar micro-grids across Mohéli and Anjouan
tourism: Eco-tourism and marine adventures: observing nesting sea turtles and humpback whales in Mohéli Marine Park, climbing Mount Karthala's vast volcanic caldera, wandering the historic Medina of Moroni.
employment: Subsistence smallholder farming, artisanal fishing, spice curing, and remittance-driven retail.
debtInflation: Currency stability anchored by French Treasury / Euro peg; substantial financial remittances from the Comorian diaspora in Marseille and Paris.
transport: Inter-island ferries; international passenger flights connecting to East Africa, Madagascar, Réunion, and France.
airports: Prince Said Ibrahim International Airport (HAH in Moroni)
cuisine: Langouste à la vanille (fresh lobster in rich vanilla sauce), Pilao (fragrant spiced meat and rice dish), Mkatra foutra (coconut milk flatbread), Mataba (mashed cassava leaves cooked in coconut cream), Ambrevades au curry (pigeon pea curry).
festivals: Maoulida (Prophet's Birthday celebration with communal drumming)
music: Twarab (hybrid of Arabic and Swahili orchestral rhythms), Mgodro (fast traditional dance beat), artists like Nawal, Salim Ali Amir, Cheikh Mc.
dance: Wadaha (pestle and mortar dance performed by women), Chigoma, Mbiwi.
art: Carved wooden doors with Arabic calligraphy, filigree gold jewelry crafted for Grand Mariage ceremonies, embroidered kofia hats.
architecture: Swahili-Arab stone town architecture in Moroni and Domoni with carved wooden lintels and coral stone mosques (Vendredi Mosque).
literature: Mohammed Toihiri (Le Kafir du Karthala), Nassur Attoumani, Soeuf Elbadawi.
cinema: Hachimiya Hadji (The Inevitable Journey), emerging documentary cinema.
sports: Football: The Coelacanths (Les Cœlacanthes, fairy-tale debut at the 2021/2022 Africa Cup of Nations reaching the round of 16), Basketball, Athletics.
media: Al-Watwan (national daily), ORTC (Office de Radio et Télévision des Comores).
clothing: Kandzu white robe with embroidered Kofia cap for men; colorful Shiromani two-piece printed cotton wrap worn gracefully by women.
holidays: March 18 (Death of President Said Mohamed Cheikh)
crafts: Intricately embroidered Kofia caps, gold wedding filigree jewelry, carved hardwood furniture.
worldHeritageSites: Historic Sultanates of the Comoros (Tentative List)
unescoIntangible: Traditions of the Grand Mariage (Anda) and artisanal ylang-ylang distillation
famousPeople: El Fardou Ben Nabouhane (historic national football striker)
Soprano (French rap star of Comorian heritage)
flagDescription: Four horizontal bands of yellow, white, red, and blue (representing Mohéli, Mayotte, Anjouan, and Grande Comore), with a green isosceles triangle based on the hoist side bearing a white crescent and four vertical white five-pointed stars.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features an Islamic crescent and four stars centered over a sunburst, surrounded by the national motto 'Unité, Solidarité, Développement' and encircled by two olive branches.
landmarks: Old Friday Mosque of Moroni (Mosquée du Vendredi)
travelNotes: An untouched, fragrant Indian Ocean gem; warm island community; respect local Islamic customs by dressing modestly outside beach resorts.
shortSummary: The Union of the Comoros, known poetically as the 'Perfume Islands', is an Indian Ocean volcanic paradise scented with ylang-ylang and vanilla, home to the living fossil Coelacanth and the dramatic caldera of Mount Karthala.
geography: Highest point: Mount Karthala (2,361 m active shield volcano). Lowest point: Indian Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Short seasonal mountain streams / crater lake streams. Climate: Tropical marine with two seasons: hot and humid rainy season from November to April, and a cooler dry season from May to October. Biodiversity: Mohéli Marine Park (sanctuary for green sea turtles and dugongs), Mount Karthala endemic scops owl, Livingstone's fruit bat, and the prehistoric Coelacanth fish in surrounding deep waters.
economy: Sectors: Agriculture & Fisheries 47%, Services 41%, Industry 12%. Key industries: Distillation of ylang-ylang essential oil (world's top exporter), Spice processing (vanilla and cloves), Artisanal fisheries, Tourism and hospitality, Construction. Natural resources: Fish and marine biodiversity, Geothermal energy potential on Karthala, Timber, Volcanic stone. Major exports: Cloves, Ylang-ylang essential oils, Vanilla beans, Scrap metal.
culture: Cuisine: Langouste à la vanille (fresh lobster in rich vanilla sauce), Pilao (fragrant spiced meat and rice dish), Mkatra foutra (coconut milk flatbread), Mataba (mashed cassava leaves cooked in coconut cream), Ambrevades au curry (pigeon pea curry).. Music & Dance: Twarab (hybrid of Arabic and Swahili orchestral rhythms), Mgodro (fast traditional dance beat), artists like Nawal, Salim Ali Amir, Cheikh Mc.. Sports: Football: The Coelacanths (Les Cœlacanthes, fairy-tale debut at the 2021/2022 Africa Cup of Nations reaching the round of 16), Basketball, Athletics.. Festivals: Independence Day (July 6), Maoulida (Prophet's Birthday celebration with communal drumming), Moroni Cultural Festival.

name: DR Congo
coastline: 37 km (narrow Atlantic access corridor at Muanda)
highestPoint: Mount Stanley / Margherita Peak in the Rwenzori Mountains (5,109 m)
longestRiver: Congo River (4,700 km, world's second-deepest and second-largest by discharge)
climate: Equatorial rainforest with high temperatures and heavy year-round rainfall in the central Congo Basin; tropical wet-and-dry in north and south; temperate alpine in eastern highlands
naturalHazards: Volcanic eruptions (Mount Nyiragongo active lava lake threatening Goma)
Earthquakes along the Great Rift Valley
Riverine flash floods
environmentalIssues: Deforestation for charcoal and agricultural expansion
Poaching of endangered mountain gorillas and okapis
biodiversity: Megadiverse global treasure harboring the world's second-largest rainforest, endemic species including the Okapi, Bonobo chimpanzee, Grauer's gorilla, and Mountain gorilla in Virunga National Park
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka (first female prime minister in DRC history)
mainPoliticalParties: Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS / Sacred Union of the Nation)
latestElections: General election December 2023 (Félix Tshisekedi re-elected president); next scheduled 2028
politicalSituation: Félix Tshisekedi second presidential term with Judith Suminwa as prime minister; focused on renegotiating strategic mineral concessions, infrastructure development, and eastern security operations (M23 conflict).
foreignRelations: Member of East African Community (EAC), SADC, ECCAS, African Union, Francophonie, UN; strategic partnerships with global powers seeking green-transition critical minerals (cobalt, copper, lithium).
military: Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC).
adminDivisions: 25 provinces and the city-province of Kinshasa
history: Heartland of renowned pre-colonial kingdoms: the Kingdom of Kongo, the Luba Empire, and the Kuba Kingdom, famous for intricate arts and administration. King Leopold II of Belgium claimed the territory as the personal 'Congo Free State' in 1885, brutalizing the population for ivory and rubber. Transferred to the Belgian state in 1908 as the Belgian Congo. Gained independence in 1960 under Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba, who was assassinated in 1961 amidst Cold War machinations. Mobutu Sese Seko seized power in 1965, ruling for 32 years and renaming the country Zaire. Ousted in 1997 by Laurent-Désiré Kabila during the First Congo War. The devastating Second Congo War (1998–2003) involved nine African nations. Peaceful historic transfer of power occurred in 2019 when Félix Tshisekedi took office.
recentEvents2020_2026: Joined the East African Community (EAC) in 2022; hosted Pope Francis in Kinshasa in 2023; re-elected President Tshisekedi and appointed Judith Suminwa Tuluka as DRC's first female prime minister in 2024; expanded copper and cobalt processing making DRC the world's #2 copper producer.
ethnicGroups: Over 250 ethnic groups: Luba ~18%, Mongo ~17%, Kongo ~12%, Mangbetu-Azande ~10%, other Bantu, Nilotic, and Pygmy groups ~43%
education: University of Kinshasa (UNIKIN), University of Lubumbashi; nationwide free primary education program expanding enrollment by millions.
healthcare: Panzi Hospital in Bukavu (founded by Nobel Laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege); regional referral networks and expanding epidemic response.
socialCustoms: Vibrant megacity life in Kinshasa (Kin la Belle), Matanga mourning wakes, Sapeur movement, intense debate and high fashion.
etiquette: Respectful greetings, shaking hands with warmth, addressing elders with deference, vibrant conversational humor.
nationalIdentity: Bound by the Congo River, Lingala music, Congolese Rumba, the Sapeur aesthetic, and an extraordinary spirit of artistic creativity and resilience.
industries: Copper and cobalt extraction and smelting (Kolwezi, Tenke Fungurume, Kamoa-Kakula)
energy: Inga I and Inga II hydroelectric complexes on the Congo River; ongoing preparations for the transformative Grand Inga Dam project (potential 40,000+ MW capacity)
tourism: Incomparable adventure and eco-tourism: tracking mountain gorillas in Virunga National Park, climbing the active lava lake of Mount Nyiragongo, cruising the mighty Congo River, visiting the Bonobo Sanctuary at Lola ya Bonobo.
employment: Artisanal and industrial mining, subsistence agriculture, informal urban transport and commerce.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic stabilization supported by high mining export revenues and IMF programs; central bank modernization.
transport: Inland waterways along the 4,700 km Congo River; Matadi-Kinshasa Railway and Atlantic corridor; modernizing RN1 national highway.
ports: Port of Matadi (major maritime river port)
cuisine: Moambé chicken (poulet à la moambé: chicken simmered in rich palm nut butter sauce), Fufu (cassava or corn paste), Pondu (stewed cassava leaves with garlic and fish), Liboke de poisson (fish steamed in marantaceae leaves), Makayabu (salted cod), Mikate (fried dough balls).
music: Congolese Rumba (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage; Franco Luambo, Tabu Ley Rochereau, Papa Wemba, Koffi Olomide, Fally Ipupa, Innoss'B), Soukous, Ndombolo.
dance: Ndombolo, Kwassa Kwassa, Soukous dancing, Mutuashi.
art: La Sape (Society of Ambianceurs and Elegant Persons: flamboyant sartorial elegance), Kuba geometric textiles, Pende wooden masks, Chéri Samba contemporary pop art.
architecture: Colonial Beaux-Arts and modernist architecture in Kinshasa and Lubumbashi; Palais de la Nation; traditional woven Kuba royal residences.
literature: Sony Lab'ou Tansi, Alain Mabanckou (Congolese heritage), Fiston Mwanza Mujila (Tram 83), V.Y. Mudimbe (The Invention of Africa).
cinema: Baloji (Omen, won New Voice Prize at Cannes 2023), Dieudo Hamadi (Downstream to Kinshasa).
sports: Football (TP Mazembe: 5-time CAF Champions League winners; Leopards: 2-time AFCON champions), Basketball (Dikembe Mutombo, NBA Hall of Famer and humanitarian; Jonathan Kuminga, Bismack Biyombo).
media: Radio Okapi, RTNC (Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise), Top Congo FM, Actualite.cd.
clothing: La Sape designer haute couture (bright suits, bespoke hats, silk ties); Liputa vibrant Dutch wax print dresses.
holidays: January 16–17 (Laurent Kabila & Patrice Lumumba Hero Days)
crafts: Kuba raffia cloth, carved Malachite stone jewelry and ornaments, wooden masks, copper repoussé art.
unescoIntangible: Congolese Rumba (inscribed 2021)
flagDescription: A sky-blue field divided diagonally from bottom hoist to top fly by a red stripe with yellow borders, with a yellow five-pointed star in the upper hoist canton.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a leopard head surrounded by an elephant tusk and a spear, resting on a stone base with the motto 'Justice, Paix, Travail'.
travelNotes: Travel requires specialized logistics and security awareness; Kinshasa is one of the world's most vibrant musical capitals; Virunga is a conservation wonder of planet Earth.
shortSummary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a continent-sized titan of nature, encompassing the boundless Congo River, the gorilla-inhabited Virunga peaks, indispensable mineral wealth for the world's green energy transition, and the intoxicating, UNESCO-honored rhythms of Congolese Rumba.
geography: Highest point: Mount Stanley / Margherita Peak in the Rwenzori Mountains (5,109 m). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Congo River (4,700 km, world's second-deepest and second-largest by discharge). Climate: Equatorial rainforest with high temperatures and heavy year-round rainfall in the central Congo Basin; tropical wet-and-dry in north and south; temperate alpine in eastern highlands. Biodiversity: Megadiverse global treasure harboring the world's second-largest rainforest, endemic species including the Okapi, Bonobo chimpanzee, Grauer's gorilla, and Mountain gorilla in Virunga National Park.
economy: Sectors: Mining & Industry 43%, Services 36%, Agriculture 21%. Key industries: Copper and cobalt extraction and smelting (Kolwezi, Tenke Fungurume, Kamoa-Kakula), Diamond mining, Gold and coltan extraction, Cement manufacturing, Beverage brewing (Bralima). Natural resources: Cobalt (produces over 70% of world supply), Copper (world's second largest producer), Coltan / Tantalum, Diamonds, Gold, Lithium (Manono), Timber, Vast hydropower (Inga Dam). Major exports: Refined copper and cathodes, Cobalt hydroxide, Gold, Crude petroleum, Diamonds, Coltan.
culture: Cuisine: Moambé chicken (poulet à la moambé: chicken simmered in rich palm nut butter sauce), Fufu (cassava or corn paste), Pondu (stewed cassava leaves with garlic and fish), Liboke de poisson (fish steamed in marantaceae leaves), Makayabu (salted cod), Mikate (fried dough balls).. Music & Dance: Congolese Rumba (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage; Franco Luambo, Tabu Ley Rochereau, Papa Wemba, Koffi Olomide, Fally Ipupa, Innoss'B), Soukous, Ndombolo.. Sports: Football (TP Mazembe: 5-time CAF Champions League winners; Leopards: 2-time AFCON champions), Basketball (Dikembe Mutombo, NBA Hall of Famer and humanitarian; Jonathan Kuminga, Bismack Biyombo).. Festivals: Independence Day (June 30), Amani Music Festival (Goma), Festival International des Étoiles (Kinshasa).
sources: National Statistical Office of DR Congo

name: Republic of the Congo
highestPoint: Mont Nabeba (1,020 m)
longestRiver: Congo River / Ubangi River / Kouilou-Niari River
climate: Equatorial with high temperatures and high humidity; two rainy seasons (March–June, September–November); dry season from June to August
naturalHazards: Seasonal riverine flooding
Mudslides in coastal hills during intense rainfall
environmentalIssues: Coastal marine pollution near oil terminals
biodiversity: Odzala-Kokoua National Park (UNESCO site with highest density of western lowland gorillas), and the pristine peatlands of the Cuvette Centrale
latestElections: Presidential election 2021 (Denis Sassou Nguesso re-elected); legislative elections 2022; next presidential election scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Stable governance under President Denis Sassou Nguesso; global leadership in tropical peatland and Congo Basin forest conservation diplomacy (Three Basins Summit).
foreignRelations: Member of CEMAC, ECCAS, African Union, Francophonie, OPEC, UN; close economic ties with France, China, and regional Central African neighbors.
military: Congolese Armed Forces (FAC) comprising Ground Forces, Navy, Air Force, and Gendarmerie.
adminDivisions: 12 departments
history: Inhabited by Pygmy hunter-gatherers followed by Bantu peoples who founded the Kingdom of Loango, Kingdom of Kongo, and Anziku (Téké) Kingdom. Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza explored the area and concluded a treaty with King Makoko of the Téké in 1880, bringing the region under French protection as Middle Congo (Moyen-Congo), with Brazzaville later serving as the historic capital of Free France under Charles de Gaulle during WWII. Independence achieved in 1960 under Fulbert Youlou. Declared a Marxist-Leninist People's Republic under Marien Ngouabi in 1969. Multi-party democracy introduced in 1992, followed by civil conflict before Denis Sassou Nguesso consolidated power.
recentEvents2020_2026: Hosted the landmark Three Basins Summit in Brazzaville in 2023 for global rainforest preservation; inaugurated the expanded offshore Marine XII LNG export terminal; modernized Pointe-Noire deepwater commercial port.
education: Marien Ngouabi University (Brazzaville); Denis Sassou-Nguesso University in Kintélé; high secondary school enrollment relative to regional peers.
healthcare: Brazzaville University Hospital (CHU); expanding network of general hospitals in departmental capitals.
socialCustoms: La Sape (originating along the Brazzaville riverfront as a supreme expression of gentility, style, and peace), Sunday family river outings, communal palm wine tastings.
etiquette: Courteous French greeting with handshake, addressing elders respectfully, dressing smartly for social meetings.
nationalIdentity: Defined by Brazzaville's history as the capital of Free France, the intellectual flair of its writers, the elegance of the Sapeurs, and the majestic sweep of the Congo River.
energy: Gas-fired thermal plants in Pointe-Noire (CEC) and Imboulou and Moukoukoulou hydroelectric dams supplying national grid
tourism: Premier ecotourism centered on Odzala-Kokoua National Park (breathtaking bai forest clearings with western lowland gorillas), the Loufoulakari Falls, and the lively cultural life of Brazzaville.
employment: Petroleum services, civil service, commercial forestry, transport and port logistics.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic restructuring supported by IMF Extended Credit Facility and regional BEAC monetary controls.
transport: Congo-Ocean Railway (CFCO) connecting Brazzaville to the ocean port of Pointe-Noire; modern asphalt national highways.
ports: Autonomous Port of Pointe-Noire (premier deepwater container hub in Central Africa)
cuisine: Saka-Saka (pounded cassava leaves cooked with smoked fish, palm oil, and peanut paste), Maboké (spiced river fish steamed in plantain leaves), Poulet à la Moambé, Grilled tilapia from the Congo River, Bouillon de poisson, Kwanga (fermented cassava bread).
festivals: Feux de Brazza traditional music festival
music: Congolese Rumba, Soukous, Afro-zouk; historic musicians like Pamélo Mounka, Youlou Mabiala, Les Bantous de la Capitale.
dance: Rumba dance, Soukous, Mutuashi, traditional Téké ritual dances.
art: Poto-Poto School of Painting (iconic modern African art movement founded in Brazzaville in 1951), carved wooden sculptures.
architecture: Basilique Sainte-Anne du Congo (architectural masterpiece with emerald ceramic tile roof in Brazzaville); colonial French villas; modern Nabemba Tower.
literature: One of Africa's most brilliant literary traditions: Alain Mabanckou (Verre Cassé, Memoires de porc-épic), Tchicaya U Tam'si, Emmanuel Dongala, Henri Lopes.
cinema: Sébastien Kamba, emerging filmmakers presented at the Brazzaville International Film Festival.
sports: Football (Red Devils / Diables Rouges, 1972 AFCON champions), Handball (women's team continental champions), Basketball.
media: Les Dépêches de Brazzaville, Télé Congo, Vox Congo.
clothing: La Sape (Société des Ambianceurs et des Personnes Élégantes: world-famous gentleman dandies in exquisite bespoke European suits); colorful Pagne wax skirts.
crafts: Poto-Poto canvas paintings, woven raffia mats, carved mahogany figures, musical instruments.
unescoIntangible: Congolese Rumba (shared with DRC)
flagDescription: A diagonal yellow band extending from the lower hoist side to the upper fly side, dividing the flag into a green triangle (upper hoist) and a red triangle (lower fly) in the Pan-African colors.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a gold shield with a red lion rampant holding a torch, against a green wavy bar, supported by two African forest elephants, crowned with a forest coronet and the motto 'Unité, Travail, Progrès'.
travelNotes: Brazzaville is one of Central Africa's most relaxed and culturally sophisticated river capitals; Pointe-Noire offers ocean dining and Atlantic surf; pristine wilderness safaris in the north.
shortSummary: The Republic of the Congo, graced by the tranquil bank of the mighty Congo River opposite Kinshasa, is renowned for the literary elegance of Brazzaville, the world-famous Sapeur sartorial subculture, and the untouched western lowland gorilla sanctuaries of Odzala-Kokoua.
geography: Highest point: Mont Nabeba (1,020 m). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Congo River / Ubangi River / Kouilou-Niari River. Climate: Equatorial with high temperatures and high humidity; two rainy seasons (March–June, September–November); dry season from June to August. Biodiversity: Odzala-Kokoua National Park (UNESCO site with highest density of western lowland gorillas), and the pristine peatlands of the Cuvette Centrale.
economy: Sectors: Petroleum & Industry 50%, Services 42%, Agriculture 8%. Key industries: Offshore crude petroleum extraction, Liquefied natural gas (Congo LNG), Commercial timber and plywood processing, Cement production, Potash and phosphate exploration. Natural resources: Petroleum (leading export revenue), Natural gas, Timber (valuable tropical hardwoods), Potash, Iron ore (Mayoko), Hydropower. Major exports: Crude petroleum, Liquefied natural gas, Lumber and logs, Copper and mineral ores, Sugar.
culture: Cuisine: Saka-Saka (pounded cassava leaves cooked with smoked fish, palm oil, and peanut paste), Maboké (spiced river fish steamed in plantain leaves), Poulet à la Moambé, Grilled tilapia from the Congo River, Bouillon de poisson, Kwanga (fermented cassava bread).. Music & Dance: Congolese Rumba, Soukous, Afro-zouk; historic musicians like Pamélo Mounka, Youlou Mabiala, Les Bantous de la Capitale.. Sports: Football (Red Devils / Diables Rouges, 1972 AFCON champions), Handball (women's team continental champions), Basketball.. Festivals: Pan-African Music Festival (FESPAM in Brazzaville), Independence Day (August 15), Feux de Brazza traditional music festival.
sources: National Statistical Office of Republic of the Congo

name: Côte d'Ivoire
highestPoint: Mount Nimba (1,752 m)
lowestPoint: Gulf of Guinea / Atlantic Ocean (0 m)
longestRiver: Bandama River (1,050 km)
climate: Warm and humid tropical along coast with two rainy seasons (May–July, October–November); semi-arid savanna in the north with winter Harmattan winds
naturalHazards: Torrential coastal rains causing urban flooding in Abidjan
Harmattan dust haze
Coastal erosion
environmentalIssues: Deforestation due to cocoa farming expansion
biodiversity: Taï National Park preserving the last primary tropical rainforest in West Africa (home to pygmy hippos and nut-cracking chimpanzees) and Comoé National Park
mainPoliticalParties: Rally of Houphouëtists for Democracy and Peace (RHDP)
latestElections: Presidential election 2020; legislative/local elections 2023; next presidential election scheduled October 2025/2026
politicalSituation: West Africa's economic locomotive experiencing over a decade of sustained 6–7% annual GDP growth under President Alassane Ouattara; massive infrastructure expansion across Abidjan and interior corridors.
foreignRelations: Leading economy in ECOWAS and UEMOA; headquarters host of the African Development Bank (AfDB) in Abidjan; close diplomatic and economic alliances with France, US, China, and EU.
military: Armed Forces of Côte d'Ivoire (FACI).
adminDivisions: 12 districts and 2 autonomous districts (Abidjan and Yamoussoukro)
history: Inhabited by diverse kingdoms including the Baoulé Kingdom (founded by Queen Abla Pokou in the 18th century), the Senufo kingdoms, and the Kong Empire. French colony established in 1893 after fierce resistance from Samori Ture. Félix Houphouët-Boigny led the anti-colonial agricultural union and governed as founding president for 33 years following independence in 1960, creating the prosperous 'Ivorian Miracle' through cocoa and coffee exports. Following his death in 1993, political instability and a civil conflict divided the nation between 2002 and 2011. Since 2011, dramatic economic resurgence and reconciliation have transformed the country.
recentEvents2020_2026: Triumphantly hosted and won the 2023/2024 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) in Abidjan; completed the monumental Cocody Bay suspension bridge; expanded local cocoa grinding capacity making Côte d'Ivoire the world's leading cocoa processor; inaugurated the massive offshore Baleine and Calao deepwater oil and gas fields.
education: Félix Houphouët-Boigny University (Cocody, Abidjan); Nangui Abrogoua University; INP-HB in Yamoussoukro (premier engineering polytechnic in Francophone Africa).
healthcare: Modernized public hospital network including new regional hospital centers in Bouaké and San-Pédro; universal health coverage (CMU) expansion.
socialCustoms: Maquis outdoor open-air restaurant culture, vibrant Nouchi urban slang, evening Zouglou gatherings, respect for traditional elders and chieftains.
etiquette: Warm handshakes, greeting everyone in a room, polite inquiries about family, generous hospitality (Akwaba).
nationalIdentity: Defined by Akwaba (the spirit of welcome), unmatched football pride (The Elephants), Zouglou and Coupé-Décalé musical dominance, and economic dynamism.
industries: Cocoa grinding and chocolate paste processing (world #1)
agriculture: Cocoa (world's largest producer, over 40% of global supply)
energy: Regional electricity exporter via West African Power Pool; gas-fired thermal plants (Azito, CIPREL) and Soubré hydroelectric dam
exports: Cocoa beans and processed cocoa products
tourism: Cultural and leisure tourism: the monumental Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in Yamoussoukro (world's largest church), colonial French town of Grand-Bassam, hiking Mount Tonkoui in Man, and surfing at Assinie.
employment: Cocoa and agricultural value chains, port logistics, financial services, commerce.
debtInflation: Strong macroeconomic standing with investment-grade sovereign eurobond issues and UEMOA monetary stability.
transport: Abidjan-Ouagadougou railway (Sitarail); modern four-lane toll motorway network connecting Abidjan to Yamoussoukro, Bouaké, and Grand-Bassam; Abidjan Metro project.
airports: Félix Houphouët-Boigny International Airport (ABJ in Abidjan)
ports: Autonomous Port of Abidjan (second largest container port in Africa)
Port of San-Pédro (world's premier cocoa export port)
cuisine: Attiéké (steamed fermented grated cassava couscous, UNESCO intangible nominee), Garba (attiéké with crispy fried seasoned tuna and fresh chili/onions), Alloco (fried ripe sweet plantains), Kedjenou (slow-cooked chicken or guinea fowl stewed in a sealed earthen pot with vegetables), Sauce graine (palm nut soup), Foutou banane with peanut sauce.
music: Zouglou (philosophical urban folk rhythm: Magic System), Coupé-Décalé (high-energy percussion dance pioneered by Douk Saga and DJ Arafat), Ziglibithy (Ernesto Djédjé), Mandingue.
dance: Coupé-Décalé, Zouglou dance, Zaouli mask dance (UNESCO masterpiece), Mapouka.
art: Senufo carved wooden Hornbill bird sculptures and Korhogo painted canvas cloth, Baoulé gold-leaf portrait masks, Guro Zaouli masks.
architecture: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace (Yamoussoukro, world's largest church building); modern high-rises of Le Plateau ('Manhattan of West Africa'); colonial seaside architecture of Grand-Bassam; Sudano-Sahelian earthen mosques of northern Côte d'Ivoire.
literature: Ahmadou Kourouma (Les Soleils des indépendances, Allah n'est pas obligé), Bernard Dadié, Véronique Tadjo, Gauz (Debout-payé).
cinema: Fadika Kramo-Lanciné, Henri Duparc (Bal Poussière), Philippe Lacôte (Night of the Kings / La Nuit des Rois).
sports: Football: The Elephants (Les Éléphants: 3-time AFCON Champions: 1992, 2015, 2023/2024; global legends Didier Drogba, Yaya Touré, Kolo Touré), Taekwondo (Cheick Sallah Cissé Olympic Gold Medalist), Athletics (Marie-Josée Ta Lou-Smith).
media: Fraternité Matin, RTI (Radiodiffusion Télévision Ivoirienne), Life TV, NCI (Nouvelle Chaîne Ivoirienne).
clothing: Kente-like Kita / Kente Baoulé handwoven royal cloth; vibrant wax print shirts; modern Parisian-Abidjan street fashion.
crafts: Korhogo painted cotton tapestries, Senufo wooden stools, Baoulé brass weight figurines, handwoven Kita fabric.
worldHeritageSites: Sudanese style mosques in northern Côte d'Ivoire (inscribed 2021)
unescoIntangible: Zaouli, popular music and dance of the Guro communities (inscribed 2017)
flagDescription: Three equal vertical bands of orange (savanna of the north and national growth), white (peace, unity, and purity), and green (coastal southern forests and hope for the future).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features an elephant head centered on a green shield, flanked by two silver palm trees, topped by a rising sun over a gold banner inscribed 'République de Côte d'Ivoire'.
landmarks: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace (Yamoussoukro)
travelNotes: Abidjan is one of Africa's most vibrant and stylish cultural metropolises with world-class dining, arts, and nightlife; hospitable and warm (Akwaba).
shortSummary: Côte d'Ivoire is the booming economic and cultural powerhouse of Francophone West Africa, famed worldwide as the top producer of cocoa, host and champion of the Africa Cup of Nations, home to the colossal Yamoussoukro Basilica, and creator of the infectious Coupé-Décalé and Zouglou dance beats.
geography: Highest point: Mount Nimba (1,752 m). Lowest point: Gulf of Guinea / Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Bandama River (1,050 km). Climate: Warm and humid tropical along coast with two rainy seasons (May–July, October–November); semi-arid savanna in the north with winter Harmattan winds. Biodiversity: Taï National Park preserving the last primary tropical rainforest in West Africa (home to pygmy hippos and nut-cracking chimpanzees) and Comoé National Park.
economy: Sectors: Services 48%, Agriculture 28%, Industry 24%. Key industries: Cocoa grinding and chocolate paste processing (world #1), Petroleum refining (SIR in Abidjan), Cashew processing, Food processing and palm oil, Textiles and construction materials. Natural resources: Cocoa and arable soils, Petroleum and natural gas (Baleine field), Gold, Manganese, Bauxite, Diamonds. Major exports: Cocoa beans and processed cocoa products, Raw cashew nuts, Refined petroleum products, Natural rubber, Gold, Crude petroleum.
culture: Cuisine: Attiéké (steamed fermented grated cassava couscous, UNESCO intangible nominee), Garba (attiéké with crispy fried seasoned tuna and fresh chili/onions), Alloco (fried ripe sweet plantains), Kedjenou (slow-cooked chicken or guinea fowl stewed in a sealed earthen pot with vegetables), Sauce graine (palm nut soup), Foutou banane with peanut sauce.. Music & Dance: Zouglou (philosophical urban folk rhythm: Magic System), Coupé-Décalé (high-energy percussion dance pioneered by Douk Saga and DJ Arafat), Ziglibithy (Ernesto Djédjé), Mandingue.. Sports: Football: The Elephants (Les Éléphants: 3-time AFCON Champions: 1992, 2015, 2023/2024; global legends Didier Drogba, Yaya Touré, Kolo Touré), Taekwondo (Cheick Sallah Cissé Olympic Gold Medalist), Athletics (Marie-Josée Ta Lou-Smith).. Festivals: FEMUA (Festival des Musiques Urbaines d'Anoumabo), Popo Carnaval de Bonoua, Carnaval de Bouaké, Abissa festival in Grand-Bassam.
sources: National Statistical Office of Côte d'Ivoire

name: Djibouti
nativeName: République de Djibouti / جمهورية جيبوتي / Jamhuuriyadda Jabuuti
highestPoint: Mousa Ali (2,028 m tripoint volcano)
lowestPoint: Lake Assal (-155 m, lowest point in Africa)
longestRiver: Seasonal wadis (no permanent perennial rivers)
majorLakes: Lake Assal (world's second saltiest body of water)
Lake Abbe (salt lake with otherworldly limestone chimneys)
climate: Torrid, hyper-arid desert climate with scorching summer temperatures exceeding 42°C; milder coastal winters
naturalHazards: Earthquakes along the Afar Triple Junction
Extreme prolonged droughts
Occasional destructive flash floods along dry wadis
environmentalIssues: Marine ecosystem protection in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait
biodiversity: Day Forest National Park (ancient remnant of juniper forest in the Goda Mountains), whale shark (Rhincodon typus) aggregations in the Gulf of Tadjoura
currency: Djiboutian Franc (DJF, Fdj, pegged to US Dollar)
mainPoliticalParties: Union for the Presidential Majority (UMP / RPP)
latestElections: Presidential election 2021; legislative elections 2023; next presidential election scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Strategic maritime and geopolitical hub at the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway connecting the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean; host to multiple foreign military facilities (US Camp Lemonnier, French, Chinese, Japanese, Italian bases).
foreignRelations: Member of IGAD (headquarters host in Djibouti City), Arab League, African Union, OIC, Francophonie, UN; vital economic lifeblood as Ethiopia's primary maritime gateway.
military: Djibouti Armed Forces (FAD).
adminDivisions: 6 regions (including Djibouti City)
history: Inhabited by pastoralist Somali (Issa) and Afar clans, part of the Sultanate of Ifat and Adal Sultanate during the medieval era. France acquired Obock in 1862 and established French Somaliland, later renamed the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas in 1967. Achieved independence in 1977 under Hassan Gouled Aptidon. Civil conflict in the 1990s between the government and the Afar FRUD movement was resolved by peace agreements. Transformed into an ultra-modern maritime transshipment and global military logistics hub in the 21st century.
recentEvents2020_2026: Expanded the multi-billion-dollar Doraleh Multi-Purpose Port and Damerjog Industrial Park; strengthened electrified standard-gauge railway traffic to Addis Ababa; hosted summit diplomacy as chair of IGAD navigating Red Sea and Horn of Africa regional security.
historicalFigures: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (historic Adal leader)
education: University of Djibouti (established 2006); specialized maritime, logistics, and port management training institutes.
healthcare: Peltier General Hospital in Djibouti City; Cheiko regional military/civilian hospital; medical cooperation with France and Cuba.
socialCustoms: Afternoon Khat chew sessions (Maqhi), oral poetry recitations (Gabaan and Afar folklore), warm seaside evening gatherings.
etiquette: Islamic greetings (As-salamu alaykum), respectful handshakes among same gender, modest attire respecting Islamic traditions.
nationalIdentity: Shared Somali and Afar pastoralist heritage, Islamic faith, pride in geopolitical status as the Horn of Africa's indispensable maritime sentinel.
sectors: Port Services & Logistics 78%, Industry 18%, Agriculture & Fishing 4%
industries: Deepwater port operations and container transshipment
agriculture: Artisanal fishing in Gulf of Tadjoura
energy: Interconnected via cross-border transmission line to Ethiopian hydropower; developing Ghoubet wind farm (60MW) and Lake Assal geothermal plant
exports: Live animals (sheep, camels, cattle to Gulf states)
tourism: Extreme adventure and marine tourism: swimming with docile whale sharks in the Gulf of Tadjoura, visiting the lunar landscape of Lake Abbe chimneys, and exploring the hyper-saline salt crusts of Lake Assal.
employment: Port handling, free trade zones, international military support services, civil service.
debtInflation: Currency rigidly pegged to the US Dollar since 1949 (177.721 DJF per USD) providing rock-solid monetary stability and low inflation.
transport: Ethio-Djibouti electrified standard gauge railway (SGR); Port of Doraleh and Damerjog; international Red Sea maritime corridors.
cuisine: Skoudehkaris (fragrant spiced rice with slow-braised lamb, cardamoms, and cloves), Fah-fah (aromatic goat meat soup), Mukbaza (mashed flatbread with honey and banana), Canjeero / Lahoh flatbread, Sabaayad, Spiced Somali tea with cardamom and cloves.
music: Traditional Somali and Afar string and oud melodies, Qaraami ballads, modern stars like Awaleh Aden and Nima Djama.
dance: Afar warrior dance (Saab), Dhaanto folk dance, Zeili dance.
art: Woven palm leaf baskets (Afar and Somali), ornamental silver dagger sheaths (Gile dagger), beadwork.
architecture: French colonial arcaded buildings and Arab-Ottoman whitewashed houses in the historic quarters of Djibouti City and Tadjoura (the 'White City').
literature: Abdourahman Waberi (Transit, In the United States of Africa), Mouna-Hodan Ahmed; rich tradition of Somali oral poetry.
cinema: Lula Ali Ismaïl (Dhalinyaro, first feature film directed by a Djiboutian woman).
sports: Athletics (Hussein Ahmed Salah 1988 Olympic Marathon Bronze Medalist, Ayanleh Souleiman 1500m World Indoor Champion), Football (Riverains de la Mer Rouge).
media: La Nation (official newspaper), RTD (Radio Télévision de Djibouti).
clothing: Macawiis (sarong) worn with light shirt by men; Dirac flowing colorful chiffon dress worn by women with Garbasaar shawl.
crafts: Afar Gile curved daggers, handwoven palm mats, incense burners (Mabkhara), leather sand sandals.
worldHeritageSites: Lake Assal / Lake Abbe Cultural Landscape (Tentative List)
unescoIntangible: Oral traditions and performing arts of Afar and Somali communities
flagDescription: Two equal horizontal bands of light blue (Somali Issa and clear sky) and light green (Afar and lush earth), with a white isosceles triangle based on the hoist side bearing a red five-pointed star (unity).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a traditional spear behind a round shield, flanked by two hands each holding a traditional Afar dagger, encircled by laurel branches and surmounted by a red star.
travelNotes: Safe, stable, and strategically vibrant; exceptional scuba diving and whale shark encounters; intense summer heat makes November–March the ideal travel window.
shortSummary: Djibouti is the vital geopolitical sentinel of the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, where hyper-saline wonders like Lake Assal meet the surreal limestone chimneys of Lake Abbe and calm ocean bays teeming with whale sharks.
geography: Highest point: Mousa Ali (2,028 m tripoint volcano). Lowest point: Lake Assal (-155 m, lowest point in Africa). Longest river: Seasonal wadis (no permanent perennial rivers). Climate: Torrid, hyper-arid desert climate with scorching summer temperatures exceeding 42°C; milder coastal winters. Biodiversity: Day Forest National Park (ancient remnant of juniper forest in the Goda Mountains), whale shark (Rhincodon typus) aggregations in the Gulf of Tadjoura.
economy: Sectors: Port Services & Logistics 78%, Industry 18%, Agriculture & Fishing 4%. Key industries: Deepwater port operations and container transshipment, Free trade zone logistics (DIFTZ), Ship bunkering and ship repair, Livestock transit logistics, Telecommunications cable landings. Natural resources: Strategic geographical location, Geothermal energy potential (Lake Assal), Salt and gypsum, Marine fisheries. Major exports: Re-exports and transit cargo, Live animals (sheep, camels, cattle to Gulf states), Salt, Scrap metals.
culture: Cuisine: Skoudehkaris (fragrant spiced rice with slow-braised lamb, cardamoms, and cloves), Fah-fah (aromatic goat meat soup), Mukbaza (mashed flatbread with honey and banana), Canjeero / Lahoh flatbread, Sabaayad, Spiced Somali tea with cardamom and cloves.. Music & Dance: Traditional Somali and Afar string and oud melodies, Qaraami ballads, modern stars like Awaleh Aden and Nima Djama.. Sports: Athletics (Hussein Ahmed Salah 1988 Olympic Marathon Bronze Medalist, Ayanleh Souleiman 1500m World Indoor Champion), Football (Riverains de la Mer Rouge).. Festivals: Independence Day (June 27), Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Islamic New Year, Fest'Horn music festival.

name: Egypt
nationalAnthem: Bilady, Bilady, Bilady (My Homeland, My Homeland, My Homeland)
motto: None (De facto: أم الدنيا / Mother of the World)
populationDensity: 114.2 / km² (over 1,500/km² in the inhabited Nile Valley/Delta)
highestPoint: Mount Catherine / Gabal Katrîna (2,629 m in Sinai)
longestRiver: Nile River (6,650 km total course, Egypt's historic lifeline)
climate: Arid desert with very hot dry summers and mild winters; Mediterranean breeze along Alexandria and northern coast
naturalHazards: Periodic flash floods in Sinai and Upper Egypt wadis
Khamsin dust storms in spring
Seismic tremors
environmentalIssues: Nile water security related to GERD upstream
Agricultural land loss from urban sprawl in the Delta
Rising sea levels threatening Alexandria and coastal lagoons
biodiversity: Ras Mohammed National Park and Red Sea coral reef barrier; Wadi El Rayan; migratory bird corridors along the Nile flyway
latestElections: Presidential election December 2023 (Abdel Fattah el-Sisi re-elected for a third term); House of Representatives elections scheduled 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Massive state-led infrastructure programs centered on the New Administrative Capital (NAC), Suez Canal Economic Zone, Ras El Hekma coastal development, and high-speed passenger rail networks.
foreignRelations: Pivotal Middle Eastern and African diplomatic power; custodian of the Suez Canal; key mediator in Arab-Israeli diplomacy and African Union affairs; joined BRICS in 2024.
military: Egyptian Armed Forces (largest military power in Africa and the Arab world).
adminDivisions: 27 governorates (muhafazat)
history: One of the cradles of human civilization, unified c. 3100 BC by Pharaoh Narmer. Built monumental pyramids, Karnak temple complexes, and the Valley of the Kings across Old, Middle, and New Kingdoms. Conquered by Alexander the Great in 332 BC, leading to the Ptolemaic Dynasty and Cleopatra VII. Incorporated into the Roman and Byzantine Empires; Christianized with the Coptic Orthodox Church founded by Saint Mark. Arab-Muslim conquest in 641 AD transformed Egypt into the heart of Fatimid, Ayyubid (Saladin), and Mamluk empires. Ottoman rule began in 1517. Muhammad Ali Pasha established the modern Egyptian state in the 19th century. British occupied in 1882; nominally independent kingdom declared in 1922. The 1952 Free Officers Revolution led by Gamal Abdel Nasser established the republic, nationalized the Suez Canal, and championed Pan-Arabism. Succeeded by Anwar Sadat (1979 Camp David Accords) and Hosni Mubarak. Historic 2011 revolution led to subsequent constitutional reshaping under Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.
recentEvents2020_2026: Hosted UN COP27 Climate Summit in Sharm El-Sheikh; inaugurated the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) at Giza; formally joined BRICS in 2024; executed the historic $35 billion Ras El Hekma investment deal; relocated central government ministries to the New Administrative Capital.
ethnicGroups: Nubians, Berbers (Siwa), Bedouins, and refugees (Sudanese, Syrian) ~0.3%
education: Al-Azhar University (founded 970 AD, premier global institution of Islamic scholarship); Cairo University; American University in Cairo; Egypt-Japan University.
healthcare: Universal Health Insurance System (UHIS) rollout; world-renowned '100 Million Healthy Lives' campaign successfully eliminating Hepatitis C.
socialCustoms: Deeply ingrained humor (nukta), evening café Ahwa culture, Ramadan lantern (Fanous) celebrations, family banquets, generosity (karam).
etiquette: Warm greetings with handshakes and inquiries after family, removing shoes before entering homes, respecting religious fasts.
nationalIdentity: Proud multi-millennial continuity as 'Umm al-Dunya' (Mother of the World), Arab cultural and cinematic primacy, and the enduring eternal Nile.
industries: Petroleum and natural gas extraction (Zohr offshore gas field)
energy: Rapid expansion into green hydrogen, Benban Solar Park (one of world's largest solar complexes), Gabal El Zeit wind farm, and El Dabaa nuclear power plant
imports: Wheat and grains (world's top wheat buyer)
tourism: World-leading cultural and resort tourism exceeding 15 million annual visitors: Pyramids of Giza, Grand Egyptian Museum, Luxor Karnak & Valley of the Kings, Nile river cruises, Red Sea diving at Sharm El-Sheikh and Hurghada.
employment: Civil administration, agriculture, tourism and hospitality, retail, manufacturing, military enterprises.
debtInflation: Monetary float and stabilization backed by expanded IMF financing, GCC direct investment, and sovereign bond issuances.
transport: Suez Canal (vital global maritime choke-point handling 12% of world trade); Cairo Metro (first underground metro in Africa); high-speed electric rail network under construction linking the Red Sea to the Mediterranean.
cuisine: Koshary (iconic national comfort dish of lentils, rice, macaroni, spiced tomato sauce, garlic vinegar, and crispy fried onions), Ful Medames (slow-simmered fava beans with olive oil and cumin), Ta'ameya (Egyptian fava bean falafel), Molokhia (garlic-coriander jute leaf soup served with rabbit or chicken), Hawawshi, Mahshi, Umm Ali dessert, Om Ali, Hibiscus Karkadeh.
music: The musical capital of the Arab world: Classical Tarab (Umm Kulthum 'Star of the East', Abdel Halim Hafez, Mohammed Abdel Wahab), Shaabi street music, modern Mahraganat electro-folk.
dance: Raqs Sharqi (classical belly dance), Tanoura Sufi whirling dervish dance, Tahtib stick martial dance (UNESCO heritage).
art: Pharaonic frescoes, Coptic Christian iconography, Islamic geometric wood and brass inlay, contemporary art at Townhouse Gallery.
architecture: Pyramids and hypostyle halls of ancient Egypt; Islamic Cairo's medieval minarets and madrasas (Al-Azhar, Sultan Hassan); Beaux-Arts downtown Cairo; cutting-edge New Administrative Capital Iconic Tower.
literature: Naguib Mahfouz (Nobel Prize in Literature 1988, Cairo Trilogy), Taha Hussein, Nawal El Saadawi, Alaa Al Aswany (The Yacoubian Building).
cinema: The 'Hollywood of the Middle East': Youssef Chahine (Cairo Station, Destiny), Salah Abu Seif, Omar Sharif, Faten Hamama, Adel Imam.
sports: Football: The Pharaohs (record 7-time AFCON champions; Mohamed Salah, global Liverpool icon), Al Ahly SC (most decorated football club in world history, CAF Champions League record holders), Squash (world #1 dominant champions: Ali Farag, Nour El Sherbini).
media: Al-Ahram (founded 1875), Al-Masry Al-Youm, Egyptian Radio and Television Union (ERTU), DMC, ON TV.
clothing: Traditional Galabeya robe worn across rural Upper Egypt; contemporary modern fashion in Cairo and Alexandria.
crafts: Khan el-Khalili brass lanterns, mother-of-pearl inlaid woodwork, hand-blown Muski glass, alabaster carvings from Luxor.
worldHeritageSites: Memphis and its Necropolis – the Pyramid Fields from Giza to Dahshur
Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae
unescoIntangible: Tahtib, stick game
Al-Sirah Al-Hilaliyyah epic poetry
Handmade weaving in Upper Egypt (Sa'eed)
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of red (sacrifices of the revolution), white (purity of the Egyptian soul), and black (dark period of foreign oppression), with the golden Eagle of Saladin centered in the white band.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features the golden Eagle of Saladin bearing a shield with vertical bands of the national colors, clutching a scroll inscribed 'جمهورية مصر العربية' (Arab Republic of Egypt).
landmarks: Great Pyramids of Giza and Sphinx
Karnak Temple and Valley of the Kings (Luxor)
travelNotes: Iconic, hospitable travel destination; outstanding rail and domestic air connectivity; hire licensed Egyptologists for temple explorations; Red Sea provides premier year-round reef diving.
shortSummary: Egypt is the eternal cradle of civilization, uniting seven thousand years of Pharaonic monuments, the majestic Grand Egyptian Museum, the pulsating cultural heartbeat of Cairo, and the world's most vital maritime artery at the Suez Canal.
geography: Highest point: Mount Catherine / Gabal Katrîna (2,629 m in Sinai). Lowest point: Qattara Depression (-133 m). Longest river: Nile River (6,650 km total course, Egypt's historic lifeline). Climate: Arid desert with very hot dry summers and mild winters; Mediterranean breeze along Alexandria and northern coast. Biodiversity: Ras Mohammed National Park and Red Sea coral reef barrier; Wadi El Rayan; migratory bird corridors along the Nile flyway.
economy: Sectors: Services 53%, Industry & Manufacturing 33%, Agriculture 14%. Key industries: Petroleum and natural gas extraction (Zohr offshore gas field), Suez Canal transit tolls, Textiles and Egyptian long-staple cotton, Chemicals and fertilizers, Automotive and machinery assembly, Pharmaceuticals, Construction. Natural resources: Natural gas (Zohr), Petroleum, Phosphates, Iron ore, Gold (Sukari mine), Limestone, Arable Nile silt. Major exports: Natural gas and LNG, Refined petroleum, Citrus and fresh produce, Fertilizers and chemicals, Textiles and garments, Gold.
culture: Cuisine: Koshary (iconic national comfort dish of lentils, rice, macaroni, spiced tomato sauce, garlic vinegar, and crispy fried onions), Ful Medames (slow-simmered fava beans with olive oil and cumin), Ta'ameya (Egyptian fava bean falafel), Molokhia (garlic-coriander jute leaf soup served with rabbit or chicken), Hawawshi, Mahshi, Umm Ali dessert, Om Ali, Hibiscus Karkadeh.. Music & Dance: The musical capital of the Arab world: Classical Tarab (Umm Kulthum 'Star of the East', Abdel Halim Hafez, Mohammed Abdel Wahab), Shaabi street music, modern Mahraganat electro-folk.. Sports: Football: The Pharaohs (record 7-time AFCON champions; Mohamed Salah, global Liverpool icon), Al Ahly SC (most decorated football club in world history, CAF Champions League record holders), Squash (world #1 dominant champions: Ali Farag, Nour El Sherbini).. Festivals: Sham El-Nessim (ancient Pharaonic spring festival), Cairo International Film Festival, Moulid of Sayyid Ahmad al-Badawi (Tanta), Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha.

name: Equatorial Guinea
nativeName: República de Guinea Ecuatorial / République de Guinée équatoriale / República da Guiné Equatorial
capital: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz / Oyala (future administrative capital)
nationalAnthem: Caminemos pisando la senda (Let Us Walk Treading the Path)
highestPoint: Pico Basile on Bioko Island (3,011 m volcanic peak)
longestRiver: Mbini / Benito River (338 km)
majorLakes: Lake Biao (volcanic crater lake on Bioko)
climate: Equatorial hot and humid with abundant year-round rainfall and heavy cloud cover; slightly drier from December to February
naturalHazards: Tropical squalls and coastal ocean surges
Volcanic activity risk on Pico Basile
environmentalIssues: Poaching of endangered primates in Monte Alén
biodiversity: Monte Alén National Park (pristine rainforest harboring mandrills, western lowland gorillas, and goliath frogs) and Bioko Island's rare drills and sea turtles
languages: Spanish (official, primary language of education and administration)
headOfState: President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo (longest-serving head of state in the world)
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister Manuel Osa Nsue Nsua
latestElections: General election November 2022 (Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo re-elected); next scheduled 2027
politicalSituation: Governed by President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo since 1979; ongoing construction of the planned futuristic inland capital Ciudad de la Paz (Oyala); efforts to attract international gas and logistics investments.
foreignRelations: The only Spanish-speaking nation in Africa; member of CEMAC, African Union, CPLP, OIF, OPEC, UN; close economic ties with US oil majors, China, and Spain.
military: Armed Forces of Equatorial Guinea (FAGE).
adminDivisions: 8 provinces (including Djibloho / Ciudad de la Paz)
history: Inhabited by the indigenous Bubi on Bioko Island and Fang peoples on the mainland (Río Muni). Portuguese explorer Fernão do Pó sighted Bioko in 1472. Ceded to Spain in 1778 under the Treaty of El Pardo, becoming Spanish Guinea. Gained independence in 1968 under Francisco Macías Nguema, whose reign of terror led to severe devastation. Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo ousted him in 1979. Discovery of the massive offshore Zafiro oilfield by Mobil in 1995 launched a colossal oil boom, transforming Equatorial Guinea into one of Africa's highest GDP per capita nations.
recentEvents2020_2026: Celebrated modern deepwater natural gas monetization via Punta Europa LNG megahub; expanded Ciudad de la Paz (Oyala) administrative complex; hosted regional CEMAC financial summits.
education: National University of Equatorial Guinea (UNGE); modern technical and petrochemical training colleges.
healthcare: La Paz Medical Centers in Malabo, Bata, and Sipopo (among the most modern medical facilities in Central Africa).
socialCustoms: Abira traditional purification ritual, communal village councils (Abaá), lively Spanish-African social gatherings.
etiquette: Formal Spanish courtesies (Buenos días, Don/Doña), firm handshakes, dressing smartly for administrative and business meetings.
nationalIdentity: Unique African-Hispanophone synthesis: Spanish language, Fang oral folklore (Mvet), colonial wooden cathedrals, and dramatic volcanic topography.
sectors: Petroleum & Gas 60%, Services 28%, Industry & Construction 8%, Agriculture 4%
industries: Liquefied natural gas (Punta Europa LNG facility)
energy: Gas-to-power generation at Punta Europa and Djibloho Hydroelectric Plant supplying the national grid
tourism: Ecotourism centered on trekking up Pico Basile, observing nesting green sea turtles at Ureka, hiking Monte Alén National Park, and visiting colonial Spanish architecture in Malabo.
employment: Oil sector contracting, public infrastructure construction, civil service, smallholder farming.
debtInflation: BEAC monetary integration using the Central African CFA Franc, managing fluctuating hydrocarbon fiscal revenues.
transport: Modern multi-lane toll highways across Bioko and the mainland; high-speed passenger ferries linking Malabo to Bata.
cuisine: Succotash, Sopa de Pescado con Pepe (spicy pepper fish soup), Bambucha (cassava leaf stew), Modika (thick wild mango seed sauce), Roasted plantains with grilled sea bass, Bilola (giant land snails in tomato-chili sauce).
music: Mvet harp poetry, Balele dance rhythms, modern Equatoguinean Afro-pop and Spanish hip-hop (Negro Bey, Piruchi Apo).
dance: Balele, Mokom, Ndongo, traditional Fang dance accompanied by drum and xylophone.
art: Fang wooden reliquary ancestor guardian figures (Eyema Byeri, which influenced European cubism and Picasso), carved wooden drums.
architecture: Spanish colonial wooden houses and Santa Isabel Cathedral in Malabo; futuristic modern conference cities at Sipopo and Ciudad de la Paz.
literature: Juan Tomás Ávila Laurel (By Night the Mountain Burns), María Nsué Angüe (Ekomo, first novel by an Equatoguinean woman), Donato Ndongo-Bidyogo.
cinema: Emerging documentary film movement; Malabo International Film Festival.
sports: Football (Nzalang Nacional / National Thunder: sensational quarter-finalists at 2012, 2015, 2021, and round-of-16 at 2024 AFCON tournaments; star Emilio Nsue Golden Boot winner 2024), Swimming (Eric Moussambani / 'Eric the Eel').
media: RTVGE (Radio Televisión Guinea Ecuatorial), La Gaceta de Guinea Ecuatorial.
clothing: Spanish-tailored formal suits for business; colorful wax print wraps (pagne) for community festivals.
crafts: Carved Fang reliquary statuettes, woven wicker baskets from Bioko, ceremonial masks.
worldHeritageSites: Monte Alén National Park and Pico Basile (Tentative List)
unescoIntangible: Oral and musical traditions of the Mvet epic of the Fang
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of green (natural resources and lush vegetation), white (peace and harmony), and red (blood shed for independence), with a blue triangle (sea linking mainland to islands) based on the hoist side, bearing the national coat of arms in the center.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a silver shield bearing a silk cotton tree (God tree / Ceiba), topped by six golden six-pointed stars representing the mainland and five islands, over a ribbon with the motto 'Unidad, Paz, Justicia'.
landmarks: Ureka Waterfalls and Sea Turtle Beach
travelNotes: A unique Spanish-speaking enclave in Africa; Malabo features manicured tropical parks and modern infrastructure; permits required for certain natural parks.
shortSummary: Equatorial Guinea is Africa's sole Spanish-speaking nation, a unique bridge between African heritage and Iberian culture, possessing offshore energy reserves, the volcanic peak of Pico Basile, and pristine primate rainforests in Monte Alén.
geography: Highest point: Pico Basile on Bioko Island (3,011 m volcanic peak). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Mbini / Benito River (338 km). Climate: Equatorial hot and humid with abundant year-round rainfall and heavy cloud cover; slightly drier from December to February. Biodiversity: Monte Alén National Park (pristine rainforest harboring mandrills, western lowland gorillas, and goliath frogs) and Bioko Island's rare drills and sea turtles.
economy: Sectors: Petroleum & Gas 60%, Services 28%, Industry & Construction 8%, Agriculture 4%. Key industries: Offshore petroleum extraction (Zafiro, Ceiba fields), Liquefied natural gas (Punta Europa LNG facility), Methanol production, Timber logging and sawmilling, Port construction and infrastructure. Natural resources: Petroleum, Natural gas, Timber, Gold, Diamond indications, Bauxite. Major exports: Crude petroleum, Liquefied natural gas (LNG), Methanol, Timber, Cocoa.
culture: Cuisine: Succotash, Sopa de Pescado con Pepe (spicy pepper fish soup), Bambucha (cassava leaf stew), Modika (thick wild mango seed sauce), Roasted plantains with grilled sea bass, Bilola (giant land snails in tomato-chili sauce).. Music & Dance: Mvet harp poetry, Balele dance rhythms, modern Equatoguinean Afro-pop and Spanish hip-hop (Negro Bey, Piruchi Apo).. Sports: Football (Nzalang Nacional / National Thunder: sensational quarter-finalists at 2012, 2015, 2021, and round-of-16 at 2024 AFCON tournaments; star Emilio Nsue Golden Boot winner 2024), Swimming (Eric Moussambani / 'Eric the Eel').. Festivals: Independence Day (October 12), President's Birthday (June 5), Malabo Hip Hop Festival, Fiesta de San Juan.
sources: National Statistical Office of Equatorial Guinea

name: Eritrea
motto: None (De facto: Awet n'Hafash / Victory to the Masses)
highestPoint: Emba Soira (3,018 m)
lowestPoint: Kulul within the Danakil Depression (-75 m)
longestRiver: Mereb (Gash) River (440 km) / Barka River
climate: Cool and temperate in central highlands (Asmara at 2,325m); scorching hot arid desert along the Red Sea coastal lowlands and Danakil Depression
naturalHazards: Frequent severe droughts
Desert locust swarms
Earthquakes in the Danakil rift zone
biodiversity: Dahlak Archipelago marine sanctuary with pristine coral reefs and dugongs; African wild ass (Equus africanus) in the northern Red Sea coastal desert
currency: Eritrean Nakfa (ERN, Nfk, pegged to USD)
mainPoliticalParties: People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ)
latestElections: Independence referendum 1993; formal national parliamentary elections pending
politicalSituation: Governed by President Isaias Afwerki since independence; focus on national self-reliance, military preparedness, and strategic port logistics along the Red Sea.
foreignRelations: Member of the African Union, UN, Arab League (observer); strategic Red Sea security partnerships with Gulf states, Russia, and China.
military: Eritrean Defence Forces (EDF).
adminDivisions: 6 regions (zobas)
history: Part of the ancient Kingdom of Aksum and the medieval maritime kingdom of Medri Bahri ('Land of the Sea') ruled by the Bahr Negus. Ottoman Turks conquered Massawa in 1557. Italy colonized the coastal territory in 1890, declaring it the colony of Eritrea ('Colonia Eritrea') and building Asmara into a modernist architectural jewel ('Piccola Roma'). British military administration governed from 1941 to 1952, after which the UN federated Eritrea with Ethiopia. Following Emperor Haile Selassie's annexation of Eritrea in 1962, a heroic 30-year armed war of independence led by the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF) culminated in victory in 1991 and overwhelming recognition of sovereignty in 1993.
recentEvents2020_2026: Rehabilitated Red Sea port infrastructure at Massawa and Assab; expanded the Colluli potash and Bisha gold-copper-zinc mining complexes; achieved historic global sports milestones with cyclist Biniam Girmay winning the Green Jersey at the Tour de France.
historicalFigures: Hamid Idris Awate (fired first shot of liberation struggle)
religions: Christianity (Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church, Catholic, Protestant) ~49%
education: Eritrea Institute of Technology (Mai Nefhi); College of Marine Sciences (Massawa); Orotta School of Medicine.
healthcare: Significant international recognition for achieving major declines in maternal mortality and malaria incidence through community health workers.
socialCustoms: Buna coffee ceremony with three rounds (Awel, Bereka, Dega) accompanied by frankincense and popcorn; community solidarity (Wefri).
etiquette: Warm handshakes with shoulder bumps among close friends, greeting elders with both hands, removing shoes when entering traditional homes.
nationalIdentity: Forged in the crucible of the 30-year liberation struggle, celebrated through self-reliance (Tsen'at), the modernist heritage of Asmara, and bicycling culture.
industries: Gold, copper, and zinc mining (Bisha mine, Zara mine)
energy: Expansion of off-grid solar-diesel hybrid plants across rural zobas and Hirgigo thermal power plant near Massawa
tourism: Architectural and cultural tourism: touring Asmara's UNESCO-listed modernist 1930s Art Deco architecture ('Africa's Modernist City'), Ottoman coral stone alleys in Massawa, ancient monastery of Debre Bizen, and diving the untouched Dahlak Archipelago.
employment: National service development corps, subsistence agriculture, mining operations, artisan trades.
debtInflation: Fixed exchange rate (15 ERN per USD) with strict import and currency controls managed by the Bank of Eritrea.
transport: Historic narrow-gauge steam railway connecting Massawa to Asmara; mountain highways descending 2,300 meters from Asmara to the Red Sea coast.
cuisine: Injera (fermented spongy flatbread made of teff or sorghum) served with Zigni (spicy slow-cooked beef or lamb stew with berbere), Alicha (mild vegetable turmeric stew), Tsebhi Derho (spicy chicken stew with boiled egg), Shiro (spiced chickpea puree), Suwa (fermented traditional beer), Buna (ceremonial spiced coffee).
music: Traditional Krar five-string lyre music, Guayla folk dance rhythms, legendary vocalists like Yemane Ghebremichael (Baria), Bereket Mengisteab, Helen Meles.
dance: Guayla (circular rhythmic shoulder-shimmying and foot-stamping dance), Kudan dance of the Kunama.
art: Orthodox illuminated manuscripts, vibrant painted church frescoes, woven grass baskets (Mesob).
architecture: Asmara: Modernist City of Africa (UNESCO World Heritage site: unmatched ensemble of Italian Futurist, Art Deco, and Rationalist buildings like the Cinema Impero and Fiat Tagliero service station); Ottoman coral architecture in Massawa.
literature: Rich oral poetry and Ge'ez religious manuscripts; contemporary literature by Alemseged Tesfai (Two Weeks in the Trenches).
cinema: Cinema Impero and Cinema Roma in Asmara; vibrant local video and drama production.
sports: Cycling (the undisputed national obsession since Italian colonial times; Biniam Girmay historic 2024 Tour de France Green Jersey winner and multiple stage champion, Natnael Berhane, Daniel Teklehaimanot), Running (Zersenay Tadese, 5-time World Half-Marathon Champion & Olympic medalist; Ghirmay Ghebreslassie World Marathon Champion).
media: Eri-TV (state television), Dimtsi Hafash (Voice of the Broad Masses radio), Hadas Ertra newspaper.
clothing: Zuria (elegant white cotton dress with embroidered borders worn by women) with Netela shawl; white Shamma wraps for men.
crafts: Colorful woven Mesob bread tables, clay coffee pots (Jebena), hand-embroidered Zuria dresses.
unescoIntangible: Oral and cultural traditions of coffee ceremony and Guayla music
famousPeople: Biniam Girmay (Tour de France Green Jersey Winner)
Nipsey Hussle (American rap icon of Eritrean heritage)
flagDescription: Two right-angled triangles of green (agricultural bounty) at top and blue (marine wealth) at bottom, separated by a red isosceles triangle (blood shed for liberation) pointing to the fly, inside of which is a golden olive wreath encircling an upright olive branch.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a dromedary camel in natural colors surrounded by a wreath of olive leaves, with the name of the state 'STATE OF ERITREA' in English, Tigrinya, and Arabic at the base.
landmarks: Fiat Tagliero Building (Futurist architectural icon in Asmara)
travelNotes: Asmara is one of the world's most unique, peaceful, and visually astonishing capitals; pleasant high-altitude climate; world-class espresso culture in Italian-era cafés.
shortSummary: Eritrea is the heroic Red Sea nation defined by Asmara's UNESCO-inscribed 1930s modernist architecture, an extraordinary national passion for cycling crowned by Tour de France green jersey triumphs, and unyielding self-reliance.
geography: Highest point: Emba Soira (3,018 m). Lowest point: Kulul within the Danakil Depression (-75 m). Longest river: Mereb (Gash) River (440 km) / Barka River. Climate: Cool and temperate in central highlands (Asmara at 2,325m); scorching hot arid desert along the Red Sea coastal lowlands and Danakil Depression. Biodiversity: Dahlak Archipelago marine sanctuary with pristine coral reefs and dugongs; African wild ass (Equus africanus) in the northern Red Sea coastal desert.
economy: Sectors: Services 58%, Industry & Mining 25%, Agriculture 17%. Key industries: Gold, copper, and zinc mining (Bisha mine, Zara mine), Potash mining development (Colluli), Port services and salt production, Food processing and brewing (Asmara Brewery), Textiles and leather. Natural resources: Gold, Copper, Potash, Zinc, Salt, Fish and marine wealth, Arable land. Major exports: Zinc and copper concentrates, Gold bullion, Livestock and hides, Textiles, Salt.
culture: Cuisine: Injera (fermented spongy flatbread made of teff or sorghum) served with Zigni (spicy slow-cooked beef or lamb stew with berbere), Alicha (mild vegetable turmeric stew), Tsebhi Derho (spicy chicken stew with boiled egg), Shiro (spiced chickpea puree), Suwa (fermented traditional beer), Buna (ceremonial spiced coffee).. Music & Dance: Traditional Krar five-string lyre music, Guayla folk dance rhythms, legendary vocalists like Yemane Ghebremichael (Baria), Bereket Mengisteab, Helen Meles.. Sports: Cycling (the undisputed national obsession since Italian colonial times; Biniam Girmay historic 2024 Tour de France Green Jersey winner and multiple stage champion, Natnael Berhane, Daniel Teklehaimanot), Running (Zersenay Tadese, 5-time World Half-Marathon Champion & Olympic medalist; Ghirmay Ghebreslassie World Marathon Champion).. Festivals: Independence Day (May 24), Martyrs' Day (June 20), Revolution Day (September 1), Meskel (Finding of the True Cross), Eid al-Fitr.

name: Eswatini
nationalAnthem: Nkulunkulu Mnikati wetibusiso temaSwati (O Lord our God, Bestower of the blessings upon the Swazi)
motto: Siyinqaba (We are a fortress / We are the mystery)
highestPoint: Emlembe (1,862 m)
longestRiver: Great Usutu (Lusutfu) River (217 km in Eswatini) / Komati River
climate: Varies sharply across four topographical regions: cool and humid Highveld, subtropical Middleveld, hot and dry Lowveld, and sub-humid Lubombo plateau
naturalHazards: Periodic prolonged droughts in the Lowveld
Flash flooding during heavy summer storms
environmentalIssues: Dwindling wildlife populations outside royal reserves
biodiversity: Hlane Royal National Park (sanctuary for white rhinos, lions, and martial eagles) and Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary
currency: Swazi Lilangeni (SZL, L / E, pegged 1:1 to South African Rand)
government: Absolute diarchy / traditional royal constitutional monarchy
headOfState: King Mswati III (Ngwenyama) and Queen Mother Ntfombi Tfwala (Ndlovukati)
legislature: Parliament (Libhandla: Senate and House of Assembly under Tinkhundla system)
mainPoliticalParties: Individual merit-based Tinkhundla electoral system (political parties are legally unrecognized in parliamentary elections)
latestElections: General election September 2023; next scheduled 2028
politicalSituation: Diarchic monarchy where the King (Ngwenyama) rules jointly with the Queen Mother (Ndlovukati); infrastructure development and youth empowerment programs amidst periodic calls for political modernization.
foreignRelations: Sole remaining nation in Africa maintaining official diplomatic relations with Taiwan (Republic of China); member of SACU, SADC, Commonwealth, AU, UN; close economic integration with South Africa.
military: Umbutfo Eswatini Defence Force (UEDF).
adminDivisions: 4 districts (Hhohho, Manzini, Lubombo, Shiselweni)
history: Bantu-speaking Swazi people migrated from East Africa, settling along the Pongola River in the 18th century under King Ngwane III. King Sobhuza I and later King Mswati II unified diverse clans into the formidable Swazi nation during the Mfecane wars. Evaded direct conquest through diplomacy and strategic British protectorate status in 1903 following the Anglo-Boer War. Regained full independence in 1968 under King Sobhuza II, who ruled until 1982 as one of history's longest-reigning monarchs. King Mswati III was crowned in 1986; renamed the country Eswatini in 2018 to mark 50 years of independence.
recentEvents2020_2026: Advanced bilateral diplomatic and high-tech cooperation with Taiwan; concluded national Tinkhundla legislative elections in 2023; expanded solar micro-grids across the Lowveld; hosted regional cultural celebrations drawing international visitors to the Reed Dance.
education: University of Eswatini (UNESWA); free primary education policy expanding literacy.
healthcare: Dramatic public health turnaround: pioneering HIV viral suppression achieving the global UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets ahead of schedule.
socialCustoms: Umhlanga (Reed Dance festival: tens of thousands of maidens gather to pay homage to the Queen Mother), Incwala (sacred kingship first-fruits ceremony), Lobolo (bride wealth in cattle).
etiquette: Greeting with 'Sawubona', clasping both hands or holding the right wrist to show respect when receiving gifts, deep respect for royalty and chiefs.
nationalIdentity: Bound by the siSwati language, cultural allegiance to the monarchy, the shield and spear emblems of the warrior regiments (Emasotsha), and vibrant living royal pageantry.
industries: Soft drink concentrate manufacturing (Coca-Cola global concentrate hub)
Sugar refining and milling (Royal Eswatini Sugar Corporation)
Wood pulp and commercial timber (Usutu Forest)
energy: Domestic hydropower (Maguga, Luphohlo) and biomass cogeneration from sugarcane bagasse supplemented by power imports from South Africa (Eskom)
tradePartners: South Africa (supplies >75% of imports and buys >65% of exports)
tourism: Cultural and eco-tourism: witnessing the Umhlanga Reed Dance and Incwala rituals, hiking the Ezulwini Valley ('Valley of Heaven'), wildlife safaris in Mlilwane and Hlane, and visiting Ngwenya Glass factory.
employment: Commercial sugar and forestry estates, light manufacturing in Matsapha Industrial Estate, civil service.
debtInflation: Monetary policy aligned with the South African Reserve Bank via the Common Monetary Area (CMA); moderate inflation.
transport: Eswatini Railways (specialized freight corridor connecting South Africa to Port of Maputo in Mozambique); King Mswati III International Airport.
airports: King Mswati III International Airport (SHO in Sikhuphe)
ports: Landlocked; primary oceanic freight gateway through Port of Maputo (Mozambique) and Port of Durban (South Africa)
cuisine: Umncweba (dried raw cured meat / biltong), Sishwala (thick porridge served with meat or bean stew), Incwancwa (sour fermented corn meal porridge), Umbidvo wetintsanga (cooked pumpkin leaves with ground peanuts), Emasi emabele (fermented milk mixed with sorghum), Roasted sweet corn.
festivals: Incwala (Kingship and first fruits ceremony in December/January)
MTN Bushfire Festival (internationally acclaimed music and arts festival in Malkerns Valley)
music: Traditional Swazi polyphonic choral singing, Sibhaca warrior drumming, Makhoyane musical bow, contemporary Afro-soul (Sands, Bholoja).
dance: Sibhaca (energetic high-kicking warrior dance), Umhlanga maidens dance, Incwala sacred steps.
art: Hand-blown recycled glassware at Ngwenya Glass, woven Lutindzi grass baskets (Gone Rural), soapstone carvings.
architecture: Traditional circular beehive grass huts (Guca); royal residences at Lobamba; colonial administrative buildings in Mbabane.
literature: Rich oral folklore; Sarah Mkhonza (Pains of a Brenda, novelist and free-speech advocate), Modison Salayedvwa Magagula.
cinema: Emerging independent shorts; Swazi National Film Festival.
sports: Football (Sihlangu Semnikati), Athletics, Boxing, Traditional stick fighting.
media: Times of Eswatini (founded 1897), Eswatini Observer, Eswatini TV.
clothing: Emahiya (brightly colored traditional cloth draped over the shoulder with a wooden pin) worn with leather aprons and beaded necklaces.
crafts: Ngwenya recycled glass animals, woven Lutindzi grass baskets, hand-carved wooden walking sticks, Swazi beaded jewelry.
worldHeritageSites: Ngwenya Mines (one of the oldest known iron ore mines in the world, Tentative List)
unescoIntangible: Living cultural expressions of the Umhlanga and Incwala ceremonies
famousPeople: Richard E. Grant (Oscar-nominated actor, born in Eswatini)
flagDescription: Five horizontal bands of blue (peace and stability), yellow (mineral wealth), crimson red (past battles), yellow, and blue, with a traditional black-and-white Nguni cowhide shield overlaid with two spears and a staff (assegai) centered on the red band.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a traditional Nguni shield supported by a lion (representing the King) and an elephant (representing the Queen Mother), surmounted by a crown of feathers over a banner bearing the national motto 'SIYINQABA'.
landmarks: Ngwenya Glass Complex and Ancient Mine
travelNotes: A tranquil, safe, and culturally captivating mountain kingdom; easy road access from South Africa; the MTN Bushfire Festival is one of Africa's premier cultural gatherings.
shortSummary: The Kingdom of Eswatini is Southern Africa's enchanting mountain monarchy, world-renowned for its living traditional ceremonies like the Umhlanga Reed Dance, the vibrant MTN Bushfire arts festival, and magnificent wildlife sanctuaries.
geography: Highest point: Emlembe (1,862 m). Lowest point: Great Usutu River (21 m). Longest river: Great Usutu (Lusutfu) River (217 km in Eswatini) / Komati River. Climate: Varies sharply across four topographical regions: cool and humid Highveld, subtropical Middleveld, hot and dry Lowveld, and sub-humid Lubombo plateau. Biodiversity: Hlane Royal National Park (sanctuary for white rhinos, lions, and martial eagles) and Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary.
economy: Sectors: Industry & Manufacturing 37%, Services 53%, Agriculture & Forestry 10%. Key industries: Soft drink concentrate manufacturing (Coca-Cola global concentrate hub), Sugar refining and milling (Royal Eswatini Sugar Corporation), Wood pulp and commercial timber (Usutu Forest), Textiles and apparel manufacturing, Mining (anthracite coal, quarrying). Natural resources: Sugarcane arable land, Commercial forests, Hydropower potential, Coal, Clay, Talc. Major exports: Soft drink concentrates, Refined sugar and molasses, Wood pulp and timber, Textiles and garments, Canned fruit.
culture: Cuisine: Umncweba (dried raw cured meat / biltong), Sishwala (thick porridge served with meat or bean stew), Incwancwa (sour fermented corn meal porridge), Umbidvo wetintsanga (cooked pumpkin leaves with ground peanuts), Emasi emabele (fermented milk mixed with sorghum), Roasted sweet corn.. Music & Dance: Traditional Swazi polyphonic choral singing, Sibhaca warrior drumming, Makhoyane musical bow, contemporary Afro-soul (Sands, Bholoja)..
