Sports: Football (Sihlangu Semnikati), Athletics, Boxing, Traditional stick fighting.. Festivals: Umhlanga (Reed Dance festival in August/September), Incwala (Kingship and first fruits ceremony in December/January), MTN Bushfire Festival (internationally acclaimed music and arts festival in Malkerns Valley).

name: Ethiopia
nationalAnthem: Wodefit Gesgeshi, Widd Innat Ityopp'ya (March Forward, Dear Mother Ethiopia)
highestPoint: Ras Dejen in the Simien Mountains (4,550 m)
longestRiver: Blue Nile / Abay River (1,450 km in Ethiopia) / Awash River
majorLakes: Lake Tana (source of the Blue Nile)
climate: Highland tropical temperate (Dega and Woina Dega zones) across central plateaus with refreshing year-round spring-like climate; arid to hyper-arid desert in lowlands (Danakil and Ogaden)
naturalHazards: Recurrent periodic droughts in southern and eastern lowlands
Volcanic activity and sulfur fissures in the Danakil rift (Erta Ale volcano)
Highland soil erosion
environmentalIssues: Water resource management along the Nile Basin
biodiversity: Extraordinary high-altitude endemism: Ethiopian wolf (world's rarest canid), Gelada baboon, Walia ibex, Mountain nyala, and the coffee plant (Coffea arabica)
timeZone: UTC+03:00 (EAT, traditional 12-hour cycle counting dawn as 1:00)
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (Nobel Peace Prize 2019)
legislature: Federal Parliamentary Assembly (House of Peoples' Representatives and House of Federation)
latestElections: General election 2021; presidential appointment October 2024 (Taye Atske Selassie elected president by parliament); general elections scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Consolidation of federal reforms and major national projects under Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, marked by full commercial commissioning of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), macroeconomic currency liberalization in 2024, and BRICS entry.
foreignRelations: Diplomatic capital of Africa (headquarters host of the African Union and UN Economic Commission for Africa in Addis Ababa); joined BRICS in 2024; active diplomatic negotiations for sovereign Red Sea port access.
military: Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF).
adminDivisions: 12 ethnically based regional states and 2 chartered cities (Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa)
history: One of humanity's primordial cradles (fossil hominids 'Lucy' / Dinknesh dating back 3.2 million years and Ardi dating back 4.4 million years). The Kingdom of Aksum flourished from the 1st millennium BC as a major trading empire, minting its own coins and adopting Christianity in 330 AD under King Ezana. Zagwe dynasty carved the monolithic rock-hewn churches of Lalibela in the 12th–13th centuries. Solomonic dynasty governed from Gondar with stone imperial castles. Fiercely defended its sovereignty during the Scramble for Africa, famously defeating the Italian colonial army at the Battle of Adwa in 1896 under Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu Betul—the sole African nation to successfully defeat a European colonial invasion. Emperor Haile Selassie ruled until overthrown in 1974 by the Marxist military Derg regime. EPRDF coalition took power in 1991. Abiy Ahmed became Prime Minister in 2018.
recentEvents2020_2026: Commenced massive multi-gigawatt electricity generation at the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD); formally joined the expanded BRICS bloc in 2024; enacted historic monetary and foreign exchange reforms floating the Birr; completed the Chaka national palace project and urban corridor beautification in Addis Ababa.
historicalFigures: Abebe Bikila (first Black African Olympic gold medalist)
education: Addis Ababa University (historic flagship institution); over 50 public universities nationwide (Jimma, Gondar, Hawassa, Mekelle); expanding STEM education.
healthcare: Nationwide Health Extension Program (HEP) praised globally for rural primary health delivery; Black Lion Hospital (Tikur Anbessa) referral center.
socialCustoms: Elaborate coffee ceremony (Buna) with frankincense, popping corn, and rue herbs; Gursha (feeding a loved one or honored guest by hand as a gesture of affection); fasting traditions (Tsom).
etiquette: Warm two-handed handshakes with slight bowing of the head, kissing both cheeks three or four times among acquaintances, never refusing a Gursha.
nationalIdentity: Defined by unbroken ancient sovereignty, the Battle of Adwa, the unique Ge'ez script, the Julian-like Ethiopian calendar (13 months of sunshine), and being the birthplace of coffee.
industries: Textiles, apparel, and footwear (Hawassa Industrial Park)
agriculture: Cut flowers and roses (major exporter to EU)
energy: Clean green powerhouse: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD, 5,150 MW capacity) making Ethiopia Africa's largest clean electricity exporter
tourism: Exceptional cultural and adventure destination: 11 rock-hewn monolithic churches of Lalibela, Aksumite obelisks and Ark of the Covenant sanctuary, Fasil Ghebbi castles of Gondar, hiking among Geladas in Simien Mountains, trekking Erta Ale lava lake.
employment: Over 65% in smallholder agriculture, textile and manufacturing parks, public infrastructure construction, civil service.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic restructuring supported by IMF and World Bank; adoption of market-determined foreign exchange system in 2024.
transport: Ethiopian Airlines (Africa's largest, most profitable, and globally acclaimed aviation carrier); electrified standard-gauge railway linking Addis Ababa to Djibouti; Addis Ababa Light Rail Transit.
airports: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport (ADD, major global transcontinental passenger hub)
ports: Landlocked; primary oceanic freight access through Port of Djibouti; developing access corridors via Berbera (Somaliland/Somalia) and Lamu (Kenya)
cuisine: Injera (sour, spongy fermented flatbread made from ancient teff grain) served with Doro Wat (rich slow-simmered spicy chicken stew with boiled egg and niter kibbeh spiced butter), Tibs (sautéed beef with rosemary and jalapeños), Kitfo (minced lean beef seasoned with mitmita chili and niter kibbeh), Shiro Wat (rich chickpea paste), Misir Wat (spiced red lentils), Tej (traditional honey wine).
festivals: Timkat (Epiphany celebrations with holy water blessings, UNESCO listed)
Meskel (Finding of the True Cross with bonfire Chibo)
music: Ethio-jazz (pioneered by Mulatu Astatke, blending pentatonic scales with jazz improvisation), Tizita (blues-like melancholic nostalgia), legendary icons Mahmoud Ahmed, Aster Aweke, Teddy Afro.
dance: Eskista (hypnotic, energetic rhythmic shoulder shrugging and neck movement), Oromo shoa dance, Gurage dance.
art: Ancient Ge'ez religious manuscripts, distinctive wide-eyed Ethiopian icon paintings, contemporary canvases by Afewerk Tekle (Stained glass at Africa Hall).
architecture: Monolithic rock-carved churches of Lalibela (carved downward from living volcanic tuff); Aksumite giant stone stele; Fasil Ghebbi 17th-century stone castles in Gondar; fortified historic town of Harar Jugol.
literature: Haddis Alemayehu (Fikir Eske Mekabir / Love Unto Crypt), Baalu Girma (Oromay), Tsegaye Gabre-Medhin; extensive ancient Ge'ez literary corpus.
cinema: Haile Gerima (Sankofa, Harvest: 3,000 Years), Yared Zeleke (Lamb, Cannes selection); expanding contemporary Addis film industry.
sports: Long-distance running dominance: Abebe Bikila (barefoot 1960 Olympic Marathon champion), Haile Gebrselassie, Kenenisa Bekele, Tirunesh Dibaba, Derartu Tulu, Tamirat Tola (Olympic Marathon Gold Paris 2024), Football (Walias).
media: EBC (Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation), Fana Broadcasting Corporate, The Reporter Ethiopia, Addis Fortune.
clothing: Habesha Kemis (exquisite white handspun cotton ankle-length dress with colorful embroidered borders) worn with matching Netela scarf; traditional Kuta cloaks for men.
crafts: Handwoven Shemma cotton textiles, carved wooden headrests, silver and brass Coptic neck crosses, clay Jebena coffee pots.
worldHeritageSites: Lower Valley of the Awash (discovery site of Lucy)
Harar Jugol, the Fortified Historic Town
unescoIntangible: Commemoration feast of the finding of the True Holy Cross of Christ (Meskel)
Fichee-Chambalaalla, New Year festival of the Sidama people
Gada system, an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo
Epiphany (Timkat)
Shuwalid festival of the Harari people
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of green (land, hope, and fertility), yellow (justice, peace, and religious harmony), and red (sacrifice and heroism for freedom), with a blue disk in the center bearing a yellow five-pointed star radiating rays of light (unity of all nations and nationalities).
coatOfArmsDescription: A blue disk bearing a golden radiant five-pointed star emitting equidistant yellow rays, representing national unity and the bright future of the Ethiopian peoples.
landmarks: Church of Saint George (Bet Giyorgis) in Lalibela
travelNotes: A land of unmatched historic majesty, cool highland plateaus, and deep spiritual traditions; Addis Ababa is a vibrant diplomatic metropolis; Lalibela and Simien are global wonders.
shortSummary: Ethiopia is an ancient titan of African sovereignty and the historic birthplace of coffee, home to the breathtaking rock-hewn monolithic churches of Lalibela, the monumental Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, and an Olympic distance-running dynasty.
geography: Highest point: Ras Dejen in the Simien Mountains (4,550 m). Lowest point: Danakil Depression (-125 m). Longest river: Blue Nile / Abay River (1,450 km in Ethiopia) / Awash River. Climate: Highland tropical temperate (Dega and Woina Dega zones) across central plateaus with refreshing year-round spring-like climate; arid to hyper-arid desert in lowlands (Danakil and Ogaden). Biodiversity: Extraordinary high-altitude endemism: Ethiopian wolf (world's rarest canid), Gelada baboon, Walia ibex, Mountain nyala, and the coffee plant (Coffea arabica).
economy: Sectors: Agriculture 36%, Services 40%, Industry & Construction 24%. Key industries: Hydropower generation (GERD, Gibe cascade), Coffee processing and roasting, Textiles, apparel, and footwear (Hawassa Industrial Park), Cement and building materials, Food processing and edible oils, Beverages and beer brewing. Natural resources: Vast hydropower potential, Arable fertile highland soils, Potash (Danakil), Gold (Lega Dembi), Tantalum, Natural gas (Calub/Hilala). Major exports: Coffee (Arabica), Cut flowers and roses, Oilseeds and sesame, Gold, Live animals and meat, Electricity, Khat.
culture: Cuisine: Injera (sour, spongy fermented flatbread made from ancient teff grain) served with Doro Wat (rich slow-simmered spicy chicken stew with boiled egg and niter kibbeh spiced butter), Tibs (sautéed beef with rosemary and jalapeños), Kitfo (minced lean beef seasoned with mitmita chili and niter kibbeh), Shiro Wat (rich chickpea paste), Misir Wat (spiced red lentils), Tej (traditional honey wine).. Music & Dance: Ethio-jazz (pioneered by Mulatu Astatke, blending pentatonic scales with jazz improvisation), Tizita (blues-like melancholic nostalgia), legendary icons Mahmoud Ahmed, Aster Aweke, Teddy Afro.. Sports: Long-distance running dominance: Abebe Bikila (barefoot 1960 Olympic Marathon champion), Haile Gebrselassie, Kenenisa Bekele, Tirunesh Dibaba, Derartu Tulu, Tamirat Tola (Olympic Marathon Gold Paris 2024), Football (Walias).. Festivals: Timkat (Epiphany celebrations with holy water blessings, UNESCO listed), Meskel (Finding of the True Cross with bonfire Chibo), Enkutatash (Ethiopian New Year in September), Irreecha (Oromo thanksgiving festival in Bishoftu), Kulubi Gabriel.

name: Gabon
highestPoint: Mont Bengoué (1,070 m)
longestRiver: Ogooué River (1,200 km)
climate: Equatorial hot and humid with over 85% forest cover; rainy season from September to May with a brief dry spell in January; dry season from June to August
naturalHazards: Localized riverine flash flooding during heavy equatorial downpours
Coastal erosion
environmentalIssues: Poaching of forest elephants for ivory
Petroleum pollution control around offshore platforms
biodiversity: Known as 'Africa's Eden' with over 88% of land covered by dense primary rainforest; 13 national parks protecting world's largest population of forest elephants and western lowland gorillas
headOfState: President of the Transition General Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema
constitution: 1991 (new constitution approved by national referendum in November 2024 establishing a presidential system)
mainPoliticalParties: Committee for the Transition and Restoration of Institutions (CTRI)
latestElections: National constitutional referendum November 2024; presidential and legislative elections scheduled for 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Transition under General Brice Oligui Nguema following the popular August 2023 coup ending 55 years of Bongo family rule; adoption of the 2024 Constitution, infrastructure rehabilitation, and sovereign resource control.
foreignRelations: Member of CEMAC, ECCAS, African Union, Commonwealth of Nations (joined 2022), Francophonie, OPEC, UN; recognized global climate champion in carbon absorption and green conservation diplomacy.
military: Gabonese Armed Forces (FAG) including the Republican Guard.
adminDivisions: 9 provinces
history: Inhabited by Pygmy peoples followed by successive Bantu migrations, notably the Fang and Myene. Portuguese navigators reached the estuary in 1472, naming it 'Gabão' (after the shape of a hooded cloak). French established a naval station in 1839; freed slaves were settled in 1849, founding Libreville ('Freetown'). Albert Schweitzer established his renowned mission hospital at Lambaréné in 1913. Gained independence in 1960 under Léon Mba. Omar Bongo Ondimba governed from 1967 until his death in 2009 (42 years), followed by his son Ali Bongo Ondimba. In August 2023, the military led by General Brice Oligui Nguema carried out a bloodless coup celebrated by the public, initiating a transitional restoration.
recentEvents2020_2026: Enacted the historic 2024 Constitution approved by 91.8% of voters; established sovereign state control over strategic oil assets via Gabon Oil Company (GOC); completed the Transgabonais railway modernization; expanded carbon credit issuance protecting Congo Basin forests.
education: Omar Bongo University (Libreville); Masuku University of Science and Technology (Franceville); high primary school enrollment.
healthcare: Albert Schweitzer Hospital in Lambaréné (historic pioneer in malaria research); modern university hospital centers in Libreville.
socialCustoms: Bwiti spiritual initiation rites utilizing the sacred psychoactive Iboga root, communal village councils, respect for forest spirits.
etiquette: Warm handshakes, addressing people with courtesy titles, showing deference to village elders, relaxed oceanfront sociability.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated as 'Africa's Eden' of pristine rainforests, proud guardian of Bwiti spiritual traditions, high urban literacy, and timber/manganese wealth.
industries: Petroleum and natural gas extraction (Port-Gentil, Rabi-Kounga)
Manganese mining (Moanda, world's second-largest high-grade manganese producer)
Timber and plywood processing (Nkok Special Economic Zone)
energy: Grand Poubara and Tchimbélé hydroelectric dams providing over 55% of power, supplemented by natural gas thermal plants in Libreville and Port-Gentil
tradePartners: China (major importer of oil and manganese)
tourism: Pristine wilderness and wildlife safari tourism: tracking 'surfing hippos' and nesting leatherback turtles in Loango National Park, mandrill trekking in Lopé National Park, and visiting Schweitzer's Hospital in Lambaréné.
employment: Oil and mining services, forestry processing at Nkok, civil service, transport logistics.
debtInflation: Upper-middle-income status with single-digit inflation anchored by BEAC and the Central African CFA Franc.
transport: Transgabonais Railway (670 km railway transporting Moanda manganese and timber to the Port of Owendo); Libreville-Port-Gentil ferry links.
airports: Léon Mba International Airport (LBV in Libreville)
ports: Port of Owendo (mineral and container port near Libreville)
cuisine: Poulet Nyembwe (chicken stewed in a rich sauce made from fresh pounded red palm nut butter), Poisson salé aux choux (salted fish with cabbage), Feuilles de manioc (cassava leaves stewed with smoked fish or peanut paste), Crabes farcis (spiced stuffed ocean land crabs), Kumu greens, Roasted plantains.
music: Traditional Ngombi (eight-string harp) music used in Bwiti ceremonies, modern Gabonese Afro-pop and rumba (Oliver N'Goma, Pierre Akendengué, Shan'L).
dance: Bwiti ritual trance dance, Mengane, Ndjembe women's dance.
art: Fang and Kota reliquary guardian figures (Mbulu Ngulu) clad in hammered brass and copper sheets, Punu white-faced Maiden masks (Okuyi).
architecture: St. Michael's Church of Nkembo in Libreville (famed for 31 intricately carved wooden columns by a blind artist); Albert Schweitzer hospital complex in Lambaréné.
literature: Angèle Rawiri (Elonga, Fureurs et cris de femmes), Jean-Baptiste Tati Loutard, Justine Mintsa (Histoire d'Awo).
cinema: Imunga Ivanga (Dôlè, won Tanit d'Or at Carthage), Henri-Joseph Koumba Bididi.
sports: Football: The Panthers (Les Panthères; Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Premier League and European superstar and all-time top scorer), Taekwondo (Anthony Obame 2012 Olympic Silver Medalist), Cycling (Tropicale Amissa Bongo stage race).
media: L'Union (national daily), Gabon 1ère (public television), Gabon Media Time.
clothing: Tailored European business wear in urban centers; colorful Iboga ceremonial white and red linen robes during Bwiti rites.
crafts: Kota copper and brass reliquaries, Punu carved white masks, Mbigou soapstone carvings, woven raffia mats.
worldHeritageSites: Ecosystem and Relict Cultural Landscape of Lopé-Okanda
unescoIntangible: Bwiti spiritual, musical and therapeutic traditions
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of green (lush natural forests), yellow (equatorial sun and mineral richness), and blue (the Atlantic Ocean).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a shield with three golden bezants and a sailing ship navigating the Atlantic, supported by two black panthers beneath an Okoumé tree, with the national motto 'Union, Travail, Justice'.
landmarks: Kongou Waterfalls in Ivindo National Park
travelNotes: High standard of living, clean and peaceful; Loango and Ivindo offer some of the most extraordinary, pristine wildlife encounters on the African continent.
shortSummary: Gabon is 'Africa's Eden', an environmentally pristine sanctuary where over 88% of the country is dense tropical rainforest, home to surfing hippos on Loango's beaches, rich manganese mines, and the sacred Bwiti spiritual tradition.
geography: Highest point: Mont Bengoué (1,070 m). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Ogooué River (1,200 km). Climate: Equatorial hot and humid with over 85% forest cover; rainy season from September to May with a brief dry spell in January; dry season from June to August. Biodiversity: Known as 'Africa's Eden' with over 88% of land covered by dense primary rainforest; 13 national parks protecting world's largest population of forest elephants and western lowland gorillas.
economy: Sectors: Petroleum & Mining 45%, Services 43%, Agriculture & Forestry 12%. Key industries: Petroleum and natural gas extraction (Port-Gentil, Rabi-Kounga), Manganese mining (Moanda, world's second-largest high-grade manganese producer), Timber and plywood processing (Nkok Special Economic Zone), Palm oil processing, Brewing (Sobraga). Natural resources: Manganese (world #2 producer), Petroleum, Timber (Okoumé wood), Iron ore (Belinga), Gold, Hydropower. Major exports: Crude petroleum, Manganese ores, Sawn timber, veneer, and plywood, Palm oil.
culture: Cuisine: Poulet Nyembwe (chicken stewed in a rich sauce made from fresh pounded red palm nut butter), Poisson salé aux choux (salted fish with cabbage), Feuilles de manioc (cassava leaves stewed with smoked fish or peanut paste), Crabes farcis (spiced stuffed ocean land crabs), Kumu greens, Roasted plantains.. Music & Dance: Traditional Ngombi (eight-string harp) music used in Bwiti ceremonies, modern Gabonese Afro-pop and rumba (Oliver N'Goma, Pierre Akendengué, Shan'L).. Sports: Football: The Panthers (Les Panthères; Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Premier League and European superstar and all-time top scorer), Taekwondo (Anthony Obame 2012 Olympic Silver Medalist), Cycling (Tropicale Amissa Bongo stage race).. Festivals: Independence Day (August 17), Fête des Cultures (Libreville), Bwiti cultural festivals.

name: The Gambia
highestPoint: Red Rock (53 m, lowest national high-point in Africa)
longestRiver: Gambia River (1,120 km total course, flowing through entire country)
climate: Tropical wet-and-dry with a short, intense rainy season from June to October, and a sunny, dry season from November to May
naturalHazards: Harmattan dust winds
Riverine and coastal storm flooding
Saltwater intrusion into agricultural soils during dry season
biodiversity: Abuko Nature Reserve and River Gambia National Park (home to chimpanzees, hippos, West African manatees, and over 540 species of migratory birds)
mainPoliticalParties: People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism (PDOIS)
latestElections: Presidential election 2021 (Adama Barrow re-elected); legislative elections 2022; next presidential election scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Democratic consolidation under President Adama Barrow; hosted the 15th OIC Islamic Summit in Banjul in May 2024; implementation of the Truth, Reconciliation and Reparations Commission (TRRC) recommendations.
foreignRelations: Member of ECOWAS, Commonwealth (rejoined 2018), OIC, African Union, UN; championed the historic international case at the ICJ upholding the Genocide Convention; very close relations with Senegal (Senegambia cooperation).
military: Gambia Armed Forces (GAF) comprising Army, Navy, and National Republican Guard.
adminDivisions: 5 rural divisions and 2 municipalities (Banjul and Kanifing)
history: Part of the ancient Ghana and Mali Empires; Kaabu Empire dominated the region from the 13th to 18th centuries. Portuguese established trading posts on James Island (now Kunta Kinteh Island) in the 15th century, later sold to Britain. In 1783, Britain acquired the banks of the Gambia River, while France controlled surrounding Senegal. Gained independence in 1965 under Sir Dawda Jawara as a constitutional monarchy before becoming a republic in 1970. Yahya Jammeh seized power in a 1994 coup, ruling autocratically for 22 years until defeated in democratic elections in December 2016 by Adama Barrow.
recentEvents2020_2026: Hosted the 15th Summit of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Banjul in 2024; opened the landmark Senegambia Bridge over the Gambia River; expanded modern container facilities at the Port of Banjul; achieved record European winter sun tourism.
historicalFigures: Kunta Kinteh (historic figure immortalized in Alex Haley's Roots)
Edward Francis Small (pioneer of trade unionism and self-determination)
education: University of The Gambia (UTG); American International University West Africa; expanding vocational training centers.
healthcare: Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital (EFSTH in Banjul); network of regional clinics; pioneering Medical Research Council (MRC) unit at Fajara.
socialCustoms: Celebrated as the 'Smiling Coast of Africa' for warm hospitality (Teranga), communal Bantaba tree meeting platforms, lively naming ceremonies.
etiquette: Right-hand use for greeting and eating, inquiring warmly about health and family, respectful greetings for community elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the Gambia River flowing through its heart, the heritage of Kunta Kinteh, Kora harp music, Wolof and Mandinka oral praise singing (Griots / Jalolu).
industries: Port transshipment and re-export trade to Senegal/Mali
energy: Expansion of solar mini-grids and the 23MW Jambur solar plant, reducing reliance on heavy fuel oil generation
tourism: Premier European winter-sun holiday destination ('The Smiling Coast'): golden Atlantic beaches at Kololi and Kotu, birdwatching tours along the mangrove creeks (Bolongs), river cruises, and heritage tours to Kunta Kinteh Island.
employment: Tourism and hospitality, peanut farming smallholders, informal urban retail in Serekunda, artisanal fishing.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic stability supported by IMF Extended Credit Facility; steady Dalasi management by Central Bank of The Gambia.
transport: Senegambia Bridge at Farafenni (revolutionizing transit between northern and southern Senegal); Port of Banjul; river transport barges.
ports: Port of Banjul (deepwater river estuary port)
cuisine: Domoda (national dish: savory groundnut peanut butter stew cooked with beef or chicken and vegetables served over white rice), Benachin (one-pot Wolof seasoned rice / Jollof rice), Superkanja (okra, fish, and palm oil stew), Yassa au poulet (marinated lemon and caramelized onion chicken), Wonjo (refreshing hibiscus juice).
music: Kora (21-string harp lute pioneered by the Jobarteh, Suso, and Cissokho griot dynasties: Jaliba Kuyateh 'King of Kora', Sona Jobarteh first female professional kora master), Afro-Manding.
dance: Kanyeleng comedic dance, Lenjen Mandinka bird dance, Sabar Wolof dance.
art: Carved wooden djembe drums and koras, tie-dye and batik textile art, woven palm leaf handicrafts.
architecture: Colonial wooden and stone architecture in Banjul; Senegambian stone circles; traditional thatched riverine compounds.
literature: Ebou Dibba (Chaff on the Wind), Lenrie Peters (The Second Round, poet and surgeon), Alex Haley's Roots (ancestral setting in Juffureh).
cinema: Emerging documentary cinema; Cinekambiya International Film Festival.
sports: Traditional wrestling (Borreh, the national sport attracting huge arena crowds), Football (The Scorpions: sensational quarter-finalists at 2021 AFCON debut, 2023 AFCON appearance).
media: The Point, Foroyaa, Daily Observer, GRTS (Gambia Radio & Television Services).
clothing: Grand Boubou robes made of shining Bazin fabric with intricate embroidery; brightly colored headscarves.
crafts: Handcrafted 21-string Koras, batik wall hangings, carved wooden wildlife figurines, silver filigree earrings.
worldHeritageSites: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites (including Fort Bullen and San Domingo)
Stone Circles of Senegambia (shared with Senegal)
unescoIntangible: Kankurang, Manding initiatory rite (with Senegal)
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of red (sun and savanna) and green (agriculture and forests), separated by a central blue band (Gambia River) edged with thin white stripes (peace and unity).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features an axe and a hoe crossed on a blue-and-white shield, supported by two lions (one holding an axe, one holding a hoe), topped by a heraldic helmet and oil palm over the motto 'Progress, Peace, Prosperity'.
landmarks: Kunta Kinteh Island (historic slave trade site in Juffureh)
travelNotes: Extremely welcoming and friendly destination ('The Smiling Coast'); English widely spoken; incredible haven for birdwatchers and beachgoers.
shortSummary: The Gambia, affectionately known as the 'Smiling Coast of Africa', winds along the banks of the Gambia River, celebrated worldwide as the ancestral setting of Roots, the home of enchanting 21-string Kora music, and sun-kissed Atlantic beaches.
geography: Highest point: Red Rock (53 m, lowest national high-point in Africa). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Gambia River (1,120 km total course, flowing through entire country). Climate: Tropical wet-and-dry with a short, intense rainy season from June to October, and a sunny, dry season from November to May. Biodiversity: Abuko Nature Reserve and River Gambia National Park (home to chimpanzees, hippos, West African manatees, and over 540 species of migratory birds).
economy: Sectors: Services & Tourism 65%, Agriculture 20%, Industry 15%. Key industries: Tourism and coastal resort hospitality, Peanut (groundnut) shelling and oil processing, Artisanal and commercial fisheries, Port transshipment and re-export trade to Senegal/Mali, Brewing (Julbrew beer). Natural resources: Fish and marine fisheries, Arable riverine soil, Titanium and ilmenite sand deposits, Sun, sand, and eco-tourism waterways. Major exports: Peanut products (groundnut oil and meal), Cashew nuts, Fish and seafood, Re-exports of consumer goods, Scrap metal.
culture: Cuisine: Domoda (national dish: savory groundnut peanut butter stew cooked with beef or chicken and vegetables served over white rice), Benachin (one-pot Wolof seasoned rice / Jollof rice), Superkanja (okra, fish, and palm oil stew), Yassa au poulet (marinated lemon and caramelized onion chicken), Wonjo (refreshing hibiscus juice).. Music & Dance: Kora (21-string harp lute pioneered by the Jobarteh, Suso, and Cissokho griot dynasties: Jaliba Kuyateh 'King of Kora', Sona Jobarteh first female professional kora master), Afro-Manding.. Sports: Traditional wrestling (Borreh, the national sport attracting huge arena crowds), Football (The Scorpions: sensational quarter-finalists at 2021 AFCON debut, 2023 AFCON appearance).. Festivals: Independence Day (February 18), Roots International Homecoming Festival, Banjul Cultural Festival, Tobaski (Eid al-Adha).
sources: National Statistical Office of The Gambia

name: Ghana
highestPoint: Mount Afadja / Afadjato (885 m)
lowestPoint: Gulf of Guinea / Atlantic Ocean (0 m)
longestRiver: Volta River (1,500 km total system)
majorLakes: Lake Volta (world's largest artificial reservoir by surface area, covering 8,502 km²)
climate: Tropical warm and comparatively dry along southeastern coastal belt; hot and humid in southwestern rainforests; semi-arid savanna in the north
naturalHazards: Harmattan dry dusty winter winds from the Sahara
Periodic seasonal droughts in northern regions
Urban flash flooding in Accra during June monsoons
environmentalIssues: Galamsey (illegal artisanal gold mining water pollution and forest destruction)
biodiversity: Kakum National Park (famed for its canopy walkway through virgin rainforest) and Mole National Park (savanna elephant sanctuary)
headOfState: President (Transition post-December 2024 general elections: John Dramani Mahama / Nana Akufo-Addo succession)
latestElections: Presidential and parliamentary elections December 7, 2024; peaceful democratic succession reinforcing Ghana's status as a democratic benchmark in West Africa
politicalSituation: Model of enduring multi-party democracy in Africa with smooth alternation of power; macroeconomic recovery supported by IMF program, debt restructuring, and the expansion of the 'Beyond the Return' diaspora initiative.
foreignRelations: Member of ECOWAS, African Union, Commonwealth, UN; headquarters host of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat in Accra; leading troop contributor to UN peacekeeping operations.
military: Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) comprising Army, Navy, and Air Force.
adminDivisions: 16 regions
history: Inhabited since the Bronze Age; site of the powerful Ashanti (Asante) Empire (founded c. 1701 by Osei Tutu I and Okomfo Anokye) renowned for the sacred Golden Stool (Sika Dwa Kofi) and military resistance under Yaa Asantewaa. European powers built over 30 fortified slave castles along the 'Gold Coast' (Elmina Castle founded by Portuguese in 1482; Cape Coast Castle). British conquered the Ashanti Empire in 1902. On March 6, 1957, visionary Pan-African leader Kwame Nkrumah led Ghana to become the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule, declaring 'our independence is meaningless unless it is linked up with the total liberation of Africa'. Transitioned to stable Fourth Republic democracy in 1992 under Jerry Rawlings.
recentEvents2020_2026: Conducted the December 2024 general elections with exemplary democratic maturity; hosted the 13th African Games in Accra in 2024; deepened continental trade integration through the AfCFTA Secretariat in Accra; advanced domestic lithium mining and refinery agreements (Ewoyaa project).
historicalFigures: Kofi Annan (UN Secretary-General & Nobel Peace Laureate)
education: University of Ghana (Legon, Accra); Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST, Kumasi); Ashesi University (renowned tech institution); free senior high school (Free SHS) policy.
healthcare: National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS); Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra (one of West Africa's premier tertiary medical centers); pioneer in drone medical delivery (Zipline).
socialCustoms: Akwaaba (warm Ghanaian welcome), vibrant Friday funerals celebrating life with fantastical figurative coffins, Sunday church and mosque fellowship, Chieftaincy durbars.
etiquette: Strict use of the right hand for greeting and eating, handshakes with a distinctive finger snap, polite inquiries after family, respect for chiefs and elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by Pan-African leadership (Black Star of Africa), rich Ashanti royal heritage, Kente cloth, highlife music, and celebrated peaceful democratic stability.
industries: Gold mining (top gold producer in Africa)
Automotive assembly (Toyota, VW, Kantanka plants in Accra)
energy: Akosombo Hydroelectric Dam on Lake Volta, Bui Dam, and offshore gas-to-power generation providing reliable electricity and exports to Togo/Benin
tourism: Premier cultural and heritage destination: Cape Coast Castle and Elmina Castle (UNESCO slave trade pilgrimage sites), Kakum National Park canopy walkway, Manhyia Palace in Kumasi, vibrant arts in Jamestown Accra, and the global 'Year of Return' diaspora pilgrimage.
employment: Commerce and retail services, smallholder cocoa farming, artisanal and industrial mining, technology startups.
debtInflation: Comprehensive debt restructuring under the G20 Common Framework backed by IMF Extended Credit Facility restoring fiscal stability and lower inflation.
transport: Modernized Tema and Takoradi ports; expanding Tema-Mpakadan standard gauge railway; modernized Kotoka International Airport Terminal 3.
ports: Port of Tema (premier maritime container gateway)
Port of Takoradi (oil and bulk cargo hub)
cuisine: Jollof Rice (Ghanaian style with aromatic basmati rice, rich tomato stew, and spices—legendary friendly culinary rivalry with Nigeria), Fufu with light soup (Abenkwan / Palm nut soup) and goat meat, Banku with grilled Tilapia and hot pepper shito, Waakye (rice and beans cooked with red sorghum leaves), Red Red (fried plantains with black-eyed pea stew), Kelewele (spicy fried plantain cubes), Kenkey with fried fish and shito pepper sauce.
festivals: Homowo (Ga festival of hooting at hunger in Accra)
music: Highlife (E.T. Mensah, Osibisa, Pat Thomas), Hiplife (Reggie Rockstone, Sarkodie), Afrobeats and modern stars (Black Sherif, Stonebwoy, Shatta Wale, King Promise).
dance: Adowa (graceful Akan dance of hand movements and footwork), Kpanlogo, Agbadza, Azonto (globally viral street dance).
art: Adinkra symbols (visual ideographs embodying philosophical concepts like Gye Nyame), fantasy figurative coffins (carved as fish, cars, cacao pods by Ga masters), contemporary art at Nubuke Foundation.
architecture: Ashanti traditional earthen buildings (UNESCO listed); UNESCO-listed coastal trading forts and castles (Elmina Castle, Cape Coast Castle); modern Black Star Square (Independence Square in Accra).
literature: Ama Ata Aidoo (The Dilemma of a Ghost, Changes), Ayi Kwei Armah (The Beautyful Ones Are Not Yet Born), Efua Sutherland, Kofi Awoonor.
cinema: Kwaw Ansah (Love Brewed in the African Pot), Shirley Frimpong-Manso, vibrant Kumawood and Ghallywood film industries.
sports: Football: The Black Stars (4-time AFCON champions; historic 2010 FIFA World Cup quarter-finalists; Michael Essien, Abedi Pele, Asamoah Gyan, Mohammed Kudus), Boxing (prolific world champion factory: Azumah Nelson, Ike Quartey).
media: Daily Graphic, Ghanaian Times, Joy FM, Citi FM, TV3, Peace FM.
clothing: Kente cloth (handwoven silk and cotton royal fabric featuring intricate geometric motifs and colors) worn off the shoulder; colorful Dutch wax Batakari tunics.
crafts: Handwoven Bonwire Kente cloth, carved Ashanti stools, Adinkra stamped textiles, Bolgatanga handwoven elephant grass baskets.
worldHeritageSites: Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions (including Elmina and Cape Coast Castles)
unescoIntangible: Craftsmanship of Kente weaving and Adinkra symbolism
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of red (blood shed for independence), yellow (mineral wealth), and green (rich forests and agriculture), with a large black five-pointed star in the center of the yellow band (the 'Black Star of Africa', guiding light of African freedom).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a blue shield divided into four quarters (sword and staff, Osu Castle, cocoa tree, gold mine), supported by two golden eagles wearing Black Stars around their necks, surmounted by a beaded torse and the Black Star, with the national motto 'Freedom and Justice'.
landmarks: Independence Arch and Black Star Square (Accra)
travelNotes: One of the most welcoming, stable, and culturally rich nations in the world; Akwaaba spirit is immediately felt; Accra boasts thriving dining, nightlife, and beach clubs.
shortSummary: Ghana is the proud vanguard of African independence and democratic freedom, renowned worldwide for the Golden Stool of the Ashanti, handwoven royal Kente cloth, the poignant history of Cape Coast Castle, and infectious Highlife and Afrobeats music.
geography: Highest point: Mount Afadja / Afadjato (885 m). Lowest point: Gulf of Guinea / Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Volta River (1,500 km total system). Climate: Tropical warm and comparatively dry along southeastern coastal belt; hot and humid in southwestern rainforests; semi-arid savanna in the north. Biodiversity: Kakum National Park (famed for its canopy walkway through virgin rainforest) and Mole National Park (savanna elephant sanctuary).
economy: Sectors: Services 49%, Industry 31%, Agriculture 20%. Key industries: Gold mining (top gold producer in Africa), Petroleum extraction (Jubilee, TEN offshore oilfields), Cocoa processing, Aluminium smelting (Valco), Automotive assembly (Toyota, VW, Kantanka plants in Accra), Food and beverage manufacturing. Natural resources: Gold (leading export), Crude petroleum, Cocoa, Bauxite, Manganese, Lithium (Ewoyaa), Timber, Hydropower. Major exports: Gold bullion, Crude petroleum, Cocoa beans, paste, and butter, Cashew nuts, Manganese, Timber.
culture: Cuisine: Jollof Rice (Ghanaian style with aromatic basmati rice, rich tomato stew, and spices—legendary friendly culinary rivalry with Nigeria), Fufu with light soup (Abenkwan / Palm nut soup) and goat meat, Banku with grilled Tilapia and hot pepper shito, Waakye (rice and beans cooked with red sorghum leaves), Red Red (fried plantains with black-eyed pea stew), Kelewele (spicy fried plantain cubes), Kenkey with fried fish and shito pepper sauce.. Music & Dance: Highlife (E.T. Mensah, Osibisa, Pat Thomas), Hiplife (Reggie Rockstone, Sarkodie), Afrobeats and modern stars (Black Sherif, Stonebwoy, Shatta Wale, King Promise).. Sports: Football: The Black Stars (4-time AFCON champions; historic 2010 FIFA World Cup quarter-finalists; Michael Essien, Abedi Pele, Asamoah Gyan, Mohammed Kudus), Boxing (prolific world champion factory: Azumah Nelson, Ike Quartey).. Festivals: Homowo (Ga festival of hooting at hunger in Accra), Aboakyer deer hunt festival (Winneba), Hogbetsotso festival (Ewe), Afrochella / Afro Future music festival, Chale Wote Street Art Festival (Jamestown).

name: Guinea
highestPoint: Mount Nimba / Mont Richard-Molard (1,752 m tripoint peak)
longestRiver: Niger River (source in Guinea highlands) / Gambia River / Senegal River (Bafing tributary)
climate: Equatorial-tropical with heavy monsoon rains along coastal Maritime Guinea from June to November; cooler in the Fouta Djallon highlands; semi-arid savanna in the northeast
naturalHazards: Harmattan dusty winds in winter
Torrential rainfall causing coastal flash flooding and landslides
environmentalIssues: Bauxite and iron ore mining runoff
biodiversity: Known as the 'Water Tower of West Africa' (Château d'eau de l'Afrique de l'Ouest) giving birth to the Niger, Senegal, and Gambia rivers; Mount Nimba harbors viviparous toads and tool-using chimpanzees
headOfState: President of the Transition General Mamadi Doumbouya
constitution: 2010 (new constitution drafted in 2024 for transitional roadmap referendum)
mainPoliticalParties: Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea (UFDG)
Union for the Progress of Guinea (UPG)
latestElections: Presidential election 2020; transition referendum scheduled 2024/2025 followed by general elections
politicalSituation: Transitional administration led by General Mamadi Doumbouya since September 2021; focused on sovereign renegotiation of mining contracts, the monumental Simandou iron ore infrastructure megaproject, and national reconciliation.
foreignRelations: Member of ECOWAS, African Union, OIC, Francophonie, UN; major strategic mining partnerships with China (Baowu, Winning Consortium), Rio Tinto, and international consortia.
military: Armed Forces of Guinea (FAG).
adminDivisions: 8 regions (including Conakry Special Zone) and 33 prefectures
history: Part of the medieval Ghana and Mali Empires; Emperor Sundiata Keita unified Mandinka lands in the 13th century. Fouta Djallon became an Islamic theocratic state in the 18th century under Karamokho Alfa. Samori Ture led a legendary 16-year anti-colonial resistance with his Wassoulou Empire before capture in 1898. In 1958, under charismatic trade unionist Ahmed Sékou Touré, Guinea made history as the only French African territory to vote 'Non' to Charles de Gaulle's French Community, boldly choosing immediate independence: 'We prefer poverty in freedom to riches in slavery'. Governed under socialist one-party rule until Sékou Touré's death in 1984, followed by Lansana Conté.
recentEvents2020_2026: Mobilized full construction of the multi-billion-dollar Simandou Iron Ore Project (world's largest undeveloped high-grade iron ore deposit, including a 650 km trans-Guinean railway and deepwater port at Moribaya); advanced domestic bauxite refining and expanded hydro power at Souapiti dam.
historicalFigures: Miriam Makeba (adopted Guinean citizenship and resided in Conakry)
education: Gamal Abdel Nasser University of Conakry (UGANC); General Lansana Conté University; Kofi Annan University of Guinea.
healthcare: Donka University Hospital and Ignace Deen Hospital in Conakry; strengthened epidemic surveillance post-Ebola.
socialCustoms: Vibrant Djembe drumming celebrations, tea gatherings (Ataya with three rounds), profound reverence for griot storytelling genealogies.
etiquette: Respectful greetings with right hand placed on the chest, inquiring at length after health and family, honoring elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the proud historic 'Non' to French colonization, the title of 'Water Tower of West Africa', Djembe percussive mastery, and unparalleled bauxite wealth.
industries: Bauxite mining (world's second largest producer and #1 exporter to China)
Iron ore mining and rail infrastructure (Simandou)
naturalResources: Bauxite (world's largest proven reserves, over 25% of global total)
energy: Souapiti Hydroelectric Dam (450 MW) and Kaléta Dam on the Konkouré River transforming Guinea into a clean energy exporter via the OMVG power pool
tourism: Eco-adventure and cultural tourism: trekking through the emerald canyons, waterfalls, and mist of the Fouta Djallon (Chutes de la Soumba, Chutes de Kinkon), climbing Mount Nimba, and relaxing on the pristine beaches of the Îles de Los off Conakry.
employment: Bauxite and infrastructure contracting, subsistence agriculture, artisanal mining, transport logistics.
debtInflation: Disciplined fiscal management supported by surging bauxite export royalties and mining foreign direct investment.
transport: Trans-Guinean Railway (under construction for Simandou iron ore); modernized Autonomous Port of Conakry; coastal highway corridors.
airports: Ahmed Sékou Touré International Airport (CKY in Conakry)
ports: Port of Conakry (container and general cargo)
Port of Moribaya (Simandou deepwater iron ore port)
cuisine: Poulet Yassa (chicken marinated in Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and caramelized onions), Kansiyé (rich peanut butter meat stew), Fouti (rice served with okra sauce and crushed chili), Konkoé (smoked catfish in tomato-palm oil sauce), Tô with baobab sauce, Beignets de banane.
festivals: Festival des Arts de la Rue de Conakry
music: The homeland of the Djembe drum and the Mandinka Kora: Les Ballets Africains (national dance troupe celebrated globally), Bembeya Jazz National, Mory Kanté (whose 1987 song 'Yéké Yéké' was the first African single to sell over one million copies worldwide), Sekouba Bambino, Grand P.
dance: Acrobatic Djembe dances (Soli, Kassa, Doundounba / Strong Man's dance), Mandinka masked dances.
art: Baga Nimba / D'mba shoulder masks (monumental wooden headdress symbolizing fertility and maternal wisdom, celebrated by Picasso and Western collectors), carved wooden Djembe drums.
architecture: Sudano-Sahelian earthen architecture; colonial structures in Conakry; Grand Mosque of Conakry (one of the largest mosques in sub-Saharan Africa).
literature: Camara Laye (L'Enfant noir / The African Child, timeless masterpiece of African literature), Williams Sassine, Tierno Monénembo (The King of Kahel, Renaudot Prize winner).
cinema: David Achkar, Mama Keïta (L'Absence); pioneer of early pan-African documentary cinema.
sports: Football: Syli National (National Elephant; quarter-finalists at 2024 AFCON; global stars Naby Keïta, Serhou Guirassy European Golden Shoe contender), Traditional wrestling.
media: Horoya (historic state newspaper), Guinéenews, Espace TV, RTG (Radio Télévision Guinéenne).
clothing: Intricately embroidered Grand Boubou made of shining damask Leppi fabric (indigo-dyed cotton of the Fouta Djallon).
crafts: Master-carved Djembe drums from hardwood (Lenke), hand-dyed indigo Leppi cloth, leather bags, hand-beaten gold jewelry.
worldHeritageSites: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve (shared with Côte d'Ivoire)
unescoIntangible: Cultural space of the Sosso-Bala (sacred ancient balafon of the 13th-century King Sumanguru Kante preserved at Niagassola, inscribed 2008)
flagDescription: Three equal vertical bands of red (blood of martyrs and sacrifice for freedom), yellow (sun and mineral riches of the earth), and green (vegetation and agricultural prosperity)—identical to the colors of the French flag reversed into Pan-African colors.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a white dove carrying an olive branch over a shield in the national colors, supported by an elephant head and the motto 'Travail, Justice, Solidarité'.
travelNotes: An unpolished adventure jewel with majestic mountain cascades in the Fouta Djallon; warm and vibrant musical life; travelers should prepare for seasonal monsoon rains.
shortSummary: Guinea, the proud 'Water Tower of West Africa', is blessed with the world's richest bauxite and iron ore reserves, the mist-clad highlands of the Fouta Djallon, and an iconic global musical legacy pioneered by Mory Kanté and master Djembe percussionists.
geography: Highest point: Mount Nimba / Mont Richard-Molard (1,752 m tripoint peak). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Niger River (source in Guinea highlands) / Gambia River / Senegal River (Bafing tributary). Climate: Equatorial-tropical with heavy monsoon rains along coastal Maritime Guinea from June to November; cooler in the Fouta Djallon highlands; semi-arid savanna in the northeast. Biodiversity: Known as the 'Water Tower of West Africa' (Château d'eau de l'Afrique de l'Ouest) giving birth to the Niger, Senegal, and Gambia rivers; Mount Nimba harbors viviparous toads and tool-using chimpanzees.
economy: Sectors: Mining & Industry 40%, Agriculture 24%, Services 36%. Key industries: Bauxite mining (world's second largest producer and #1 exporter to China), Iron ore mining and rail infrastructure (Simandou), Gold and diamond extraction, Alumina refining (Fria), Cement manufacturing, Beverages and brewing (Guicopres, Sobragui). Natural resources: Bauxite (world's largest proven reserves, over 25% of global total), High-grade iron ore (Simandou), Gold, Diamonds, Hydropower potential ('Water Tower of Africa'). Major exports: Bauxite ore, Gold, Alumina, Diamonds, Agricultural produce.
culture: Cuisine: Poulet Yassa (chicken marinated in Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and caramelized onions), Kansiyé (rich peanut butter meat stew), Fouti (rice served with okra sauce and crushed chili), Konkoé (smoked catfish in tomato-palm oil sauce), Tô with baobab sauce, Beignets de banane.. Music & Dance: The homeland of the Djembe drum and the Mandinka Kora: Les Ballets Africains (national dance troupe celebrated globally), Bembeya Jazz National, Mory Kanté (whose 1987 song 'Yéké Yéké' was the first African single to sell over one million copies worldwide), Sekouba Bambino, Grand P.. Sports: Football: Syli National (National Elephant; quarter-finalists at 2024 AFCON; global stars Naby Keïta, Serhou Guirassy European Golden Shoe contender), Traditional wrestling.. Festivals: Independence Day (October 2), Festival des Arts de la Rue de Conakry, FIDA (Festival International de Danse Africaine).

name: Guinea-Bissau
nationalAnthem: Esta É a Nossa Pátria Bem Amada (This Is Our Beloved Homeland)
coastline: 350 km (plus extensive estuarine shorelines and Bijagós Archipelago)
highestPoint: Unnamed hill in the eastern plateau (300 m)
longestRiver: Geba River (540 km total) / Corubal River / Cacheu River
majorMountains: None (predominantly coastal lowland, mangrove estuaries, and interior savanna)
climate: Tropical hot and humid with a heavy monsoon rainy season from June to November (bringing up to 2,000mm rainfall) and a dry Harmattan season from December to May
naturalHazards: Harmattan winter dust haze
Extensive coastal flooding during high tides and rainy seasons
biodiversity: Bijagós Archipelago (UNESCO Biosphere Reserve comprising 88 islands and islets, sanctuary for saltwater-adapted hippos, green sea turtles, and African manatees)
languages: Crioulo / Guinea-Bissau Creole (universal national lingua franca spoken by over 90%)
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister Rui Duarte de Barros
mainPoliticalParties: PAIGC (African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde)
latestElections: Legislative elections 2023; presidential election scheduled November 2024 / 2025
politicalSituation: President Umaro Sissoco Embaló served as Chairperson of ECOWAS (2022–2023); ongoing political dialogues, public sector formalization, and anti-narcotics enforcement.
foreignRelations: Member of ECOWAS, UEMOA, CPLP, African Union, OIC, Francophonie, UN; close historical and cultural brotherhood with Cabo Verde and Portugal.
military: Revolutionary Armed Forces of the People (FARP).
adminDivisions: 8 regions and 1 autonomous sector (Bissau)
history: Part of the Kaabu Empire (tributary of the Mali Empire) that flourished from the 13th to 18th centuries. Portuguese navigator Nuno Tristão arrived in 1446; Cacheu and Bissau became prominent slave trading forts. Amílcar Cabral founded the PAIGC in 1956, leading one of Africa's most brilliant, ideologically cohesive armed national liberation struggles (1963–1974) combining guerrilla warfare with literacy and healthcare. Unilaterally declared independence in 1973, recognized by Portugal in 1974 following Lisbon's Carnation Revolution. Underwent periods of political turbulence and military coups before democratic stabilization.
recentEvents2020_2026: Chaired ECOWAS summit leadership; advanced cashew industrial processing to capture domestic export value; expanded the modernized commercial port at Bissau; hosted international oceanographic research in the Bijagós Biosphere Reserve.
historicalFigures: Amílcar Cabral (founding father, philosopher of liberation)
education: Amílcar Cabral University; Jean Piaget University; expanding community primary schooling in Crioulo and Portuguese.
healthcare: Simão Mendes National Hospital in Bissau; community health post network supported by international humanitarian agencies.
socialCustoms: Matriarchal traditions of the Bijagó islands (where women hold spiritual and family authority), lively Bissau Carnival, communal palm wine tapping.
etiquette: Warm handshakes with both hands, sharing meals from common platters, respectful greetings in Crioulo ('Kuma ku bu sta?').
nationalIdentity: Defined by the revolutionary legacy of Amílcar Cabral, the universally unifying Crioulo language, Gumbe dance rhythms, and the untamed paradise of the Bijagós islands.
agriculture: Cashew nuts (accounts for over 85% of total export revenue, world's 5th largest producer)
Rice (staple crop cultivated in mangrove polders)
energy: Connecting to the regional OMVG hydroelectric grid (from Kaléta/Souapiti in Guinea) alongside expanding solar micro-grids in Bissau
tradePartners: India (purchases over 75% of raw cashew exports)
tourism: Incomparable ecotourism: exploring the 88 islands of the Bijagós Archipelago (Orango National Park to observe rare saltwater hippopotamuses, Poilão Island sea turtle nesting), fishing charters, and the historic Portuguese colonial architecture of Bolama.
employment: Over 75% in smallholder cashew farming, artisanal fishing, and informal urban market commerce.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic discipline within UEMOA and the euro-pegged West African CFA Franc.
transport: Inter-island pirogue and ferry transit; modernized national roads connecting Bissau to Ziguinchor (Senegal) and Boké (Guinea).
airports: Osvaldo Vieira International Airport (OXB in Bissau)
ports: Port of Bissau (main maritime cargo terminal)
cuisine: Caldo de Mancarra (rich chicken or fish stew made with ground peanut paste and palm oil, served over rice), Caldo de Chabe (palm nut fruit stew), Sigá, Grilled freshly caught Red Snapper (Garoupa), Fried sweet plantains, Cashew apple juice and fermented cashew wine.
festivals: Carnaval de Bissau (extraordinary national carnival featuring gigantic papier-mâché masks and Bijagó feathered warrior costumes)
music: Gumbe (upbeat national percussive rhythm popularized by Super Mama Djombo and Patche Di Rima), Tina music, Kora melodies.
dance: Gumbe, Broxa, traditional Bijagó warrior initiation dances.
art: Bijagó carved wooden zoomorphic masks (bull masks / Dugn'be, sawfish, shark heads), painted Carnival masks, carved wooden stools.
architecture: Portuguese colonial Art Deco and neoclassical architecture in Bissau Velho and the decaying former capital of Bolama; traditional circular mud and thatch houses with veranda posts.
literature: Amílcar Cabral (Unity and Struggle), Abdulai Silá (A Última Tragédia, first published novel in Guinea-Bissau), Odete Semedo.
cinema: Flora Gomes (Mortu Nega, The Blue Eyes of Yonta, internationally award-winning cinema pioneer), Sana Na N'Hada (Nome, Cannes 2023 selection).
sports: Football: Djurtus (The Wild Dogs; 4 consecutive AFCON qualifications: 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023), Wrestling, Athletics.
media: Nô Pintcha, Rádio Sol Mansi, Televisão da Guiné-Bissau (TGB).
clothing: Pano de Pente (traditional handwoven geometric cotton wrap cloth produced by Manjaco weavers); modern casual attire.
crafts: Pano de Pente handwoven textiles, Bijagó carved wooden bull masks, woven palm leaf fans and baskets.
unescoIntangible: Cultural expressions and craftsmanship of the Bijagó mask rituals
flagDescription: Two equal horizontal bands of yellow (sun, labor, and savanna) and green (lush agriculture and hope), with a vertical red band (blood shed for liberation) on the hoist side bearing a black five-pointed star (African unity and freedom).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a red shield bearing a black star, bordered by two symmetrical olive branches and joined at the bottom by a golden sea shell, with the banner 'UNIDADE, LUTA, PROGRESSO'.
landmarks: Bissau Velho (Old Town Bissau) and Fortaleza de São José da Amura
travelNotes: An authentic, off-the-beaten-path destination; Bijagós islands offer some of the most magical, remote eco-marine experiences on earth; vibrant welcoming spirit.
shortSummary: Guinea-Bissau is the proud birthplace of Amílcar Cabral's liberation philosophy, home to the enchanted 88 islands of the Bijagós Archipelago where saltwater hippos roam pristine beaches, and producer of the world's most prized cashew nuts.
geography: Highest point: Unnamed hill in the eastern plateau (300 m). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Geba River (540 km total) / Corubal River / Cacheu River. Climate: Tropical hot and humid with a heavy monsoon rainy season from June to November (bringing up to 2,000mm rainfall) and a dry Harmattan season from December to May. Biodiversity: Bijagós Archipelago (UNESCO Biosphere Reserve comprising 88 islands and islets, sanctuary for saltwater-adapted hippos, green sea turtles, and African manatees).
economy: Sectors: Agriculture & Fisheries 50%, Services 36%, Industry 14%. Key industries: Cashew nut processing and export, Artisanal and commercial fisheries, Peanut and palm oil processing, Beverage brewing and bottling, Bauxite and phosphate exploration (Boe bauxite). Natural resources: Fish and shrimp, Timber, Bauxite (Boe deposit), Phosphates (Farim), Offshore petroleum potential. Major exports: Raw cashew nuts, Fish and shrimp, Sawn wood and timber, Peanuts.
culture: Cuisine: Caldo de Mancarra (rich chicken or fish stew made with ground peanut paste and palm oil, served over rice), Caldo de Chabe (palm nut fruit stew), Sigá, Grilled freshly caught Red Snapper (Garoupa), Fried sweet plantains, Cashew apple juice and fermented cashew wine.. Music & Dance: Gumbe (upbeat national percussive rhythm popularized by Super Mama Djombo and Patche Di Rima), Tina music, Kora melodies.. Sports: Football: Djurtus (The Wild Dogs; 4 consecutive AFCON qualifications: 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023), Wrestling, Athletics.. Festivals: Carnaval de Bissau (extraordinary national carnival featuring gigantic papier-mâché masks and Bijagó feathered warrior costumes), Independence Day (September 24), Amílcar Cabral Day (January 20).

internationalOrgs: UN (UNEP and UN-Habitat headquarters in Nairobi)

history: Inhabited since the dawn of humanity (fossil hominids discovered by Louis and Mary Leakey in the Turkana Basin). Swahili coastal city-states (Mombasa, Lamu, Malindi) flourished from the 8th century through Indian Ocean maritime trade. British established the East Africa Protectorate in 1895, building the Uganda Railway ('Lunatic Express') from Mombasa to Lake Victoria, which founded Nairobi. Mau Mau armed uprising in the 1950s fought British colonial rule. Gained independence in 1963 under founding father Jomo Kenyatta. Daniel arap Moi ruled from 1978 to 2002. Promulgated a transformative progressive constitution in 2010 establishing 47 devolved counties.
recentEvents2020_2026: Hosted the historic inaugural Africa Climate Summit in Nairobi; celebrated Kelvin Kiptum's official world marathon record (2:00:35) and Faith Kipyegon's Olympic gold triumphs; expanded geothermal generation making Kenya a top-10 global geothermal producer; designated Major Non-NATO Ally by the US in 2024.
historicalFigures: Wangari Maathai (first African woman Nobel Peace Laureate)
education: University of Nairobi; Kenyatta University; Strathmore University; pioneering 'Silicon Savannah' tech incubator hubs (iHub).
healthcare: Universal health coverage rollout under the Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF); Kenyatta National Hospital; Gertrude's Children's Hospital.
socialCustoms: Harambee (community self-help fundraising spirit), Nyama Choma open-air barbecue gatherings, lively Nairobi matatu pop culture, tea breaks (Chai).
etiquette: Friendly greetings ('Habari yako' / 'Jambo'), shaking hands with warmth, respectful address of elders as 'Mzee' or 'Mama'.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the spirit of Harambee, long-distance running world supremacy, breathtaking wildlife safaris, Swahili coastal culture, and cutting-edge mobile fintech (M-Pesa).
industries: Mobile fintech and digital technology ('Silicon Savannah')
agriculture: Cut flowers and roses (supplying over 35% of European flower market)
energy: Over 90% of electricity generated from renewable sources: world leader in geothermal power (Olkaria), Lake Turkana Wind Power (largest wind farm in Africa), and solar
tourism: Premier global safari and beach destination: witnessing the Great Migration in the Maasai Mara, admiring elephants against Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, hiking Mount Kenya, and unwinding on white Diani Beach.
employment: M-Pesa digital economy, tea and horticultural estates, safari hospitality, tech and financial services.

ports: Port of Mombasa (largest container port in East Africa)

art: Kisii soapstone carvings, Maasai beadwork jewelry, Kitengela hand-blown glass, vibrant Matatu custom graffiti vehicle art.

media: Daily Nation, The Standard, Citizen TV, NTV, Capital FM.
clothing: Kikoi woven cotton wrap cloth; colorful Maasai Shúkà plaid blanket worn by pastoralists; modern urban smart-casual.
crafts: Maasai beaded necklaces, Kisii soapstone chess sets and dishes, Kiondo handwoven sisal handbags, Akamba wood carvings.
worldHeritageSites: Kenya Lake System in the Great Rift Valley
unescoIntangible: Isukuti dance of Isukha and Idakho communities of Western Kenya (inscribed 2014)
Enkipaata, Eunoto and Olng'esherr, three male rites of passage of the Maasai
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of black (the people of Kenya), red with white fringes (blood shed for freedom, with white for peace and honesty), and green (natural wealth and agriculture), overlaid in the center by a traditional Maasai warrior shield and two crossed white spears.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features two lions holding Maasai spears and a traditional shield depicting a cockerel holding an axe against the national colors, resting on Mount Kenya and agricultural crops over the motto 'HARAMBEE'.

Freezing winter blizzards and snowstorms in the highlands
Severe gully erosion (Dongas)

foreignRelations: Member of SACU, SADC, Commonwealth, African Union, UN; completely surrounded by South Africa, creating an inseparable economic, customs, and monetary union.
military: Lesotho Defence Force (LDF).
adminDivisions: 10 administrative districts
history: Inhabited by San hunter-gatherers who left thousands of rock paintings. In the 1820s, King Moshoeshoe I brilliantly unified fragmented refugee clans fleeing the Difaqane (Mfecane) wars, establishing his mountain stronghold on the flat-topped plateau of Thaba Bosiu. Successfully defended his people against Zulu impis and Boer incursions through tactical diplomacy. To prevent Boer conquest, Moshoeshoe requested Queen Victoria's protection in 1868, creating the British protectorate of Basutoland. Gained independence in 1966 as the Kingdom of Lesotho under King Moshoeshoe II.
recentEvents2020_2026: Launched major construction of the Polihali Dam (Phase II of the Lesotho Highlands Water Project) to double water export royalties to South Africa; expanded high-value diamond mining at Letseng (source of the world's largest high-clarity diamonds); hosted international high-altitude marathon and cycling events.
historicalFigures: King Moshoeshoe I (master statesman and founder of the Basotho nation)
religions: Christianity (Roman Catholic ~45%, Protestant / Lesotho Evangelical Church ~40%, Anglican/Other ~10%) ~95%
literacyRate: 81.0% (uniquely with female literacy surpassing male literacy due to traditional male herding practices)
education: National University of Lesotho (NUL in Roma); Limkokwing University of Creative Technology in Maseru; free primary education.
healthcare: Queen 'Mamohato Memorial Hospital in Maseru; network of mountain clinics and flying doctor services for remote alpine villages.
socialCustoms: Basotho Blanket culture (wearing beautifully patterned wool heritage blankets like the Seanamarena as daily formal wear and protection against mountain frost), equestrian pony riding, herd boy traditions (Balisana).
etiquette: Greeting with 'Khotso' (Peace), shaking hands using both hands, offering items with the right hand cupped by the left.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated as the 'Mountain Kingdom in the Sky', defined by the Basotho blanket, the iconic conical Mokorotlo straw hat, hardy Basotho ponies, and the sacred mountain of Thaba Bosiu.
industries: Textiles and garment manufacturing (major exporter to the US under AGOA)
Highlands water export and hydropower generation
Wool and mohair shearing and processing
agriculture: Livestock rearing (sheep for fine wool, Angora goats for mohair)
naturalResources: Diamonds (Letseng mine produces the world's highest dollar-per-carat diamonds)
energy: 'Muela Hydropower Station (generating 72 MW from water transfer tunnels), expanding utility-scale solar farms (Mafeteng Solar Plant)
exports: Fresh water (via LHWP tunnels to Gauteng, South Africa)
tradePartners: South Africa (dominant import source and partner)
tourism: Mountain adventure tourism: skiing and snowboarding at Afriski Mountain Resort (one of Africa's only ski resorts), pony trekking through remote Maloti valleys, viewing Maletsunyane Falls (192 m single-drop waterfall), and scaling Sani Pass.
employment: Textile factories in Maseru and Maputsoe, diamond mining, water project construction, wool/mohair pastoralism, remittances from South African mines.
debtInflation: Exchange rate parity with the South African Rand under the Common Monetary Area ensuring financial predictability.
transport: Paved trans-mountain highways (A1 mountain route); iconic Sani Pass 4x4 gravel zig-zag route to KwaZulu-Natal; Maseru rail terminus connecting to South African freight network.
airports: Moshoeshoe I International Airport (MSU in Maseru)
ports: Landlocked enclave; 100% of maritime freight handled through Port of Durban (South Africa)
cuisine: Papa (thick cornmeal porridge) served with Moroho (sauteed wild mustard greens) and braised beef or oxtail stew, Chakalaka, Motoho (fermented sour sorghum porridge), Nyekwe (boiled corn and beans), Roasted sweet potatoes.
music: Famo (accordion-driven traditional music with vocal accordion duels), traditional Lesiba mouth-bow music, choral hymns.
dance: Mokhibo (graceful kneeling shoulder and head dance performed by women), Mohobelo (vigorous leaping and foot-stamping dance performed by men).
art: San rock paintings across Sehlabathebe, hand-woven mohair tapestries from Teyateyaneng, traditional Mokorotlo straw weaving.
architecture: Traditional circular sandstone rondavels with thatched grass conical roofs; historic French missionary stone church at Roma; fortress ruins of Thaba Bosiu.
literature: Thomas Mofolo (Chaka, pioneering classic of early African literature translated into multiple world languages), Manka Mofolo.
cinema: Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese (This Is Not a Burial, It's a Resurrection, internationally acclaimed masterpiece starring Mary Twala).
sports: Athletics (marathon running and mountain trail racing), Football (Likuena / The Crocodiles), Taekwondo.
media: Lesotho Times, Public Eye, LNRBS (Lesotho National Broadcasting Service).
clothing: Basotho Blanket (Kobo) worn draped over the shoulders with pride; Mokorotlo conical woven straw hat (the national symbol depicted on the flag).
crafts: Mokorotlo conical straw hats, handwoven mohair rugs and tapestries, clay pottery, carved wooden walking sticks.

landmarks: Thaba Bosiu (Sacred Mountain of King Moshoeshoe I)
travelNotes: The 'Kingdom in the Sky' offers unmatched alpine scenery, pony trekking across dramatic canyons, and skiing in winter; all travelers should bring warm layers year-round.
shortSummary: Lesotho is the majestic 'Kingdom in the Sky', an entirely high-altitude mountain monarchy enclaved within South Africa, celebrated for its iconic Mokorotlo straw hats, heritage Basotho wool blankets, hardy mountain ponies, and the colossal Maletsunyane Falls.

name: Liberia
motto: The Love of Liberty Brought Us Here
highestPoint: Mount Wuteve (1,440 m)
longestRiver: Cavalla River (515 km, border river) / St. Paul River
climate: Tropical wet equatorial climate with intense monsoon rainfall from May to November; warm and humid year-round
naturalHazards: Harmattan dusty winter winds
Coastal storm surges and severe beach erosion in West Point Monrovia
environmentalIssues: Deforestation of the Upper Guinea rainforest
Artisanal gold and diamond panning runoff
biodiversity: Sapo National Park (second largest primary tropical rainforest in West Africa, sanctuary for endangered pygmy hippopotamuses, western chimpanzees, and forest elephants)
currency: Liberian Dollar (LRD, L$) and US Dollar (USD, $ co-circulating)
legislature: Legislature of Liberia (Senate and House of Representatives)
latestElections: General election late 2023 (Joseph Boakai defeated incumbent George Weah in an exemplary peaceful democratic runoff; inaugurated January 2024); next scheduled 2029
politicalSituation: Smooth democratic transition in 2024 under President Joseph Boakai; focus on the ARREST agenda (Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation, Tourism) and anti-corruption.
foreignRelations: Africa's oldest modern republic (founded 1847); unique historic ties with the United States; member of Mano River Union, ECOWAS, African Union, UN.
military: Armed Forces of Liberia (AFL).
adminDivisions: 15 counties
history: Inhabited by diverse indigenous peoples (Kpelle, Bassa, Kru, Vai). In 1822, the American Colonization Society (ACS) established a settlement for freed African Americans at Cape Mesurado, founding Monrovia (named after US President James Monroe). On July 26, 1847, Americo-Liberian settlers declared independence as a sovereign republic, drafting a constitution modeled on that of the United States. Americo-Liberian elites dominated politics through the True Whig Party until a violent 1980 military coup led by Samuel Doe. Two devastating civil wars (1989–2003) claimed over 250,000 lives before the Accra Comprehensive Peace Agreement. Ellen Johnson Sirleaf was elected in 2005 as Africa's first democratically elected female head of state, winning the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize.
recentEvents2020_2026: Conducted the acclaimed 2023 presidential election recognized globally as a triumph of democratic resilience; celebrated former football legend George Weah's gracious concession; President Joseph Boakai inaugurated in 2024 launching infrastructure and anti-graft initiatives; expanded Mount Coffee Hydropower facility.
historicalFigures: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf (first female elected African president & Nobel Laureate)
George Weah (FIFA Ballon d'Or winner & president)
Momolu Duwalu Bukele (inventor of the Vai syllabic script)
education: University of Liberia (founded 1862 in Monrovia); Cuttington University (historic Episcopal institution founded 1889); Tubman University.
healthcare: John F. Kennedy Medical Center in Monrovia; strengthened national epidemic resilience after surviving the 2014-2015 Ebola outbreak.
socialCustoms: Palava hut mediation system for dispute resolution, Friday fish fry gatherings, strong community church fellowships, high respect for secret societies (Poro and Sande).
etiquette: Warm handshakes with the distinctive Liberian middle finger snap at release, addressing elders respectfully, asking after family welfare.
nationalIdentity: Defined by Africa's oldest modern republican constitution, the historic bond with American freedom movements, Vai literary innovation, and enduring resilience.
industries: World's largest open maritime ship registry (Liberian flag of convenience)
agriculture: Natural rubber (Firestone, world's largest contiguous rubber estate)
energy: Mount Coffee Hydroelectric Plant on the St. Paul River (88 MW capacity), supplemented by West African Power Pool (CLSG line) cross-border electricity imports
tourism: Untamed coastal and eco-adventure tourism: surfing the legendary left-hand point breaks of Robertsport, trekking through the pristine rainforest of Sapo National Park, and exploring Lake Piso wetland lagoon.
employment: Rubber tapping, informal trade and retail, artisanal gold mining, shipping registry administration.
debtInflation: Dual-currency monetary framework managed by the Central Bank of Liberia with support from IMF Extended Credit Facility.
transport: Freeport of Monrovia; iron ore mining railway from Yekepa to the Port of Buchanan; modernizing coastal highways.
airports: Roberts International Airport (ROB in Harbel / Monrovia)
cuisine: Jollof Rice (Liberian style with smoked meats and country spice), Palm Butter Soup (rich soup made from boiled, pounded oil palm pericarp cooked with crab, shrimp, or beef, served over rice), Cassava Leaf stew, Pepper Soup (spicy broth with fresh goat meat or fish), Fried plantain (Kala), Fufu with torborgee sauce (fermented pea and bitter ball stew cooked in palm oil).
music: Gbema traditional music, Hipco (indigenous Liberian hip-hop incorporating colloquial Liberian Kreyol), highlife.
dance: Traditional mask dancing of the Dan and Gio peoples, Kru seafaring dances, acrobatic stilt dancing.
art: Dan / Gio carved wooden masks with smooth black patina, Vai syllabic script manuscripts, woven country cloth.
architecture: Americo-Liberian southern antebellum-style wooden houses with wide verandas in Monrovia, Careysburg, and Harper; historic Providence Baptist Church.
literature: Wilton Sankawulo (The Rain and the Night), Bai T. Moore (Murder in the Cassava Patch), Patricia Jabbeh Wesley.
cinema: Emerging independent film movement; Liberia Film Institute.
sports: Football (Lone Star; George Weah remains the only African footballer in history to win the FIFA World Player of the Year and Ballon d'Or in 1995), Athletics (Joseph Fahnbulleh 200m Olympic finalist).
media: The Inquirer, FrontPage Africa, Daily Observer, ELBC (Liberia Broadcasting System).
clothing: Traditional Country Cloth woven tunics; vibrant patterned Lappa wrap skirts; American-style business suits.
crafts: Dan wooden masks, handwoven Lofa country cloth, carved wooden mortars, soapstone beads.
worldHeritageSites: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve (Tentative List / transboundary extension)
unescoIntangible: Vai indigenous syllabic script and traditional storytelling
flagDescription: Eleven horizontal stripes alternating red (valor) and white (purity of mind), with a square blue canton in the upper hoist bearing a white five-pointed star (liberty granted to the African ex-slaves), closely modeled on the United States flag.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a sailing ship approaching the Liberian coast with a rising sun, a dove with a scroll, an oil palm, and a plow and spade, with the national motto 'The Love of Liberty Brought Us Here'.
landmarks: Providence Island (historic landing site in Monrovia)
travelNotes: Robertsport is a hidden paradise for international surfers; Monrovia is lively with beachfront nightlife; yellow fever vaccination required.
shortSummary: Liberia is Africa's oldest modern independent republic, famed for its historic constitutional heritage, the world-class left-hand surf breaks of Robertsport, the rare pygmy hippos of Sapo National Park, and the footballing immortality of George Weah.
geography: Highest point: Mount Wuteve (1,440 m). Lowest point: Atlantic Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Cavalla River (515 km, border river) / St. Paul River. Climate: Tropical wet equatorial climate with intense monsoon rainfall from May to November; warm and humid year-round. Biodiversity: Sapo National Park (second largest primary tropical rainforest in West Africa, sanctuary for endangered pygmy hippopotamuses, western chimpanzees, and forest elephants).
economy: Sectors: Agriculture & Forestry 34%, Services 48%, Industry & Mining 18%. Key industries: World's largest open maritime ship registry (Liberian flag of convenience), Iron ore mining (ArcelorMittal at Yekepa), Natural rubber processing (Firestone plantation), Gold mining (New Liberty, Bea Mountain), Commercial forestry. Natural resources: Iron ore, Natural rubber, Timber, Gold, Diamonds, Hydropower potential. Major exports: Iron ore, Natural rubber, Gold, Palm oil, Timber.
culture: Cuisine: Jollof Rice (Liberian style with smoked meats and country spice), Palm Butter Soup (rich soup made from boiled, pounded oil palm pericarp cooked with crab, shrimp, or beef, served over rice), Cassava Leaf stew, Pepper Soup (spicy broth with fresh goat meat or fish), Fried plantain (Kala), Fufu with torborgee sauce (fermented pea and bitter ball stew cooked in palm oil).. Music & Dance: Gbema traditional music, Hipco (indigenous Liberian hip-hop incorporating colloquial Liberian Kreyol), highlife.. Sports: Football (Lone Star; George Weah remains the only African footballer in history to win the FIFA World Player of the Year and Ballon d'Or in 1995), Athletics (Joseph Fahnbulleh 200m Olympic finalist).. Festivals: Independence Day (July 26), National Flag Day (August 24), Thanksgiving Day (first Thursday of November), Armed Forces Day.

name: Libya
coastline: 1,770 km (longest Mediterranean coastline of any African nation)
highestPoint: Bikku Bitti in the Tibesti Mountains (2,266 m)
longestRiver: Great Man-Made River (GMMR, colossal subterranean engineering pipeline network tapping ancient Sahara aquifers)
majorLakes: Gaberoun (desert oasis lake in Idhan Ubari sand sea)
Waw an Namus volcanic caldera lake
climate: Mediterranean along northern coastal belt with mild rainy winters and hot dry summers; hyper-arid Sahara desert covering over 90% of territory
naturalHazards: Ghibli (hot, dry, dust-laden desert wind)
Desert sandstorms
Severe flash flooding from intense Mediterranean cyclones (Medicane Daniel in 2023)
environmentalIssues: Reconstruction of flood barriers in eastern coastal cities
biodiversity: Jabal al Akhdar Mediterranean pine and cypress forests, desert-adapted fennec foxes, gazelles, and loggerhead sea turtle nesting beaches along the Gulf of Sirte
government: Transitional state under UN-facilitated political process
headOfState: Chairman of the Presidential Council Mohamed al-Menfi
headOfGovernment: Prime Minister of the Government of National Unity (GNU) Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh
legislature: House of Representatives (Tobruk) and High Council of State (Tripoli)
mainPoliticalParties: Various civic and regional parliamentary blocs
latestElections: UN-mediated roadmap working toward unified general presidential and parliamentary elections
politicalSituation: Transitional framework supported by the UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL); National Oil Corporation (NOC) maintaining crude production above 1.2 million barrels per day; nationwide post-flood reconstruction.
foreignRelations: Member of the Arab League, African Union, OPEC, OAPEC, Arab Maghreb Union, OIC, UN; significant geopolitical cooperation with Italy, Turkey, Egypt, and international energy majors.
military: Armed Forces under institutional unification efforts.
adminDivisions: 22 districts (shabiyat) across the historic regions of Tripolitania, Cyrenaica, and Fezzan
history: Inhabited by indigenous Berbers since antiquity. Phoenicians founded the coastal emporia of Oea (Tripoli), Labdah (Leptis Magna), and Sabratha (forming the 'Tripolis').
