Ancient Greeks colonized Cyrenaica, founding Cyrene in 631 BC. Annexed by the Roman Empire, becoming a wealthy agricultural province and the birthplace of Roman Emperor Septimius Severus. Arab-Islamic expansion reached Libya in 643 AD. Ruled by the Ottoman Empire from 1551. Colonized by Italy in 1911, sparking fierce heroic resistance led by Omar al-Mukhtar ('Lion of the Desert') until his execution in 1931. Gained independence in 1951 as a federal kingdom under King Idris I. Muammar Gaddafi seized power in 1969, governing for 42 years under his Third Universal Theory until ousted during the 2011 Arab Spring revolution.
recentEvents2020_2026: Mobilized major coastal reconstruction following catastrophic Medicane Daniel dam bursts in Derna; stabilized crude oil output via the National Oil Corporation (NOC); hosted international infrastructure conferences restoring Tripoli International Airport and Mediterranean highway links.
historicalFigures: Septimius Severus (Roman Emperor born in Leptis Magna)
Eratosthenes (calculated Earth's circumference, born in Cyrene)
religions: Christian and other foreign resident minorities ~3%
education: University of Tripoli (historic Al Fateh University); University of Benghazi; free public primary, secondary, and tertiary schooling.
healthcare: Tripoli Central Hospital; Benghazi Medical Center; subsidized public healthcare system recovering from conflict disruptions.
socialCustoms: Traditional mint tea (Shah-i) with thick foam (Raghwa), generous hospitality, Friday family gatherings, deep pride in tribal lineage and anticolonial history.
etiquette: Respectful greetings with right hand placed over heart, addressing elders with reverence, modest attire in public areas.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the anticolonial martyrdom of Omar al-Mukhtar, immense Saharan oil wealth, majestic Roman coastal cities, and Mediterranean seafaring heritage.
industries: Crude petroleum extraction and refining (Es Sider, Ras Lanuf)
Natural gas extraction and LNG export (Greenstream pipeline to Italy)
Iron and steel manufacturing (LISCO in Misrata)
agriculture: Wheat and barley (coastal plains and Kufra circular pivot fields)
naturalResources: Crude petroleum (largest proven reserves in Africa, over 48 billion barrels)
energy: Gas-fired thermal power generation plants and the colossal engineering marvel of the Great Man-Made River utilizing fossil groundwater to irrigate the coast
tourism: Unmatched classical archaeological treasures: UNESCO Roman ruins of Leptis Magna (vast amphitheater, Severan Arch), Sabratha theatre overlooking the Mediterranean, ancient Greek Cyrene, prehistoric rock art of the Acacus Mountains, and desert oasis towns of Ghadames.
employment: National Oil Corporation (NOC) and subsidiaries, civil administration, port logistics in Misrata, retail commerce.
debtInflation: Very low external public debt backed by substantial sovereign wealth (Libyan Investment Authority) and foreign exchange reserves.
transport: Coastal Libyan Highway connecting Tunisia to Egypt; modern commercial container port at Misrata; reconstructed international airports.
ports: Port of Misrata (leading commercial container hub)
Ras Lanuf and Es Sider (crude oil terminals)
cuisine: Bazeen (traditional unleavened barley dough dome served in a rich spiced tomato-onion stew with lamb, hard-boiled eggs, and potatoes), Couscous with mutton, Shakshouka, Usban (spiced tripe sausage stuffed with rice, liver, herbs, and spices), Asida (sweet flour dough dome with honey and clarified butter), Sharba Libiya (spicy aromatic soup with lamb, chickpeas, tomato, and mint).
music: Malfuf and Ma'luf Andalusi classical music, Libyan Bedouin desert poetry (Ghinna), modern stars like Ahmed Fakroun (pioneer of Arab world funk and synth-pop), Asmahan.
dance: Hajalah Bedouin dance, Tuareg sword dance, traditional wedding line dancing.
art: Prehistoric rock art in Tadrart Acacus (spanning 12,000 years of Saharan environmental evolution), Islamic calligraphy, silver Berber filigree.
architecture: Magnificent Roman limestone and marble architecture at Leptis Magna; UNESCO mud-brick oasis architecture of Ghadames ('Pearl of the Desert') with covered subterranean alleys; Red Castle (Assaraya al-Hamra) in Tripoli.
literature: Ibrahim al-Koni (master of Tuareg magical realism: Gold Dust, The Bleeding of the Stone), Hisham Matar (Pulitzer Prize winner: The Return: Fathers, Sons and the Land in Between), Sadeq Naihoum.
cinema: Filming setting for Moustapha Akkad's epic film Lion of the Desert (starring Anthony Quinn as Omar al-Mukhtar).
sports: Football (Al Ahli Tripoli, Al Ittihad Tripoli; Mediterranean Games champions), Athletics, Futsal, Traditional equestrian events.
media: Libya Al Ahrar TV, 218 TV, LANA (Libyan News Agency), Alwasat.
clothing: Traditional Jurd (pure wool white toga-like wrap worn by men over a tunic), embroidered Farmla vest and Shashiya red cap; Bedouin silver jewelry.
crafts: Ghadames embroidered leather slippers, Tuareg silver jewelry and amulets, woven wool carpets, copper pots.
unescoIntangible: Bedouin oral poetry and Ghadames traditional craftsmanship
flagDescription: Three horizontal bands of red (blood shed for liberation), black (the Senussi dynasty and banner of independence, twice the width of other bands), and green (prosperity and agriculture), with a white crescent and five-pointed star centered in the black band.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features the star and crescent of Islam enclosed within circular inscriptions, serving as the official seal of the Government of National Unity and Presidential Council.
landmarks: Leptis Magna (one of the grandest Roman cities in the world)
Old Town of Ghadames ('Pearl of the Desert')
travelNotes: Possesses what many archaeologists consider the finest Roman ruins on Earth; travel requires guided arrangements and up-to-date security protocols; people are dignified and hospitable.
shortSummary: Libya spans the longest Mediterranean coastline in Africa and vast petroleum reserves, distinguished by the magnificent Roman ruins of Leptis Magna, the mud-brick oasis of Ghadames, and the enduring anticolonial heroism of Omar al-Mukhtar.
geography: Highest point: Bikku Bitti in the Tibesti Mountains (2,266 m). Lowest point: Sabkhat Ghuzayyil (-47 m). Longest river: Great Man-Made River (GMMR, colossal subterranean engineering pipeline network tapping ancient Sahara aquifers). Climate: Mediterranean along northern coastal belt with mild rainy winters and hot dry summers; hyper-arid Sahara desert covering over 90% of territory. Biodiversity: Jabal al Akhdar Mediterranean pine and cypress forests, desert-adapted fennec foxes, gazelles, and loggerhead sea turtle nesting beaches along the Gulf of Sirte.
economy: Sectors: Hydrocarbons 62%, Services 30%, Industry & Construction 6%, Agriculture 2%. Key industries: Crude petroleum extraction and refining (Es Sider, Ras Lanuf), Natural gas extraction and LNG export (Greenstream pipeline to Italy), Petrochemicals and fertilizers, Iron and steel manufacturing (LISCO in Misrata), Cement production. Natural resources: Crude petroleum (largest proven reserves in Africa, over 48 billion barrels), Natural gas, Gypsum, Silica sand, Fossil groundwater (Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System). Major exports: Crude petroleum, Natural gas (via Greenstream to Italy), Refined petroleum products, Petrochemicals, Iron and steel products.
culture: Cuisine: Bazeen (traditional unleavened barley dough dome served in a rich spiced tomato-onion stew with lamb, hard-boiled eggs, and potatoes), Couscous with mutton, Shakshouka, Usban (spiced tripe sausage stuffed with rice, liver, herbs, and spices), Asida (sweet flour dough dome with honey and clarified butter), Sharba Libiya (spicy aromatic soup with lamb, chickpeas, tomato, and mint).. Music & Dance: Malfuf and Ma'luf Andalusi classical music, Libyan Bedouin desert poetry (Ghinna), modern stars like Ahmed Fakroun (pioneer of Arab world funk and synth-pop), Asmahan.. Sports: Football (Al Ahli Tripoli, Al Ittihad Tripoli; Mediterranean Games champions), Athletics, Futsal, Traditional equestrian events.. Festivals: Independence Day (December 24), Revolution Day (February 17), Ghadames International Oasis Festival, Ghat Heritage Festival, Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha.

name: Madagascar
nationalAnthem: Ry Tanindrazanay malala ô! (Oh, Beloved Land of our Ancestors!)
motto: Fitiavana, Tanindrazana, Fandrosoana (Love, Ancestral Land, Progress)
highestPoint: Maromokotro in the Tsaratanana Massif (2,876 m)
longestRiver: Mangoky River (564 km) / Ikopa River / Betsiboka River
climate: Tropical along the eastern coast with humid rainforests and trade winds; temperate and cool in the central highlands; semi-arid sub-desert in the south and southwest
naturalHazards: Destructive tropical cyclones from December to April
Periodic droughts in the southern 'Grand Sud' causing food stress
Locust swarms
environmentalIssues: Deforestation and extreme soil erosion causing red sediment runoff into rivers ('Red Island')
biodiversity: One of the planet's prime biodiversity hotspots: isolated for 88 million years, over 90% of all plant and animal species are found nowhere else on Earth (including over 100 species of lemurs, fossas, and two-thirds of the world's chameleon species)
languages: French (official, widely used in business, administration, and higher education)
mainPoliticalParties: Together with President Andry Rajoelina (TGV / IRD)
latestElections: Presidential election late 2023 (Andry Rajoelina re-elected); legislative elections May 2024; next presidential election scheduled 2028
politicalSituation: President Andry Rajoelina second term; focus on the 'Initiative Émergence Madagascar' (IEM), building highway corridors, expanding vanilla value retention, and addressing southern climate resilience.
foreignRelations: Member of SADC, Indian Ocean Commission (IOC), African Union, Francophonie, UN; close economic ties with France, China, the EU, and Indian Ocean neighbors.
military: Madagascar People's Armed Forces (FAP).
adminDivisions: 23 regions (faritra)
history: Settled around 500 AD by Austronesian voyagers traveling from Indonesia across the Indian Ocean in outrigger canoes, later blending with East African Bantu settlers. Powerful kingdoms emerged, notably the Merina Kingdom in the central highlands. King Andrianampoinimerina and his son King Radama I unified much of the island in the early 19th century from the Rova of Antananarivo. Queen Ranavalona I defended Malagasy sovereignty against European encroachment. France invaded in 1895 and deposed the last monarch, Queen Ranavalona III, in 1897. A major anticolonial uprising in 1947 was brutally suppressed. Independence gained in 1960 under Philibert Tsiranana.
recentEvents2020_2026: Reconstructed the historic Rova of Antananarivo (Queen's Palace) complex; advanced the modern Antananarivo-Toamasina motorway project; opened the world's largest nickel-cobalt refinery at Ambatovy; hosted regional Indian Ocean athletic games.
ethnicGroups: Austronesian-Bantu blend divided into 18 recognized cultural groups: Merina ~26%, Betsimisaraka ~15%, Betsileo ~12%, Tsimihety ~7%, Sakalava ~6%, Antaisaka, Antandroy, Bara, others ~34%
education: University of Antananarivo (Ankatso); regional universities in Toamasina, Mahajanga, and Fianarantsoa.
healthcare: Joseph Ravoahangy Andrianavalona Hospital (HJRA in Antananarivo); Institut Pasteur de Madagascar (world leader in tropical medicine research).
socialCustoms: Famadihana ('Turning of the Bones': joyful traditional exhumation ceremony where ancestor shrouds are replaced and families dance with their forebears), Fady (sacred ancestral taboos), Fihavanana (communal harmony and mutual aid).
etiquette: Honoring ancestral Fady taboos, gentle handshakes, never pointing directly with index finger at tombs or elders, speaking softly.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the Austronesian-African Malagasy language, deep reverence for ancestral spirits (Razana), the iconic Baobab trees, and love for rice.
industries: Bourbon vanilla curing and export (world's #1 producer, ~80% of global supply)
Nickel and cobalt mining and refining (Ambatovy project)
Ilmenite and titanium mining (Rio Tinto QMM in Taolagnaro)
Textile and apparel manufacturing (free trade zone)
agriculture: Rice (staple diet consumed three times daily, highest per capita rice consumption in Africa)
energy: Hydropower (Andekaleka hydroelectric dam, Sahofika project) and expanding solar photovoltaic parks (Ambatolampy Solar)
tourism: Premier global ecotourism and natural history destination: Avenue of the Baobabs in Morondava, Tsingy de Bemaraha stone forests, tracking ring-tailed lemurs in Isalo and Andasibe-Mantadia National Parks, and whale watching in Île Sainte-Marie.
employment: Over 75% in smallholder farming (vanilla, cloves, rice paddy cultivation), zebu pastoralism, textile assembly.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic management supported by IMF Extended Credit Facility; floating Malagasy Ariary.
transport: National Route 2 (RN2) connecting Antananarivo to Port of Toamasina; Madagascar Railways (Fianarantsoa-Côte Est line); expanding deepwater port at Toamasina.
ports: Port of Toamasina (leading maritime freight hub)
cuisine: Vary amin'anana (rice porridge with leafy greens, ginger, and meat or zebu sausage), Romazava (national dish: fragrant beef or zebu stew simmered with leafy green anamamy and brèdes mafana producing a mild tongue-tingling sensation), Ravitoto (pounded cassava leaves cooked with fatty pork and coconut milk), Koba ravina (sweet dessert of ground peanuts, rice flour, and brown sugar wrapped in banana leaves), Mofo gasy (sweet fried rice cakes).
music: Valiha (bamboo tube zither, the national instrument), Salegy (energetic dance rhythm driven by Jaojoby 'King of Salegy'), Tsapiky fast guitar rhythms of the south, world music legends Tarika, Rossy, D'Gary.
dance: Salegy dancing, Tsapiky, traditional Merina court dances.
art: Zafimaniry woodcraft (UNESCO masterpiece: intricate geometric carved wooden windows, doors, and furniture without a single nail), Antaimoro paper crafted with embedded wild flower petals.
architecture: Rova of Antananarivo (Queen's Palace perched atop the highest hill); traditional high-pitched red clay houses of the Merina highlands; timber and thatch coastal huts.
literature: Jean-Joseph Rabearivelo (father of modern African poetry), Flavien Ranaivo, Michèle Rakotoson (L'Aînée des châtaignes), Jean-Luc Raharimanana.
cinema: Soleil O (Med Hondo, classic), Lova Nantenaina; Rencontres du Film Court (Madagascar Short Film Festival).
sports: Pétanque (national passion; Madagascar is a multi-time World Pétanque Champion!), Rugby Union (Makis, immensely popular spectator sport packing stadiums in Antananarivo), Football (Barea: fairy-tale quarter-finalists at 2019 AFCON), Savika (traditional zebu bull wrestling).
media: Midi Madagasikara, L'Express de Madagascar, TVM (Télévision Malagasy), Radio Madagasikara.
clothing: Lamba (versatile woven rectangular cloth draped around shoulders or waist, worn by both men and women for daily and ceremonial occasions); Malagasy straw sun hats.
crafts: Zafimaniry carved wooden boxes and shutters, Antaimoro floral paper, raffia woven hats and baskets, silk Lambamena funerary shrouds.
worldHeritageSites: Tsingy de Bemaraha Strict Nature Reserve
unescoIntangible: Woodcrafting knowledge of the Zafimaniry (inscribed 2008)
Malagasy Kabary (oratorical art, inscribed 2021)
flagDescription: Two equal horizontal bands of red (top) and green (bottom), with a vertical white band on the hoist side (white and red were colors of the Merina kingdom, green represented the coastal Hova).
coatOfArmsDescription: A circular seal bearing a stylized map of Madagascar over an ocean, topped by a zebu head, radiating sun rays, flanked by two rice stalks with the national motto 'Fitiavana, Tanindrazana, Fandrosoana'.
travelNotes: A world apart with species found nowhere else on planet Earth; internal travel can require patience due to road conditions; gentle, polite culture deeply welcoming to travelers.
shortSummary: Madagascar is the enchanted 'Eighth Continent', an island wonderland isolated for millions of years, celebrated for the otherworldly Avenue of the Baobabs, over one hundred species of playful lemurs, world-dominating Bourbon vanilla, and the intricate oratorical art of Kabary.
geography: Highest point: Maromokotro in the Tsaratanana Massif (2,876 m). Lowest point: Indian Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Mangoky River (564 km) / Ikopa River / Betsiboka River. Climate: Tropical along the eastern coast with humid rainforests and trade winds; temperate and cool in the central highlands; semi-arid sub-desert in the south and southwest. Biodiversity: One of the planet's prime biodiversity hotspots: isolated for 88 million years, over 90% of all plant and animal species are found nowhere else on Earth (including over 100 species of lemurs, fossas, and two-thirds of the world's chameleon species).
economy: Sectors: Agriculture & Fisheries 24%, Services 56%, Industry & Mining 20%. Key industries: Bourbon vanilla curing and export (world's #1 producer, ~80% of global supply), Nickel and cobalt mining and refining (Ambatovy project), Ilmenite and titanium mining (Rio Tinto QMM in Taolagnaro), Textile and apparel manufacturing (free trade zone), Essential oils and spices (cloves), Prawn and shrimp aquaculture. Natural resources: Vanilla and spices, Nickel, Cobalt, Ilmenite (titanium), Sapphires and gemstones (Ilakaka), Graphite, Chromite, Petroleum potential. Major exports: Vanilla beans, Nickel and cobalt, Cloves, Textiles and garments, Precious gemstones, Crustaceans (shrimp).
culture: Cuisine: Vary amin'anana (rice porridge with leafy greens, ginger, and meat or zebu sausage), Romazava (national dish: fragrant beef or zebu stew simmered with leafy green anamamy and brèdes mafana producing a mild tongue-tingling sensation), Ravitoto (pounded cassava leaves cooked with fatty pork and coconut milk), Koba ravina (sweet dessert of ground peanuts, rice flour, and brown sugar wrapped in banana leaves), Mofo gasy (sweet fried rice cakes).. Music & Dance: Valiha (bamboo tube zither, the national instrument), Salegy (energetic dance rhythm driven by Jaojoby 'King of Salegy'), Tsapiky fast guitar rhythms of the south, world music legends Tarika, Rossy, D'Gary.. Sports: Pétanque (national passion; Madagascar is a multi-time World Pétanque Champion!), Rugby Union (Makis, immensely popular spectator sport packing stadiums in Antananarivo), Football (Barea: fairy-tale quarter-finalists at 2019 AFCON), Savika (traditional zebu bull wrestling).. Festivals: Independence Day (June 26), Donia Music Festival (Nosy Be), Madajazzcar International Jazz Festival, Fanjaomba (whale festival on Île Sainte-Marie).

name: Malawi
nativeName: Republic of Malawi / Dziko la Malaŵi
nationalAnthem: Mulungu dalitsa Malaŵi (O God Bless Our Land of Malawi)
coastline: 0 km (landlocked, but over 580 km shoreline along Lake Malawi)
highestPoint: Sapitwa Peak on Mount Mulanje (3,002 m)
lowestPoint: Confluence of Shire River and international boundary with Mozambique (37 m)
longestRiver: Shire River (402 km, sole outlet of Lake Malawi draining to Zambezi River)
majorLakes: Lake Malawi (Lake Nyasa, covering 20% of the country, home to over 1,000 species of colorful cichlid fish)
climate: Subtropical highland in plateau regions; warm and humid along Lake Malawi shore; single rainy season from November to April, pleasant dry season from May to October
naturalHazards: Destructive tropical cyclones moving inland from Mozambique Channel (Cyclone Freddy in 2023)
Periodic drought in southern valleys
environmentalIssues: Severe deforestation for firewood and charcoal
Overfishing in near-shore waters of Lake Malawi
biodiversity: Lake Malawi National Park (first freshwater lake UNESCO World Heritage site, famous for adaptive radiation of colorful Mbuna cichlids) and Majete Wildlife Reserve (revitalized Big Five sanctuary)
languages: Chichewa (national and official language spoken across the country)
latestElections: Historic court-ordered rerun election 2020 (Lazarus Chakwera elected); next general election scheduled September 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Model of judicial independence following the historic 2020 rerun election; implementation of the Malawi 2063 vision focusing on agricultural commercialization, tourism, and industrialization.
foreignRelations: Known as 'The Warm Heart of Africa'; member of SADC, COMESA, Commonwealth, African Union, UN; close partnerships with US, UK, EU, Japan, and international donors.
military: Malawian Defence Force (MDF).
adminDivisions: 3 regions (Northern, Central, Southern) divided into 28 districts
history: Inhabited by hunter-gatherers followed by Bantu Maravi Empire in the 15th century, from which the name Malawi ('flames of fire') originates. David Livingstone explored Lake Nyasa in 1859. Established as the British protectorate of Nyasaland in 1891. Anti-colonial resistance culminated in the 1915 uprising led by John Chilembwe. Gained independence in 1964 under Dr. Hastings Kamuzu Banda, who declared himself President for Life in 1971 and ruled with an iron fist for 30 years. Multi-party democracy was restored peacefully in 1994 under Bakili Muluzi. In 2020, Malawi's constitutional court made global history by annulling a rigged election, leading to a peaceful opposition victory.
recentEvents2020_2026: Rehabilitated the Nacala Railway Corridor connecting landlocked Malawi to Mozambique's deepwater port; recovered from Cyclone Freddy through community resilience; expanded solar mini-grids (Golomoti 20MW solar with battery storage); advanced specialty macadamia and tea value chains.
historicalFigures: William Kamkwamba (author of 'The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind')
education: University of Malawi (UNIMA in Zomba); Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources (LUANAR); Mzuzu University; expanding community day secondary schools.
healthcare: Kamuzu Central Hospital (Lilongwe) and Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital (Blantyre); global pioneer in the universal rollout of the RTS,S malaria vaccine.
socialCustoms: Celebrated as 'The Warm Heart of Africa' for genuine friendliness and kindness, Gule Wamkulu masked spiritual rituals among the Chewa, communal maize pounding.
etiquette: Greeting with gentle handshakes supported by touching the right elbow with the left hand, addressing elders respectfully with 'Bambo' (father) or 'Mayi' (mother).
nationalIdentity: Defined by the sparkling blue expanse of Lake Malawi, the friendly spirit of 'The Warm Heart of Africa', Chichewa linguistic unity, and the dramatic granite peak of Mount Mulanje.
industries: Tobacco leaf sorting and curing (Auction Floors in Lilongwe)
Tea and macadamia nut processing (Thyolo, Mulanje)
Sugar refining (Illovo Sugar in Nchalo and Dwangwa)
Beer brewing and soft drinks (Carlsberg Malawi / Castel)
agriculture: Tobacco (dominant cash crop and export revenue earner)
Black tea (second largest producer in Africa)
energy: Hydroelectric generation on the Shire River (Nkula, Tedzani, Kapichira) providing ~80% of power, complemented by the Golomoti solar-battery installation
tourism: Eco-tourism and lake vacations: snorkeling and diving among rainbow-colored cichlids in Lake Malawi, relaxing on Cape Maclear beaches, hiking Mount Mulanje's towering granite cliffs, wildlife safaris in Liwonde and Majete National Parks.
employment: Over 75% in smallholder subsistence and cash crop farming, fishing on Lake Malawi, informal trade.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic adjustment under IMF Extended Credit Facility program; addressing foreign exchange liquidity and stabilizing the Kwacha.
transport: Nacala Railway Corridor linking Blantyre and Lilongwe to Port of Nacala (Mozambique); paved M1 national spine highway; lake passenger steamers (MV Ilala).
ports: Landlocked; primary oceanic freight access through Port of Nacala and Port of Beira in Mozambique, and Port of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania
cuisine: Nsima (thick, smooth porridge made from finely ground white maize flour / Ufa, the cornerstone of every meal) served with Ndiwo (relish of pumpkin leaves, beans, or meat), Chambo (prized endemic Lake Malawi tilapia, grilled or fried with peri-peri), Kondowole (cassava fufu), Mandasi (puffed fried bread), Thobwa (fermented sweet drink made from maize and millet).
festivals: Lake of Stars Music Festival (internationally celebrated festival on the shores of Lake Malawi)
Mulanje Porters Race (extreme mountain footrace up Mount Mulanje)
music: Traditional Gule Wamkulu drumming, acoustic guitar fingerpicking (Malawi mouse boys, Faith Mussa), modern Afro-dancehall and gospel (Tay Grin, Lucius Banda, Driemo).
dance: Gule Wamkulu ('The Great Dance' of the Nyau secret society, UNESCO masterpiece), Beni dance, Vimbuza healing dance (UNESCO).
art: Intricate wood carvings from Mua Mission (Kuwala art school), woven palm leaf furniture, painted village pottery.
architecture: Colonial brick buildings in historic Zomba; traditional earthen houses with grass thatch; modern government buildings on Capital Hill in Lilongwe.
literature: Jack Mapanje (renowned poet: Of Chameleons and Gods), Steve Chimombo, Legson Kayira (I Will Try), William Kamkwamba (The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind).
cinema: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind (directed by Chiwetel Ejiofor, filmed on location in Wimbe); emerging local filmmakers at Lake of Stars.
sports: Netball: The Queens (Malawi national netball team, world top-6 powerhouse and African champions; legendary shooter Mwawi Kumwenda), Football (The Flames, reached knockout stage at 2021 AFCON).
media: The Daily Times, The Nation, Zodiak Broadcasting Station (ZBS), MBC (Malawi Broadcasting Corporation).
clothing: Chitenje (vibrant printed cotton wrap cloth worn around the waist by women); tailored modern shirts for men.
crafts: Mua Mission wood sculptures, woven Malawian cane chairs and tables, woven baskets, beaded crafts.
worldHeritageSites: Chongoni Rock-Art Area (densest concentration of rock art in Central Africa)
unescoIntangible: Gule Wamkulu, ritual dance of the Chewa people
Vimbuza healing dance
Tchopa, sacrificial dance of the Lhomwe people
Mwinoghe, joyful dance of three ethnic communities in northern Malawi
flagDescription: Three equal horizontal bands of black (the indigenous people of Africa), red (blood shed for freedom), and green (the lush nature and agriculture of Malawi), with a red rising sun with 31 rays centered on the top black band (representing the dawn of hope and freedom).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a shield showing wavy blue and white lines (Lake Malawi), a lion passant, and a rising sun, supported by a lion and a leopard resting on Mount Mulanje above the motto 'Unity and Freedom'.
landmarks: St. Michael and All Angels Church (Blantyre)
travelNotes: Earns its title 'The Warm Heart of Africa' with extraordinary friendliness; Lake Malawi is warm, fresh, and free of ocean tides; hiking Mount Mulanje offers world-class alpine hut trekking.
shortSummary: Malawi is the enchanting 'Warm Heart of Africa', world-renowned for the crystal-clear waters and colorful cichlids of Lake Malawi, the towering granite peaks of Mount Mulanje, and the UNESCO-honored spiritual dance of Gule Wamkulu.
geography: Highest point: Sapitwa Peak on Mount Mulanje (3,002 m). Lowest point: Confluence of Shire River and international boundary with Mozambique (37 m). Longest river: Shire River (402 km, sole outlet of Lake Malawi draining to Zambezi River). Climate: Subtropical highland in plateau regions; warm and humid along Lake Malawi shore; single rainy season from November to April, pleasant dry season from May to October. Biodiversity: Lake Malawi National Park (first freshwater lake UNESCO World Heritage site, famous for adaptive radiation of colorful Mbuna cichlids) and Majete Wildlife Reserve (revitalized Big Five sanctuary).
economy: Sectors: Services 52%, Agriculture 28%, Industry 20%. Key industries: Tobacco leaf sorting and curing (Auction Floors in Lilongwe), Tea and macadamia nut processing (Thyolo, Mulanje), Sugar refining (Illovo Sugar in Nchalo and Dwangwa), Beer brewing and soft drinks (Carlsberg Malawi / Castel), Cement manufacturing. Natural resources: Lake Malawi freshwater and fish, Arable fertile soils, Uranium (Kayelekera), Rare earth minerals (Songwe Hill), Hydropower, Limestone. Major exports: Raw and processed tobacco, Black tea, Raw sugar, Macadamia nuts, Soybeans and legumes.
culture: Cuisine: Nsima (thick, smooth porridge made from finely ground white maize flour / Ufa, the cornerstone of every meal) served with Ndiwo (relish of pumpkin leaves, beans, or meat), Chambo (prized endemic Lake Malawi tilapia, grilled or fried with peri-peri), Kondowole (cassava fufu), Mandasi (puffed fried bread), Thobwa (fermented sweet drink made from maize and millet).. Music & Dance: Traditional Gule Wamkulu drumming, acoustic guitar fingerpicking (Malawi mouse boys, Faith Mussa), modern Afro-dancehall and gospel (Tay Grin, Lucius Banda, Driemo).. Sports: Netball: The Queens (Malawi national netball team, world top-6 powerhouse and African champions; legendary shooter Mwawi Kumwenda), Football (The Flames, reached knockout stage at 2021 AFCON).. Festivals: Lake of Stars Music Festival (internationally celebrated festival on the shores of Lake Malawi), Independence Day (July 6), Mulanje Porters Race (extreme mountain footrace up Mount Mulanje).

name: Mali
nationalAnthem: Le Mali (Pour l'Afrique et pour toi, Mali)
motto: Un Peuple, Un But, Une Foi (One People, One Goal, One Faith)
highestPoint: Hombori Tondo (1,155 m sandstone mesa)
longestRiver: Niger River (flows 1,700 km through Mali, life-giving interior arc)
climate: Hyper-arid Saharan desert in the north; semi-arid Sahelian belt through the center; tropical Sudanian savanna with summer monsoon in the south
naturalHazards: Harmattan dusty winter winds
Recurrent severe droughts
Desert locust swarms
Seasonal flooding of the Niger River
biodiversity: Inner Niger Delta (colossal wetland oasis in the Sahel supporting millions of migratory birds and manatees) and the desert-adapted elephants of Gourma
headOfState: President of the Transition General Assimi Goïta
mainPoliticalParties: Union for the Republic and Democracy (URD)
latestElections: Constitutional referendum June 2023; general elections postponed to prioritize sovereign security and territorial reclamation
politicalSituation: Governed by General Assimi Goïta; founded the Alliance/Confederation of Sahel States (AES) with Burkina Faso and Niger in 2024; reclaimed Kidal in northern Mali; adopted the 2023 Constitution and revised the mining code.
foreignRelations: Founding member of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES); withdrew from ECOWAS in 2024; strategic defense and economic partnership with Russia, China, Turkey; member of AU, OIC, UN.
military: Malian Armed Forces (FAMa).
adminDivisions: 19 regions and the District of Bamako
history: Heartland of medieval Africa's greatest empires: the Ghana Empire, the Mali Empire (founded c. 1235 by Sundiata Keita, immortalized by the 1236 Kouroukan Fouga charter of human rights and the legendary wealth of Mansa Musa on his 1324 Mecca pilgrimage), and the Songhai Empire centered on Gao and Timbuktu under Askia Muhammad. Timbuktu's Sankore University became a world-renowned center of Islamic learning housing hundreds of thousands of illuminated manuscripts. French colonized the territory by 1898 as French Sudan. Gained independence in 1960 under Pan-Africanist Modibo Keïta. Moussa Traoré ruled from 1968 to 1991. Transitioned to multi-party democracy in 1992 before modern security challenges prompted the 2020/2021 transitions led by Assimi Goïta.
recentEvents2020_2026: Founded the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) in 2024; reclaimed state authority over the northern desert bastion of Kidal; enacted the new mining code establishing 35% state and local ownership in mining ventures; inaugurated the Goulamina lithium project; successfully protected Timbuktu ancient manuscripts.
religions: Sunni Islam (Maliki school, Sufi orders like Tijaniyyah) ~94.8%
education: University of Bamako (divided into specialized faculties); historic Ahmed Baba Institute of Higher Islamic Studies (Timbuktu).
healthcare: Point G University Hospital Center in Bamako; Gabriel Touré Hospital; regional hospital centers across Sikasso and Ségou.
socialCustoms: Sinankunya (cousinage / joking relationships: cross-clan banter defusing social conflict), sharing three rounds of sweet green mint tea (Ataya), communal clay replastering of the Great Mosque of Djenné.
etiquette: Inquiring about family and health at length ('I ka kênê?'), using the right hand, honoring community griots (Djelis) and elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the imperial majesty of the Mali Empire, the mud-brick architecture of Djenné and Timbuktu, the mystical cliff villages of the Dogon, and peerless global musical influence.
industries: Gold mining (top African producer: Loulo-Gounkoto, Fekola, Syama)
energy: Expansion of utility-scale solar generation (Kita 50MW Solar, Tiakadougou) and regional hydropower from Manantali, Felou, and Gouina dams
tourism: Monumental cultural tourism: Great Mosque of Djenné (world's largest mud-brick building), historic libraries of Timbuktu, Bandiagara Escarpment of the Dogon country, and Niger riverboat journeys.
employment: Over 70% in farming and nomadic pastoralism, artisanal gold mining, informal urban trade in Bamako.
debtInflation: Fiscal sovereignty bolstered by gold royalty retention and regional agricultural self-sufficiency.
transport: Dakar-Bamako Railway corridor; Niger River navigation (COMANAV riverboats during flood season); trans-Sahelian asphalt corridors.
airports: Modibo Keita International Airport (BKO in Bamako)
ports: Landlocked; primary oceanic freight access through Port of Dakar (Senegal), Port of Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire), and Port of Conakry (Guinea)
cuisine: Tigaligué / Mafé (rich peanut butter stew cooked with beef, mutton, or chicken served over rice), Riz au Gras, Tô with okra or baobab sauce, Capitaine (Nile perch) grilled or stewed with vegetables, Fakoye (Songhai black herb sauce from Timbuktu), Dabaleni (hibiscus drink).
festivals: Crépissage de la Grande Mosquée de Djenné (annual community replastering festival)
music: The musical superpower of Africa: Desert blues (Ali Farka Touré 3-time Grammy winner, Tinariwen Grammy winners, Songhoy Blues), Golden Voice of Africa Salif Keita, Kora virtuoso Toumani Diabaté and Sidiki Diabaté, Oumou Sangaré (Wassoulou diva), Habib Koité, Amadou & Mariam.
dance: Dogon masked funeral dances (Dama), Bambara Didadi dance, Takamba Songhai and Tuareg flowing dance.
art: Bògòlanfini (traditional hand-dyed Malian mud cloth featuring geometric symbols), Chiwara antelope wooden headdresses, Dogon wooden granary doors and kanaga masks.
architecture: Sudano-Sahelian earthen architecture: Great Mosque of Djenné (colossal earthen cathedral), Sankore and Djinguereber Mosques of Timbuktu, Dogon cliff-side granaries at Bandiagara.
literature: Amadou Hampâté Bâ ('In Africa, an old man who dies is a library that burns'), Yambo Ouologuem (Bound to Violence, Renaudot Prize), Massa Makan Diabaté; hundreds of thousands of medieval Timbuktu manuscripts.
cinema: Souleymane Cissé (Yeelen, won Jury Prize at Cannes 1987), Cheick Oumar Sissoko (Guimba the Tyrant), Abdoulaye Ascofaré.
sports: Basketball (continental youth champions, FIBA stars), Football (Les Aigles / The Eagles; historic legends Salif Keïta first African Footballer of the Year 1970, Seydou Keïta, Frédéric Kanouté, Yves Bissouma).
media: L'Essor (state daily), Les Échos, ORTM (Office de Radiodiffusion Télévision du Mali).
clothing: Grand Boubou made of embroidered Bazin Riche (damask cotton shined and beaten to a mirror finish); Bògòlanfini mud-cloth tunics and scarves.
crafts: Bògòlanfini mud cloth, Chiwara wood carvings, Tuareg silver Tuareg cross jewelry, leatherwork from Timbuktu.
worldHeritageSites: Timbuktu (including Djinguereber, Sankore, and Sidi Yahia mosques)
Cliff of Bandiagara (Land of the Dogons)
unescoIntangible: Cultural space of the Yaaral and Degal (cattle crossing festivals of the Inner Niger Delta)
Manden Charter, proclaimed in Kouroukan Fouga (1236)
Sanké mon, collective fishing rite of San
flagDescription: Three equal vertical bands of green (fertility of the land and agriculture), yellow (mineral wealth and purity), and red (blood shed for freedom and defense of the fatherland) in the classic Pan-African colors.
coatOfArmsDescription: A circular light blue seal featuring a white dove of peace, the minaret of the Great Mosque of Djenné, a rising golden sun, and two bows with arrows, surrounded by the national motto 'Un Peuple, Un But, Une Foi'.
landmarks: Great Mosque of Djenné (world's largest mud-brick structure)
travelNotes: One of humanity's greatest cultural and musical motherlands; travelers should consult security advisories; Djenné and the Niger River remain awe-inspiring monuments of world civilizational history.
shortSummary: Mali is the historic heart of West Africa's greatest medieval empires, famed for the legendary golden pilgrimage of Mansa Musa, the monumental earthen Great Mosque of Djenné, the ancient scholarly manuscripts of Timbuktu, and global Grammy-winning musical dynasties.
geography: Highest point: Hombori Tondo (1,155 m sandstone mesa). Lowest point: Senegal River (23 m). Longest river: Niger River (flows 1,700 km through Mali, life-giving interior arc). Climate: Hyper-arid Saharan desert in the north; semi-arid Sahelian belt through the center; tropical Sudanian savanna with summer monsoon in the south. Biodiversity: Inner Niger Delta (colossal wetland oasis in the Sahel supporting millions of migratory birds and manatees) and the desert-adapted elephants of Gourma.
economy: Sectors: Agriculture & Livestock 38%, Mining & Industry 26%, Services 36%. Key industries: Gold mining (top African producer: Loulo-Gounkoto, Fekola, Syama), Cotton ginning and processing (CMDT), Lithium mining (Goulamina lithium project), Food processing and sugar refining, Textiles and artisanal crafts. Natural resources: Gold (leading export), Lithium (Goulamina), Bauxite, Iron ore, Manganese, Limestone, Hydropower potential. Major exports: Gold bullion, Raw cotton, Live animals and meat, Mangoes and shea butter, Fertilizer minerals.
culture: Cuisine: Tigaligué / Mafé (rich peanut butter stew cooked with beef, mutton, or chicken served over rice), Riz au Gras, Tô with okra or baobab sauce, Capitaine (Nile perch) grilled or stewed with vegetables, Fakoye (Songhai black herb sauce from Timbuktu), Dabaleni (hibiscus drink).. Music & Dance: The musical superpower of Africa: Desert blues (Ali Farka Touré 3-time Grammy winner, Tinariwen Grammy winners, Songhoy Blues), Golden Voice of Africa Salif Keita, Kora virtuoso Toumani Diabaté and Sidiki Diabaté, Oumou Sangaré (Wassoulou diva), Habib Koité, Amadou & Mariam.. Sports: Basketball (continental youth champions, FIBA stars), Football (Les Aigles / The Eagles; historic legends Salif Keïta first African Footballer of the Year 1970, Seydou Keïta, Frédéric Kanouté, Yves Bissouma).. Festivals: Festival sur le Niger (Ségou), Crépissage de la Grande Mosquée de Djenné (annual community replastering festival), Festival au Désert (Essakane/Timbuktu heritage), Independence Day (September 22).

name: Mauritania
nativeName: الجمهورية الإسلامية الموريتانية / République islamique de Mauritanie
nationalAnthem: Bilada-l Ubati-l Kiram (Country of the Proud and Noble)
motto: شرف إخاء عدل / Honneur, Fraternité, Justice (Honor, Fraternity, Justice)
highestPoint: Kediet ej Jill (915 m mountain of pure magnetite iron ore)
longestRiver: Senegal River (border river with Senegal, 1,086 km course) / seasonal desert wadis
climate: Hyper-arid desert across over 85% of territory with hot, dry Saharan winds; narrow semi-arid Sahelian belt along the southern Senegal River valley
naturalHazards: Harmattan severe dust storms
Persistent droughts causing desertification
Desert locust plagues
environmentalIssues: Desertification and moving sand dunes burying oases and highways
biodiversity: Banc d'Arguin National Park (UNESCO site with shallow tidal mudflats hosting millions of migratory shorebirds, pink flamingos, and monk seals)
languages: Hassaniya Arabic (spoken vernacular of the Moorish population)
headOfState: President Mohamed Ould Ghazouani (Chairperson of the African Union 2024)
mainPoliticalParties: Tewassoul (National Rally for Reform and Development)
latestElections: Presidential election June 2024 (Mohamed Ould Ghazouani re-elected in first round); legislative/local elections 2023; next presidential election 2029
politicalSituation: Stable democratic consolidation under President Mohamed Ould Ghazouani, who served as Chairperson of the African Union throughout 2024; successful counter-terrorism doctrine and major offshore gas developments.
foreignRelations: Bridge between the Arab Maghreb and Sub-Saharan West Africa; member of Arab League, African Union, Arab Maghreb Union, G5 Sahel, OIC, UN; strategic natural gas partnership with Senegal.
military: Armed Forces of Mauritania (comprising Army, Navy, Air Force, and National Gendarmerie).
adminDivisions: 15 regions (wilayas, including 3 regions of Nouakchott)
history: Inhabited by Bafour agriculturalists and Berber tribes; northern trading center of the medieval Ghana Empire. The Almoravid movement emerged in the 11th century from a ribat along the Mauritanian coast, conquering Morocco and Islamic Spain. Ancient desert caravan towns (Chinguetti, Ouadane, Oualata, Tichitt) flourished as epicenters of Islamic scholarship and trans-Saharan trade. Colonized by France in 1904 as part of French West Africa. Gained independence in 1960 under Moktar Ould Daddah, who built the capital of Nouakchott from a small fishing outpost. Successfully navigated political transitions in recent decades to emerge as a stable beacon in the Sahel.
recentEvents2020_2026: Chaired the African Union in 2024 under President Ghazouani; commenced commercial production at the massive offshore Greater Tortue Ahmeyim (GTA) LNG project shared with Senegal; advanced the Bir Allah gas field development and green hydrogen projects; expanded iron ore capacity on the historic Mauritania Railway.
education: University of Nouakchott Al Aasriya; Higher Institute of Accounting and Business Administration; traditional Mahadras (prestigious desert Quranic universities).
healthcare: National Hospital Center of Nouakchott; National Oncology Center; Mother and Child Specialized Hospital in Nouakchott.
socialCustoms: Ataya mint tea ritual (poured from high above to create a thick white foam called Raghwa, served in three rounds), desert hospitality, poetry recitations in Hassaniya and Pulaar.
etiquette: Respectful Islamic greetings with right hand over heart, dressing modestly in traditional robes, showing reverence for Quranic scholars (Marabouts).
nationalIdentity: Defined by the synthesis of Arab-Berber and Sub-Saharan African traditions, ancient scholarly libraries of Chinguetti, the vast Sahara desert, and world-class Atlantic fisheries.
industries: Iron ore mining and beneficiation (SNIM at Zouérat)
Offshore natural gas extraction and LNG liquefaction (Greater Tortue Ahmeyim - GTA)
agriculture: Rice and sorghum (along Senegal River valley)
naturalResources: One of the world's richest marine fisheries
energy: GTA offshore gas-to-power, Nouakchott solar and wind farms, and hydropower from the Manantali dam via OMVS
exports: Frozen and processed fish and octopus
tourism: Extreme adventure and heritage tourism: riding the world's longest freight train (Mauritania Iron Ore Train from Zouérat to Nouadhibou), visiting ancient manuscript libraries in Chinguetti, birdwatching in Banc d'Arguin National Park, and exploring the Eye of the Sahara (Richat Structure).
employment: National mining company SNIM, commercial fishing, pastoral livestock herding, civil service.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic stability backed by surging mining, fishing, and gas revenues; disciplined monetary policy by Central Bank of Mauritania.
transport: Mauritania Railway (704 km railway carrying 2-3 km long iron ore trains through the desert); Port of Nouakchott; deepwater mineral terminal at Nouadhibou.
ports: Port of Nouadhibou (mineral and fishing port)
Autonomous Port of Nouakchott (Port de l'Amitié)
cuisine: Thieboudienne / Ceebu Jën (fish cooked with seasoned red or white rice and cassava, carrots, and cabbage), Couscous with camel meat, Maro we-Hut (fish and rice with dried fish sauce), Cherchem (warm lamb and grain stew), Camel milk (Zrig: sweet frothy camel milk mixed with water and sugar), Ataya green tea.
festivals: Festival of Ancient Cities (rotating annually among Chinguetti, Ouadane, Oualata, and Tichitt)
music: Moorish classical music on the Tidinit lute and Ardin harp (traditionally played by women), Pulaar acoustic guitar (Baaba Maal heritage), vocal masters like Dimi Mint Abba and Noura Mint Seymali.
dance: Guetna oasis celebration dances, traditional sword dancing.
art: Leatherwork (painted and embroidered leather camel bags and cushions), silver desert jewelry, Arabic calligraphy in ancient manuscripts.
architecture: Dry stone architecture of ancient Ksour (Chinguetti, Ouadane); hand-painted geometric doorway murals of Oualata; contemporary desert architecture in Nouakchott.
literature: Known across the Arab world as 'The Land of a Million Poets' (Bilad al-Milyun Sha'ir); celebrated poets include Ahmed Ould Abdel Qader and Moussa Ould Ebnou (The Impossible Love).
cinema: Abderrahmane Sissako (world-renowned director: Timbuktu won 7 César Awards and was nominated for an Academy Award; Waiting for Happiness; Black Tea 2024).
sports: Football: Al-Murabitun (The Lions of Chinguetti: historic qualification and knockout round run at the 2023/2024 Africa Cup of Nations defeating Algeria), Camel racing.
media: Chaab, Horizons, Alakhbar, AMI (Agence Mauritanienne d'Information), Télévision de Mauritanie.
clothing: Dara'a (flowing, wide-sleeved damask cotton robe in deep blue or white worn by men with a matching Tagelmust turban); Malafa (colorful, lightweight veil wrap worn by women).
crafts: Elaborately painted Oualata leather cushions, silver pectoral crosses and amulets, carved wooden bowls.
worldHeritageSites: Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata
unescoIntangible: Moorish epic poetry and traditional oral storytelling of the Griots (Iggawin)
famousPeople: Dimi Mint Abba (Diva of the Desert)
flagDescription: Green field charged with a golden crescent and five-pointed star in the center, flanked at the top and bottom by red horizontal stripes (added in 2017 to honor the blood shed by defenders of the nation).
coatOfArmsDescription: A circular seal bearing a white crescent and five-pointed star over a green field, encircled by an open palm branch and a date palm sprig, with the state name in Arabic and French.
landmarks: Ancient City of Chinguetti and its Manuscript Libraries
travelNotes: A land of poetic majesty and sweeping Saharan tranquility; riding the iron ore train from Zouérat to the coast is one of the world's ultimate railway adventures; people are exceptionally dignified and hospitable.
shortSummary: Mauritania, poetically honored as the 'Land of a Million Poets', bridges the Arab Maghreb and West Africa, celebrated for the ancient desert libraries of Chinguetti, the epic Mauritania Iron Ore Train, the bird-filled waters of Banc d'Arguin, and Oscar-nominated cinema by Abderrahmane Sissako.
geography: Highest point: Kediet ej Jill (915 m mountain of pure magnetite iron ore). Lowest point: Sebkha de Ndrhamcha (-5 m). Longest river: Senegal River (border river with Senegal, 1,086 km course) / seasonal desert wadis. Climate: Hyper-arid desert across over 85% of territory with hot, dry Saharan winds; narrow semi-arid Sahelian belt along the southern Senegal River valley. Biodiversity: Banc d'Arguin National Park (UNESCO site with shallow tidal mudflats hosting millions of migratory shorebirds, pink flamingos, and monk seals).
economy: Sectors: Mining & Gas 32%, Fisheries & Agriculture 25%, Services 43%. Key industries: Iron ore mining and beneficiation (SNIM at Zouérat), Offshore natural gas extraction and LNG liquefaction (Greater Tortue Ahmeyim - GTA), Commercial and artisanal fish processing (Nouadhibou), Gold mining (Tasiast mine), Green hydrogen development projects (Aman, Nour). Natural resources: Iron ore (high-grade magnetite and hematite), Offshore natural gas, Gold (Tasiast), One of the world's richest marine fisheries, Copper, Phosphate. Major exports: Iron ore, Frozen and processed fish and octopus, Gold bullion, Liquefied natural gas (GTA), Copper concentrates.
culture: Cuisine: Thieboudienne / Ceebu Jën (fish cooked with seasoned red or white rice and cassava, carrots, and cabbage), Couscous with camel meat, Maro we-Hut (fish and rice with dried fish sauce), Cherchem (warm lamb and grain stew), Camel milk (Zrig: sweet frothy camel milk mixed with water and sugar), Ataya green tea.. Music & Dance: Moorish classical music on the Tidinit lute and Ardin harp (traditionally played by women), Pulaar acoustic guitar (Baaba Maal heritage), vocal masters like Dimi Mint Abba and Noura Mint Seymali.. Sports: Football: Al-Murabitun (The Lions of Chinguetti: historic qualification and knockout round run at the 2023/2024 Africa Cup of Nations defeating Algeria), Camel racing.. Festivals: Festival of Ancient Cities (rotating annually among Chinguetti, Ouadane, Oualata, and Tichitt), Independence Day (November 28), Nomad Festival.

name: Mauritius
nativeName: Republic of Mauritius / République de Maurice / Repiblik Moris
motto: Stella Clavisque Maris Indici (Star and Key of the Indian Ocean)
highestPoint: Piton de la Petite Rivière Noire (828 m)
longestRiver: Grand River South East (39.5 km)
majorLakes: Ganga Talao / Grand Bassin (sacred crater lake)
majorMountains: Le Morne Brabant (556 m basalt monolith)
climate: Tropical maritime with two seasons: warm humid summer from November to April, and cool dry winter from May to October; tempered by southeastern trade winds
naturalHazards: Tropical cyclones from January to March
Localized coastal storm surges
environmentalIssues: Invasive plant and animal species threatening endemic flora/fauna
biodiversity: Black River Gorges National Park (sanctuary for the rescued Mauritius kestrel, pink pigeon, and echo parakeet), Ile aux Aigrettes giant Aldabra tortoise sanctuary, and the historic home of the extinct Dodo bird (Raphus cucullatus)
languages: English (official language of parliament and administration)
French (widely spoken and dominant in media and commerce)
Mauritian Creole / Morisien (universal mother tongue spoken by 90%)
mainPoliticalParties: Alliance du Changement (Labor Party / MMM coalition)
latestElections: Historic general election November 10, 2024 (Alliance du Changement led by Navin Ramgoolam won a landslide 60-0 parliamentary sweep; peaceful democratic transfer of power); next scheduled 2029
politicalSituation: Consolidated high-income democratic exemplar; ranked #1 in Africa on the Mo Ibrahim Index of African Governance and Democracy Index; achieved historic UK diplomatic agreement over the Chagos Archipelago in October 2024.
foreignRelations: Member of SADC, Indian Ocean Commission (IOC headquarters host in Ebène), African Union, Commonwealth, Francophonie, UN; concluded historic treaty with the UK in 2024 recognizing Mauritian sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago.
military: No standing army; national defense maintained by the Mauritius Police Force, Special Mobile Force (SMF), and National Coast Guard.
adminDivisions: 9 districts and 3 outer dependencies (Rodrigues, Agaléga, St. Brandon)
history: Uninhabited volcanic island charted by Arab and Portuguese navigators. Dutch attempted colonization in 1598, naming it Mauritius after Prince Maurice of Nassau; during this period the flightless Dodo bird became extinct. French colonized the island in 1715 as Île de France, developing sugar estates under Governor Mahé de La Bourdonnais using enslaved African labor. Captured by Britain in 1810 during the Napoleonic Wars. Following the abolition of slavery in 1835, Britain initiated the 'Great Experiment' at Aapravasi Ghat, bringing over 450,000 indentured laborers from India. Independence achieved in 1968 under Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam. Transformed from a monocrop sugar economy into a sophisticated upper-middle-income global financial, tech, and luxury tourism powerhouse.
recentEvents2020_2026: Concluded the historic October 2024 agreement with the UK recognizing Mauritian sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago (including Diego Garcia); held peaceful November 2024 general elections resulting in a decisive democratic transition under Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam; expanded the Metro Express light rail connecting Port Louis across central cities.
historicalFigures: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam (Father of the Nation)
education: University of Mauritius (Réduit); University of Technology Mauritius; free primary, secondary, and tertiary public undergraduate education; world-class bilingual literacy.
healthcare: Universal free healthcare system through public regional hospital networks; world-class specialized private medical tourism clinics.
socialCustoms: Exemplary multicultural harmony (vivre-ensemble), evening Sega dancing along the beach, sharing sweet gateaux piments and samosas at street corners.
etiquette: Respectful greetings in French, English, or Creole, removing shoes before entering Hindu temples and mosques, welcoming hospitality.
nationalIdentity: Defined by rainbow multicultural unity ('Enn Sel Lepep, Enn Sel Nasion'), the memory of the Dodo bird, the freedom spirit of Le Morne Brabant, and Sega music.
sectors: Financial & Business Services 24%, Tourism & Hospitality 16%, Manufacturing & Textiles 14%, Information Technology 8%, Agriculture 3%
industries: International offshore banking, wealth management, and fintech
agriculture: Sugarcane (covers majority of cultivated land, producing premium unrefined brown and demerara sugars)
naturalResources: Marine fisheries (exclusive economic zone spanning 2.3 million km²)
energy: Over 22% renewable generation from sugarcane bagasse biomass, utility-scale solar farms, and wind, advancing toward 60% renewable electricity by 2030
tourism: World-class luxury beach and eco-tourism exceeding 1.4 million visitors annually: turquoise lagoons of Belle Mare and Le Morne, Seven Coloured Earths of Chamarel, Black River Gorges hiking, and catamaran cruises to Île aux Cerfs.
employment: Financial services, luxury hospitality, software development, customer contact centers, public sector.
debtInflation: Strong macroeconomic stewardship by Bank of Mauritius; high foreign exchange reserves; stable investment-grade sovereign profile.
transport: Metro Express light rail transit system traversing Port Louis to Curepipe; Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport; Port Louis modern container terminal.
airports: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport (MRU in Plaisance)
ports: Port Louis Harbour (modern container transshipment terminal and cruise jetty)
cuisine: Dholl Puri (thin, soft griddle flatbreads stuffed with yellow split peas, wrapped around rougaille tomato sauce, bean curry, and chili pickle—the beloved national street food), Mine Frit (fried noodles Mauritian style with egg, chicken, and cabbage), Biryani (fragrant spiced meat and potato rice dish), Rougaille (rich Creole tomato, garlic, thyme, and ginger stew with salted fish or sausages), Gateau Piment (crispy chili and split pea fritters), Alouda (sweet chilled milk beverage with basil seeds and agar-agar jelly).
festivals: Maha Shivaratri (grand pilgrimage of hundreds of thousands dressed in white carrying decorated Kanwars to the sacred lake of Ganga Talao)
music: Sega (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: pulsating polyrhythmic dance music played on the Ravanne goat-skin drum, Maravanne rattle, and Triangle, popularized by Ti Frère), Seggae (reggae-sega fusion pioneered by Kaya).
dance: Sega dance (fluid, expressive hip and foot movements where dancers never lift their feet completely from the sand).
art: Vibrant seaside paintings of Malcolm de Chazal and Vaco Baissac, glassblowing at Mauritius Glass Gallery, ship model crafting.
architecture: French colonial wooden plantation mansions (Maison Eureka, Château de Labourdonnais); Aapravasi Ghat stone immigration depot; modern gleaming glass towers of Ebène Cybercity.
literature: J.M.G. Le Clézio (Nobel Prize in Literature 2008, French-Mauritian ancestry: The Prospector), Ananda Devi (Eve Out of Her Ruins), Malcolm de Chazal, Nathacha Appanah.
cinema: Emerging film shooting destination with film rebate incentives; Île Courts International Short Film Festival.
sports: Horse Racing (The Champ de Mars in Port Louis, founded 1812, oldest racecourse in the Southern Hemisphere), Football (Club M), Badminton, Boxing (Bruno Julie 2008 Olympic Bronze Medalist).
media: L'Express, Le Mauricien, Defi Media, MBC (Mauritius Broadcasting Corporation).
clothing: Saris, churidars, and Western contemporary high-street fashion; colorful ruffled Sega dance skirts.
crafts: Intricately detailed wooden historic ship models, Mauritian cane sugar gift boxes, hand-woven vacoas basketry.
worldHeritageSites: Aapravasi Ghat (immigration depot where the modern indentured labor diaspora was established)
Le Morne Cultural Landscape (monumental basalt mountain sanctuary for runaway slaves / maroons)
unescoIntangible: Traditional Mauritian Sega
Bhojpuri folk songs in Mauritius (Geet-Gawai)
Sega Tambour of Rodrigues Island
flagDescription: Four equal horizontal bands of red (blood shed for freedom and independence), blue (the Indian Ocean), yellow (the new light of freedom shining over the island), and green (the lush vegetation and agriculture) - known as 'Les Quatre Bandes'.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a quartered shield depicting a medieval sailing ship, three palm trees, a key, and the star of the Indian Ocean, supported by the extinct Dodo bird and a sambar deer, over the Latin motto 'STELLA CLAVISQUE MARIS INDICI'.

symbols.animal: Dodo (Raphus cucullatus, extinct bird icon of Mauritius)

landmarks: Seven Coloured Earths of Chamarel and Waterfalls
travelNotes: Consistently rated one of the world's premier, safest, and most romantic island destinations; impeccable luxury beach resorts, culinary diversity, and warm multilingual island hospitality.
shortSummary: Mauritius is the glittering 'Star and Key of the Indian Ocean', Africa's leading beacon of governance and high-income living, world-renowned for the legendary Dodo, the dramatic UNESCO cliffs of Le Morne, soul-stirring Sega rhythms, and seven-colored volcanic dunes.
geography: Highest point: Piton de la Petite Rivière Noire (828 m). Lowest point: Indian Ocean (0 m). Longest river: Grand River South East (39.5 km). Climate: Tropical maritime with two seasons: warm humid summer from November to April, and cool dry winter from May to October; tempered by southeastern trade winds. Biodiversity: Black River Gorges National Park (sanctuary for the rescued Mauritius kestrel, pink pigeon, and echo parakeet), Ile aux Aigrettes giant Aldabra tortoise sanctuary, and the historic home of the extinct Dodo bird (Raphus cucullatus).
economy: Sectors: Financial & Business Services 24%, Tourism & Hospitality 16%, Manufacturing & Textiles 14%, Information Technology 8%, Agriculture 3%. Key industries: International offshore banking, wealth management, and fintech, Luxury resort tourism and hospitality, Textile and high-end apparel manufacturing, Information and communication technology (Ebène Cybercity), Sugar milling and specialty sugars, Tuna processing and seafood hub. Natural resources: Arable agricultural land, Marine fisheries (exclusive economic zone spanning 2.3 million km²), Deep ocean water applications, Solar and bagasse energy. Major exports: Processed fish and tuna, Specialty unrefined sugars, High-end textiles and garments, Precious jewelry and polished diamonds, Optical devices.
culture: Cuisine: Dholl Puri (thin, soft griddle flatbreads stuffed with yellow split peas, wrapped around rougaille tomato sauce, bean curry, and chili pickle—the beloved national street food), Mine Frit (fried noodles Mauritian style with egg, chicken, and cabbage), Biryani (fragrant spiced meat and potato rice dish), Rougaille (rich Creole tomato, garlic, thyme, and ginger stew with salted fish or sausages), Gateau Piment (crispy chili and split pea fritters), Alouda (sweet chilled milk beverage with basil seeds and agar-agar jelly).. Music & Dance: Sega (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: pulsating polyrhythmic dance music played on the Ravanne goat-skin drum, Maravanne rattle, and Triangle, popularized by Ti Frère), Seggae (reggae-sega fusion pioneered by Kaya).. Sports: Horse Racing (The Champ de Mars in Port Louis, founded 1812, oldest racecourse in the Southern Hemisphere), Football (Club M), Badminton, Boxing (Bruno Julie 2008 Olympic Bronze Medalist).. Festivals: Maha Shivaratri (grand pilgrimage of hundreds of thousands dressed in white carrying decorated Kanwars to the sacred lake of Ganga Talao), Independence Day (March 12), Cavadee (Tamil festival), Chinese Spring Festival, Eid al-Fitr, Divali (Festival of Lights), Gheere Festival.

name: Morocco
motto: الله، الوطن، الملك (God, the Homeland, the King)
borders: Spain (land borders at Ceuta, Melilla, Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera)
highestPoint: Toubkal in the High Atlas Mountains (4,167 m, highest peak in North Africa)
longestRiver: Draa River (1,100 km) / Sebou River (most voluminous)
climate: Mediterranean along northern coasts with warm dry summers and mild wet winters; oceanic along Atlantic; alpine with heavy snow in Atlas Mountains; arid to hyper-arid desert in southern Saharan regions
naturalHazards: Seismic earthquakes (Al Haouz High Atlas earthquake in 2023)
Periodic droughts in agricultural plains
Flash floods in mountain wadis
biodiversity: Talassemtane National Park (Rif fir forests), Souss-Massa National Park (last viable wild colonies of northern bald ibises), endemic Argan forests (Argania spinosa), and Barbary macaques in the cedar forests of Azrou
languages: Moroccan Darija (spoken vernacular of all Moroccans)
French (widely used in business, higher education, and government)
Spanish (spoken in north and southern coastal zones)
legislature: Parliament (House of Representatives and House of Councillors)
constitution: 2011 (establishing Tamazight as official language and strengthening parliamentary powers)
latestElections: General legislative elections 2021; next scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Dynastic stability under King Mohammed VI (Alaouite dynasty reigning since 1666); rapid modernization of renewable energy, high-speed rail, automotive manufacturing, and co-hosting preparations for the 2030 FIFA World Cup.
foreignRelations: Member of African Union, Arab League, OIC, UN; Major Non-NATO Ally of the US; strategic Atlantic gateway linking Europe, Africa, and the Americas; diplomatic recognition of sovereignty over the Western Sahara provinces consolidated by international partners.
military: Royal Moroccan Armed Forces (FAR).
adminDivisions: 12 regions (including the southern provinces of Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra and Dakhla-Oued Ed-Dahab)
history: Inhabited by indigenous Amazigh (Berber) peoples since prehistory; kingdom of Mauretania ruled in classical times. The Islamic era began with the founding of the Idrisid Dynasty by Idris I in 789 AD and the establishment of Fes. Succeeded by powerful Berber imperial dynasties that ruled northwest Africa and Moorish Iberia (Al-Andalus): the Almoravids (built Marrakech), the Almohads (built the Koutoubia and Giralda), the Marinids, and the Saadians. The Alaouite Dynasty has ruled continuously since 1666. Protected by treaty in 1912 as French and Spanish protectorates. Gained independence in 1956 under King Mohammed V, followed by King Hassan II (who led the historic 1975 Green March consolidating the Sahara). King Mohammed VI ascended the throne in 1999, driving industrial and social modernization.
recentEvents2020_2026: Made historic football history as the first African and Arab nation to reach the FIFA World Cup semi-finals (Qatar 2022); selected as joint host of the 2030 FIFA World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal; hosted the 2023 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Marrakech; constructed the mega-port of Nador West Med and Dakhla Atlantic Port; expanded Noor Ouarzazate solar complex.
historicalFigures: Ibn Battuta (greatest medieval global traveler, born in Tangier)
Fatima al-Fihriya (founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in 859 AD)
religions: Sunni Islam (Maliki school, official state religion) ~99%
Christianity and historic Moroccan Jewish community ~1%
education: University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fes (founded 859 AD by Fatima al-Fihri, recognized by UNESCO and Guinness as the oldest continuously operating university in the world); Mohammed V University (Rabat); Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P).
healthcare: Mohammed VI University Hospital Centers in Marrakech, Tangier, and Rabat; nationwide universal compulsory health insurance (AMO) coverage for all citizens.
socialCustoms: Atay b'naana (sweet Moroccan green tea with fresh spearmint poured theatrically from high silver teapots), Friday family couscous lunches, Hammam bath rituals, Souk bartering.
etiquette: Right-hand use for dining from communal tagines, polite greetings with handshakes and slight bow, removing shoes before carpeted living rooms, deep respect for elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by twelve centuries of continuous imperial sovereignty, Islamic and Amazigh heritage, world-renowned Moorish architecture and crafts, and passionate football pride (Atlas Lions).
industries: Automotive manufacturing (Africa's largest car producer: Renault Tanger Méditerranée, Stellantis Kenitra)
Phosphate extraction and fertilizer processing (OCP Group, world's leading exporter of phosphates)
naturalResources: Phosphates (holds over 70% of world's proven phosphate rock reserves)
Marine fisheries (largest fish producer in Africa)
energy: World leader in renewables: Noor Ouarzazate Solar Complex (one of the world's largest concentrated solar power plants), Midelt solar-wind projects, and Tarfaya wind farm targeting >52% clean electricity
tourism: Premier global tourism destination exceeding 14.5 million annual visitors: labyrinthine medieval medinas of Fes and Marrakech, blue city of Chefchaouen, coastal ramparts of Essaouira, High Atlas trekking, and Sahara dunes at Merzouga.
employment: Automotive and aerospace industrial zones, tourism and hospitality, agriculture, traditional handicrafts, logistics.
debtInflation: Investment-grade sovereign rating; stable Moroccan Dirham pegged to a basket of Euro and US Dollar; prudent central bank policy (Bank Al-Maghrib).
transport: Al Boraq (Africa's first and fastest high-speed bullet train operating at 320 km/h connecting Tangier, Kenitra, Rabat, and Casablanca; expanding to Marrakech); Tanger Med Port (largest container transshipment port in the Mediterranean and Africa).
airports: Mohammed V International Airport (CMN in Casablanca, major African hub)
ports: Tanger Med Port Complex (world top-20 container hub)
Port of Jorf Lasfar (world's premier phosphate hub)
cuisine: Tagine (slow-simmered savory stew cooked in a conical earthenware dish: Lamb tagine with prunes and toasted almonds, Chicken tagine with preserved lemons and olives), Couscous Royal (seven vegetables and meats), Pastilla / Bstilla (flaky warka pastry pie layered with shredded spiced pigeon or chicken, crushed almonds, cinnamon, and powdered sugar), Harira (rich tomato, lentil, and chickpea soup served with dates), Zaalouk (spiced roasted eggplant and tomato dip), Mechoui, Gazelle Horns (cornes de gazelle pastry stuffed with almond paste and orange blossom water).
festivals: Fes Festival of World Sacred Music
Tan-Tan Moussem (UNESCO recognized desert nomad gathering)
music: Gnaoua (UNESCO heritage: spiritual Afro-Berber trance music featuring the Guembri bass lute and Qraqeb iron castanets), Andalusi classical music, Chaabi street folk, Berber folk rhythms (Ahidous, Ahwash), modern Moroccan rap (ElGrandeToto).
dance: Ahidous (communal circular Berber dance with frame drums), Ahwash, Gnaoua trance dance, Shikhat dance.
art: Zellij (intricate, hand-cut geometric ceramic tilework mosaics), Moorish carved plasterwork (Stucco / Gebs), hammered copper and brass lanterns, Berber woven carpets.
architecture: Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca (with its 210-meter minaret overlooking the Atlantic Ocean); Bahia Palace (Marrakech); Bab Mansour gate in Meknes; Ksar of Ait Benhaddou (clay earthen fortress).
literature: Tahar Ben Jelloun (The Sacred Night, won the Prix Goncourt), Driss Chraïbi, Leila Slimani (The Perfect Nanny, Prix Goncourt winner), Mohamed Choukri (For Bread Alone), Abdellah Taïa.
cinema: World's preferred international filming destination (Atlas Studios in Ouarzazate, 'Hollywood of Africa': Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia, Game of Thrones); Marrakech International Film Festival.
sports: Football: Atlas Lions (historic 4th place at the 2022 FIFA World Cup, Olympic Bronze Medalists Paris 2024; global stars Achraf Hakimi, Yassine Bounou, Brahim Díaz), Athletics (Soufiane El Bakkali, back-to-back Olympic Gold Medalist 3000m Steeplechase Tokyo 2020 & Paris 2024; Hicham El Guerrouj, 1500m world record holder and double Olympic champion).
media: Le Matin, L'Économiste, Hespress, 2M TV, Al Aoula, Medi1 TV.
clothing: Djellaba (long hooded robe with pointed hood / Qob, worn by both men and women); Caftan (luxurious embroidered silk and velvet dress worn for weddings); Babouche (leather pointed slippers).
holidays: January 14 (Yennayer / Amazigh New Year, official national holiday)
crafts: Hand-cut Zellij mosaic tiles, carved cedar woodwork, Fes blue-and-white pottery, Beni Ourain wool carpets, embossed leather tanneries (Chouara Tannery in Fes), argan oil cosmetics.
worldHeritageSites: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City: a Shared Heritage
unescoIntangible: Cultural space of Jemaa el-Fna Square (Marrakech)
Moussem of Tan-Tan
Gnaoua music and rituals
Falconry heritage
Argan knowledge and practices
Date palm knowledge and practices
Couscous traditions (multinational)

coatOfArmsDescription: Features a shield bearing a rising sun over the Atlas Mountains in gold and green with a green pentagram, supported by two Barbary lions and topped by the Royal Crown of Morocco, with the Quranic verse: 'If you assist God, He will assist you'.

travelNotes: One of the most culturally intoxicating, safe, and hospitable travel destinations on Earth; high-speed rail connects major hubs; wandering the car-free alleys of Fes and Marrakech is an unforgettable journey through living medieval splendor.
shortSummary: The Kingdom of Morocco is an imperial North African jewel spanning twelve centuries of dynastic civilization, home to the world's oldest university in Fes, the sensory magic of Marrakech's Jemaa el-Fna, high-speed Al Boraq bullet trains, and an inspiring global football legacy.
geography: Highest point: Toubkal in the High Atlas Mountains (4,167 m, highest peak in North Africa). Lowest point: Sebkha Tah (-55 m). Climate: Mediterranean along northern coasts with warm dry summers and mild wet winters; oceanic along Atlantic; alpine with heavy snow in Atlas Mountains; arid to hyper-arid desert in southern Saharan regions. Natural resources: Phosphates (holds over 70% of world's proven phosphate rock reserves), Argan forests, Marine fisheries (largest fish producer in Africa), Silver, Zinc, Manganese, Solar and wind energy.
